t: Eight rows from the kit (KICK, SNARE, CLAP, TOM, HAT, OPEN, CYMBAL, PERC) and an accent row; mute, solo and level per row on knobs 1–3; ACOUSTIC kits picked inside a General MIDI font (Jazz, Brush, Standard, Room, Power, Orchestra, the Latin and cumbia kits). engines

CHORDS, NOTES and SLOTS views; seven chord keys for the key and scale, chord sets; SLOTS compose with whole chords (1, 2, 4 or 8 bars each) and write the pattern; TAL NoiseMaker's factory sounds or a soundfont. manual
A mono line on a piano roll with ACCENT and SLIDE lanes, OCT − / +, ♭♯, RANDOM; the 303's WAVE, CUTOFF, RESO, ENV MOD, ACCENT, TUNE as its MODS. engines
Legato and portamento on Calf Monosynth, a ribbon that plays and adds vibrato as it is dragged up, soundfont instruments from Rhodes and vibes to sax, flute, fiddle and bagpipe. engines
Four banks × eight slots, each bank with its pattern; trim, PITCH ±12, REVERSE, record into a slot, the input's effects, CHOP and AUTO CHOP. manual

Sixteen pads on the step keys, record to a pad with SMART stop, NOTE ON / LOOP / REVERSE / MUTE, latch a loop with a long press, ERASE, COPY, 16 LEVELS, PAD FX, the wave editor with REGIONS, THRESHOLD and MANUAL cuts. manual
Bass, lead and chords can sound like a soundfont instrument instead of their synth, grouped in the picker with ★ favourites and a SORT; an imported soundfont's presets join at once. manual
One profile per engine (FILTER, ENVELOPE, MOTION… for a soundfont; the synths' own knobs), driven by the device knobs, kept with the project and with a preset's MODS. engines
Every machine's chain: DRIVE, COMPRESSOR, REVERB, EQ, PAN, SIDECHAIN, DELAY, each a card with its knobs, switched from the bar or the SELECT key. architecture
DROP, NO KICK, ONLY KICK, CRUSH, LO PASS, HI PASS, STUTTER and LOOP as pads (ALT + step keys 1–8), PHASER, ECHO and HEAVY as sends on ALT + the knobs. manual
Every melodic machine follows the root and scale (a key change snaps the lines); SWING 8 or SWING 16; the tempo on the header, templates and demos setting it. manual

MODE turns the step keys into pads for the machine on screen (the scale, the chord keys, the drums' rows); ● records a take, counting in or punching in on the loop, overdubbing loop after loop; a MIDI keyboard plays the LIVE machine too. manual
Every strip at once (✱): level, pan, mute, solo, the step keys picking a strip, the big knob a fine level. manual

A step grid for the drums and the samplers, a piano roll for bass and lead, a chord roll in degrees; up to eight bars paged with ‹ ›; one finger drags, two pinch to zoom; LOCK keeps a stray touch from writing while it plays. manual

h: Features › SELECT and the note knobs
t: Pick notes instead of writing them, move them by a note of the key or a step, a long press picks the whole pattern; knobs 1–3 set the picked notes' LENGTH, VELOCITY and NUDGE. manual
SAVE CURRENT AS NEW keeps the pattern with the machine's sound and the MODS that are set; a GROUP per genre, SORT, ★ favourites; SOURCE picks the device or a stick, played straight from it. manual

h: Features › WITH ITS SOUND · MODS · BARS
t: What a preset brings with it: its sound source or kit, its MODS (only the parts it names), its bar count (or laid over the pattern's bars). manual
Nineteen packs, five presets per machine, each one's tempo, sound and swing in the tables; one scale per pack so its four instruments play together; the waltz and jig packs in 3/4 and 6/8. the packs
PROJECT ▾ → TEMPLATES: a new project at a tempo, swing, key and LIVE FX; SAVE TEMPLATE keeps the session's own; every pack ships one. manual
Autumn Leaves (a jazz trio and sax), 5AM (dark electronic pop over the changes of 4ÆM) and B3rlin (dark techno), on the image's own soundfonts, never changed by a SAVE. manual
SAVE (the name asked once, AGAIN? to write over), SAVE AS NEW, ★ favourites, DEMOS and MY PROJECTS groups; a new project starts clean. manual
One history for the project (the header's ↶ ↷, ALT + ◀ ▶): patterns, slots and the arrangement, a change over several machines as one step; a machine's own ↶ ↷ undo its changes alone. undo
AUTO records knob moves into lanes per machine; a long press on AUTO clears them. architecture
A whole project built over the remote-control fifo: samples, patterns, sounds and all. scripting

Up to sixteen, each every machine's pattern and which machines rest, a shorter pattern looping through it (LOOP) or playing once and resting (ONCE); the sounds, effects, levels, tempo and key stay the project's, so a switch never restarts an engine; the one on screen is the one you edit. manual
A pick lands on the next bar, or waits for the section playing to end its pass; in LOOP up to three picks queue, each playing one pass. manual

h: Features › On the bar line, exactly
t: Each machine writes the new pattern into its track's other clip and libzynthbox swaps the two on the bar's first tick: no note drops or doubles (measured). design
ALT + step keys 9–16 pick sections 1–8 on any page; ALT + MODE or a long press on the plate puts the section keys in the header, where ALT + 1–16 pick sixteen. manual

Square keys with a dot per sounding machine: tap, double tap to rename, hold and drag to move; RENAME, NEW, COLOUR, LENGTH, MOVE, ADD TO SONG; the song a strip of blocks with their repeats and PLAY FROM HERE. manual
What PLAY plays: the section on screen looped, or the song through, the pages following it, stopping on the bar line after its end. manual
The plate sweeps in the section's colour and the page glows round its frame as a change lands; the keys fill with the section's progress. manual

MIC · GUITAR · LINE on jacks 4 and 5, MONITOR, GAIN with its meter, effects made for the input (CLEAN, TAME, FUZZ VOICE, ROBOT, TELEPHONE, OCTAVE; the guitar's amps and pedals), takes kept as they came in. manual
On GUITAR: McLeod's pitch method as guitarix's tuner has it, AUTO or MANUAL strings, fifteen tunings, A4 430–450 Hz; it runs only while on screen. manual
ALT + ● records the master as a WAV; a machine's ● records its take; the metronome holds on during a take. manual

MENU → LIVE REC: a VIDEO, the screen (or a USB camera) with the master's sound as an MP4, or AUDIO ONLY, the sound as a 24-bit WAV among the TRACKS (LIVE REC SAVED → METADATA… tags it, draws its cover and writes it as WAV, FLAC, OGG or MP3 through the export dialog); three quality tiers measured at 0 xruns, a TIMER, the RECORDER's input mixed in (a voice over: the music ducks under the voice, 12 dB over what the speakers leak into the mic, the voice lifted and crisp, a look-ahead limiter on the mix, the mic's level standing on the project plate with a MIC TOO HOT warning; a guitar or a line summed as it is), every key pressed named on a video; the dialog's START is the confirmation; a new project switches it off; VIDEO SAVED / LIVE REC SAVED deletes it (two taps), renames it and sends it on. video

Any number of laptops or PCs over SSH (SETTINGS → COMPUTERS → ADD A COMPUTER): a password used once to install the device's one key, files landing in that computer's Downloads; each with CHANGE, TEST and FORGET; the export dialog can send a track to one as it is written. video
PHONE · QR CODE: a link served by ravving on the Wi‑Fi, 15 minutes at most, WAITING FOR THE PHONE / SENDING / DOWNLOADED ✓; the way to an iPhone. manual

Mounted when needed and EJECTed safely; the USB page lists a stick's samples, soundfonts, presets, bundles and projects with IMPORT (IMPORT ALL for a sample pack); files go the other way from FILES → SEND…; a read-only stick can be formatted. manual

Everything in the library by kind, newest first, each entry with SEND… and DELETE: the one place every kind of file leaves the device; PHONE · BROWSE shows a QR code of the same library as pages on a phone, a DOWNLOAD per file. manual
Speakers and headphones (PLAY THROUGH), files sent to a phone and received from one, pairing with a passkey, the setup a Zynthbox needs applied by ravving. bluetooth
The jacks, HDMI or a Bluetooth output, fed glitch-free through a loopback while the jacks keep the graph's clock, remembered and put back when the output returns. manual

Recorded while the project plays from its first beat, BARS × LOOPS plus a TAIL, or the whole SONG; WAV 24-bit, FLAC, OGG Vorbis or MP3 with title, artist, album, genre, composer, comment, date and BPM, a cover and a JSON sidecar. manual
A .ravv zip of the project with every sample it uses; IMPORT makes a project of one, from the library or a stick. manual
Full screen: TRACKS, ALBUMS and ARTISTS, SORT, REPEAT, a queue, the cover and the transport; the keys drive it (1 2 3 the views, the big knob the volume, knob 1 the position). manual
SETTINGS: USER and AUTHOR, credited on every exported track. manual

jalv hosts the LV2s (TAL NoiseMaker, DISTRHO Nekobi, Calf Monosynth, Calf Crusher and Phaser, Dragonfly Room Reverb, TAP Echo; Calf Saturator as DRIVE); FluidSynth 2 plays the kits and soundfont sources; the port facts of each, audited against the engine mods' research. engines

The SFZ Drum Machines kits (Roland TR909, TR808, LINN9000 and the rest of the folder), FluidR3Mono GM (MuseScore's), the SF2 Instruments (guitars, pipe organ, basses, the Ambients & Drones pads), the AVL kits inside their FluidPlug bundles; a soundfont brought in by USB is used at once. the packs
PipeWire's JACK at 48 kHz and 256 frames: libzynthbox's passthroughs, the jalv inserts wired only while on, FluidSynth told the graph's clock; the clocks, links and xruns checked in one go. routing

One theme, the Miko look, pinned in code; each machine in its own finish (the 909's cream, the 808's dark wood, LinnBeats, the 303's lime, POLY‑6's blue, the lead's purple, the samplers' grey and black) after easyrave's machines; one set of base types and UI rules checked by a test. UI rules
The logo while ravving starts, then a short show into the page: ANIME, GLOW, STILL, ZOOM or OFF in SETTINGS → STARTUP; a still picture while loading, since animating cost the start 2–3 s. manual

What is wrong on the device right now, in plain words, worst first, with what to do: an engine that could not start, dropouts, the keys dying, a stick that would not mount, storage nearly full. manual

NOTES OUTSIDE THE SCALE, the startup look, SBC‑XQ for Bluetooth, the LANGUAGE, the video's quality, timer, source, mic, voice over and keys, the COMPUTERS list, HELP; each section on its own frame. manual

English, Spanish and Japanese, with the music terms musicians use in each; SETTINGS · LANGUAGE follows the device's own language or picks one, and the screen changes at once. A new language is one catalog to translate, this page included. translations
Built on the device, a setup page over Zynthbox: try it, make it the default, Zynthbox at boot again, remove; nothing bundled but ravving. packaging
CUIA commands and backend calls over the webconf fifo, the test suites and the screenshot tour that keep it honest. testing

Key 1 cycles three drum machines, each a FluidSynth kit: a Roland TR909, a TR808 and a LINN9000 to start, any kit from the device's folder from the nameplate. 2 is CHORDS on Noize Mak3r (TAL NoiseMaker's open port), 3 BASS on a 303 (DISTRHO Nekobi), 4 LEAD on Calf Monosynth, 5 the samplers. Every machine has its strip, its SOUND MODIFIERS, a pattern editor and a SOUND EFFECTS chain; the header holds the key and scale, the transport, tempo and swing, the LIVE FX and the master.

h: Features › Two samplers on one key.
t: SAMPLE KING : four banks of eight slots with their own pattern, each slot trimmed, pitched or reversed, a take recorded straight into it, CHOP and AUTO CHOP over the bank. Press 5 again for the PAD SAMPLER : sixteen MPC-style pads on the step keys, record to a pad with SMART stop, loops and latched pads, 16 LEVELS, PAD FX held while a pad plays (ECHO, REVERSE, SKIP, STUTTER, SCRATCH, TAPE STOP) and a wave editor the two share.

h: Features › Presets that bring their sound.
t: Nineteen packs of pattern presets for a USB stick, five patterns for each of the drums, the bass, the lead and the chords, written in scale degrees so they follow the project's key. A preset says ♪ and the sound it was written for, and + MODS when it keeps its tweaks; WITH ITS SOUND, WITH ITS MODS and WITH ITS BARS at the top decide what loads. Each pack ships a template : a new project at its tempo, swing, key and LIVE FX.

A section holds every machine's pattern at once: up to sixteen, picked from any page with ALT and a step key, switched sample-accurately on the next bar ( BAR ) or when the section playing has finished its pass ( SECTION ), with up to three queued. LOOP plays the section on screen; SONG plays the blocks through, each with its repeats, and EXPORT records the whole song in one take.

h: Features › Record anything. Tune the guitar.
t: The RECORDER takes the input (MIC · GUITAR · LINE) as played while the beat goes on, through effects made for it (on GUITAR the amps and pedals: AMP, OVERDRIVE, FUZZ, TUBE, WAH, HOT AMP), and keeps the takes beside the samplers or the tracks: PLAY, TRIM, NORMALISE, CHOP, TO SAMPLE KING, TO PADS. The TUNER reads the dry input: the note and its cents on a ±50 scale, AUTO walking the strings from the lowest, fifteen tunings for guitar, bass and ukulele, A4 from 430 to 450 Hz.

h: Features › Record the session as it happens.
t: One card in the menu, LIVE REC, and the whole session goes to a file: a video of the screen or a USB camera with the master's sound, in sync, at three quality tiers measured to cost the music nothing, or the sound alone as a 24-bit WAV among your tracks, tagged afterwards with a title, artist and cover in the format you pick, through the same dialog an export uses. Plug a mic into the RECORDER and it becomes a voice over : the music ducks under your voice and comes back when you stop, the voice is lifted and made crisp, a look-ahead limiter keeps the mix clean, and the mic's level stands on the project plate while you record (MIC TOO HOT when the gain is too high). Every key you press is named on screen. When it ends: DELETE, RENAME or SEND… to a stick, a computer or the phone.

h: Features › Out of the device, three ways.
t: One SEND… button wherever a file is: a USB stick's ravving folder, one of your computers (laptops or PCs over SSH, each set up once with its password) or the phone, by a QR code of a link served by ravving itself: no app, no pairing, so an iPhone works too. The VIDEO card (tapped twice, so a stray tap never starts one) records the screen or a USB camera with the master's sound, RECORD and STOP starting and ending it from any page. FILES browses the library by kind, and from a phone too: PHONE · BROWSE is a QR code of the library as pages, every file a download. A stick's samples, soundfonts, presets and projects come in from the USB page. This page too: SETTINGS → HELP shows its address as a QR code.

h: Features › Export the track. Play it back.
t: PROJECT ▾ → EXPORT writes the production as the speakers hear it, in WAV 24‑bit, FLAC, OGG or MP3, with its tags and a cover drawn for it, or a .ravv bundle with every sample for another ravving to play the same. The MUSIC PLAYER plays the exported tracks and the recordings full screen, by title, album or artist, with a queue, through the jacks, HDMI or a Bluetooth speaker.

ravving is a C++ Qt 6 app on libzynthbox , GPL‑3.0‑or‑later, and plays what the Zynthbox image ships: jalv hosting the LV2 synths and effects, FluidSynth 2 for the drum kits and the soundfont instruments, PipeWire's JACK at 48 kHz and 256 frames. It starts and wires them at run time; the AppImage bundles none of it.

This is the interim manual: what each page, key and dialog does. A friendlier guide with screenshots is on its way. Each of the five left-column number keys opens a page: Key Page Machines What plays (the nameplate shows it) 1 Drums (press 1 again to cycle) DRUMS 1 · 2 · 3 FluidSynth with a drum kit each: Roland TR909, Roland TR808 and LINN9000 to start, any kit from the device's SFZ Drum Machines folder from the nameplate 2 Chords CHORDS TAL NoiseMaker (jalv) with its factory sounds, or a soundfont instrument (Rhodes, vibes, organ, strings…) 3 Bass BASS DISTRHO Nekobi (jalv), or a soundfont bass (upright, acoustic, finger, fretless, synth) 4 Lead LEAD Calf Monosynth (jalv), or a soundfont instrument (Rhodes, vibes, guitar, sax, flute…) 5 Sampler (press 5 again to switch) SAMPLE KING · PAD SAMPLER a sampler: four banks of eight slots, or sixteen MPC-style pads on the step keys with takes, pad FX, 16 levels and a shared wave editor All five share the top bar: key and scale, transport, tempo and swing, live FX, the instruments strip and master; every machine has a mix strip, SOUND MODIFIERS, its pattern editor and a SOUND EFFECTS chain; a song is made of SECTIONS that change on the bar line, and the whole session lives in projects.

ravving comes from the Zynthbox Store's Apps category as an AppImage. The AppImage opens a setup page over Zynthbox with four choices: TRY IT, MAKE IT THE DEFAULT, ZYNTHBOX AT BOOT AGAIN, REMOVE RAVVING. Projects, takes and recordings stay when ravving is removed.

Shortcuts on the device: ALT + ▲ jumps to the app header from anywhere; ALT + step keys 1–8 toggle the header's LIVE FX in their order (DROP, NO KICK, ONLY KICK, CRUSH, LO PASS, HI PASS, STUTTER, LOOP; the keys light orange while ALT is held and the pads show their key numbers); ALT + knobs 1–3 move PHASER, ECHO and HEAVY; ALT + the big knob is the master volume. A long press on a machine's S (the strip's or the header's) solos it alone. MODE walks the instrument on screen OFF → LIVE → STEP + LIVE → OFF. STOP while stopped is the panic: every instrument's held notes end (a note left sounding). In STEP entry ◀ ▶ move the entry cursor a step, and keys held together go into the same step (a chord in one column). LIVE on the melodic pages: bass, lead and the chords page's NOTES tab play the scale on all 16 step keys with ▲ ▼ shifting the octave; the chords page's CHORDS and SLOTS tabs play the seven chord keys. In STEP entry with the transport stopped, SELECT writes the editor's selected row (a note, or the chord on CHORDS) at the cursor, and with LIVE and STEP on (playing or not) ▲ ▼ walk the rows instead of the octave, each row sounding as it is reached, to find the note by ear first. On a piano roll and the chord roll one finger drags sideways to page the bars (a piano roll also drags its rows up and down; past eight semitones the octave shifts); two fingers pinch to zoom; a tap still toggles a note. The first SAVE asks for the project's name (the on-screen keyboard comes up), later saves write over it after a second press within three seconds (AGAIN?), and the button reads SAVED, asleep, until the next change; SAVE AS NEW asks again. PROJECT ▾ lists the projects and the demos: a tap opens one (a second tap when there are unsaved changes), a long press or ★ makes it a favourite; its one row of actions works on the project open: NEW, TEMPLATES, IMPORT | SAVE AS NEW | EXPORT. The pointer is shown only while a mouse is plugged in. Undo : the header's ↶ ↷ (and ALT + ◀ ▶ on the machine pages) walk the project's timeline back and forth, a change that touched several machines at once (CLEAR ALL, a key change snapping the bass and the lead) being one step; a machine's toolbar ↶ ↷ undo that machine's own changes only. Patterns and slots are undone, and so is the arrangement: a section removed comes back with its content, a rename, a colour, a length and the song's edits go back too (picking a section is not a step). Sounds, the mix and the project's settings are not undone. LOCK (every pattern toolbar, first): the note grids write nothing while it is on: a tap on a cell, a step key, STEP entry, SELECT's moves and note knobs are refused, and LOCK flashes to say why; the grids still scroll, page and audition. Pressing PLAY locks them, so a stray touch cannot change what plays, and STOP unlocks them again. Tap LOCK to edit while it plays (it then stays unlocked past the stop), or to lock the grids while stopped (it then stays locked). One lock for every page; a take (●) still records. SELECT (bass, lead and chords, in the pattern toolbar beside ♭♯): while it is on, a tap on the grid picks a note instead of writing one (again: unpicks; on a held note's tail, the note), on any bar, and ▲ ▼ move every picked note one note of the key up or down (a semitone with ♭♯ on), keeping its length, accent and slide; each move is one UNDO. On the chords page the CHORDS view picks chords and moves them a degree, the NOTES view picks single notes; a held chord always moves as one. A long press on SELECT turns it on with every note (or chord) of the pattern picked, in all its bars, to move the whole pattern at once. Turning SELECT off drops the picks. A note's own settings (bass and lead): with SELECT on and notes picked, the device's knobs 1–3 set them, the picked notes together, and a readout at the grid's top right shows the first one's with its knob badges (the big knob stays the volume; a focused dial group keeps its knobs): Knob Setting A detent 1 LENGTH , 1 step to 4 bars (the lighter cells; a long press on a cell sets it too) a step 2 VELOCITY , 1–127, over the plain or ACCENT one; the ACCENT lane's cell fills to it (bright red when accented), and a tap there still flips the accent: full, or back to the plain velocity (clearing the note's own) 4 3 NUDGE , half a step early to half a step late, from where the swing puts the note (a LIVE take with Q off records one) a 16th of a step They move with the note (▲ ▼ ◀ ▶ in SELECT), are one UNDO a detent, and are kept with the project and in a saved pattern preset (the chart's HOLD lane, and VELOCITY and NUDGE , by step: a velocity, a % of a step). SLOTS (chords page) composes with whole chords: tap a slot, play a chord key (the next slot arms itself), set each slot's length (1, 2, 4 or 8 bars, never past the pattern's eight in all: "n / 8 BARS"); the slots write the chord pattern and PLAY plays them in order, the slot playing lit with its bar. ＋ adds four more slots (up to eight), − takes them away. The slots generate the pattern: once the CHORDS or NOTES view changes it, the view says PATTERN CHANGED and dims the slots, and editing a slot rebuilds from them (UNDO brings the edits back).

Page 5 holds two samplers. Press 5 again to swap between SAMPLE KING and the PAD SAMPLER; ravving remembers which one you used. SAMPLE KING gives you four banks (A to D) of eight slots, and each bank has its own pattern. The bank on screen is the one that plays.

h: SAMPLE KING › Get a sound in
t: Get a sound in. Pick a slot (its row in the grid) and hit LOAD to choose one of your samples. Or record one: ● REC records the device's input straight into the slot, ● again stops, and the take lands there trimmed to its last burst of sound. INPUT sets up what's plugged in, the gain and the monitor.

Shape it. Drag the start and end handles on the waveform (or use knobs 1 and 2 once the waveform has the focus), set PITCH up to 12 semitones up or down, and flip REVERSE to play it backwards. A slot plays one-shot: hitting it again cuts the last hit off.
Chop it. CHOP and AUTO CHOP open the wave editor and spread the pieces over a bank's slots (see the wave editor below).

Play it. Each row of the step grid is a slot, with an accent row under them, and knobs 1–3 set the selected row's mute, solo and level, just like the drums. Turn LIVE on and step keys 1–8 play the slots, with key 9 held for accents. A MIDI keyboard plays them too.
Sixteen pads in four banks (A to D), laid out like an MPC. Pick a pad on screen and its sample, its tools and its settings show up beside the pads; its 16 steps sit underneath.

h: The PAD SAMPLER › Get a sound in
t: Get a sound in. LOAD picks a sample for the pad. ● REC records the input into it; with SMART on, the take stops by itself once the sound goes quiet, and the pad gets it trimmed to its last burst. COPY copies a pad onto another, CLEAR empties it, and ERASE removes the pad's hits from the pattern.

h: The PAD SAMPLER › How it plays
t: How it plays. NOTE ON plays the pad only while you hold it; with it off, a tap plays the whole sample (one-shot). LOOP loops it from the loop point, REVERSE plays it backwards, and MUTE silences it (UNMUTE ALL brings every pad back).

Tweak it. The tabs TRIM, MIX, AMP ENV, TUNE, PLAY and FILTER each put three settings on knobs 1–3, and ◀ ▶ switch tabs. That's the start and end, the volume and pan, the attack and decay, the tuning (semitones, then fine), mono or poly with a mute group, and a filter with its type, cutoff and resonance.

h: The PAD SAMPLER › Play it live
t: Play it live. Turn LIVE on and the 16 step keys become the 16 pads. A tap plays a pad; hold one for half a second and it latches, looping until you tap it again. STOP ends every latched loop.
PAD FX. While a pad plays, hold ECHO, TAPE STOP, SCRATCH, STUTTER, SKIP or REVERSE to throw an effect on it. Let go and it's back to normal.

16 LEVELS. Switch 16 LVL on and all sixteen pads play the pad you had selected, spread by TYPE: VELOCITY (soft to hard), TUNE (a semitone per pad) or SCALE (up your project's scale). The kit's SOUND MODIFIERS set the kit's volume and tuning for every pad.

Both samplers share it. CHOP cuts a sample into pieces three ways: REGIONS (equal slices), THRESHOLD (at the hits louder than a level) and MANUAL (tap the wave to add a cut, tap a cut to remove it). AUTO CHOP opens it straight on the hits. ◀ ▶ change the chop type, the big knob sets the slices or the threshold, NORMALISE raises the sample to full level, TRIM cuts the silence at both ends, and APPLY sends the pieces to a bank's slots or to the pads.

The project has one history. The header's ↶ ↷ (and ALT + ◀ ▶ on the machine pages) walk it back and forth, and a toast names each step ("UNDO · CHORDS + BASS"). A machine's own ↶ ↷ on its pattern toolbar undo that machine's last change only, wherever it is in the history. What is undone: every machine's notes, steps, chords, slots, accents, slides, lengths, automation and live timing, and the arrangement: which sections there are, their order, names, colours and lengths, and the song. A section removed comes back whole, in its place. What is not: the sounds, the mix, the effects and the project's settings (tempo, swing, key). Picking a section is not a step either. One step: a change that touches several machines at once (CLEAR ALL, a key change that snaps the bass and the lead) is one step; so are quick changes in a row (a knob turning, a handle dragged) and a whole recorded take. The history keeps the last 100 steps, and starts afresh when a project is opened or a new one begins.

Bass, lead and chords can sound like something other than their synth: a tap on the nameplate opens the machine's sounds, its own engine first (the 303, Calf Monosynth, TAL NoiseMaker and its factory sounds) and then soundfont instruments played by FluidSynth (an upright and other basses, Rhodes, vibes, organ, strings, sax, flute…, from the device's General MIDI and instrument soundfonts). Choosing one stops the engine and starts the other in its place; a soundfont source has SOUND MODIFIERS of its own (FILTER, ENVELOPE, MOTION). The choice is kept with the project. Acoustic sources for jazz and the like: Grand piano (Fazioli) and Upright piano (Kawai) and a Jazz guitar on CHORDS, Alto and Tenor sax and a Grand piano on LEAD, the Upright on BASS. The drum machines' kit picker has an ACOUSTIC group: General MIDI kits picked inside FluidR3's font ( Jazz and Brush with the ride and the hi-hat foot on their rows, or with the crash; Standard , Room ). Bass and lead notes can last longer than a step (a long press on a cell stretches the row's note up to it), and the header's swing, tapped on its caption, swings the 8ths as jazz does (SWING 8) or the 16ths (SWING 16).

h: Sound sources › Pattern presets with their sound and MODS
t: Pattern presets with their sound and MODS. SAVE CURRENT AS NEW in the presets dialog (PRESET on a pattern toolbar) keeps the machine's sound with the pattern, its source or factory sound, its MODS, or for the drums the kit and the kit's MODS. SAVE PATTERN AS has WITH ITS SOUND (the source or kit playing, its factory sound) and WITH ITS MODS (the MODS that are set: one nobody turned is left out), both on each time it opens; both off, the pattern alone. A curated pack may name just a source or a kit, or add MODS too. Such presets say ♪ and the sound's name under their genre, "+ MODS" when they keep MODS, and the dialog then shows WITH ITS SOUND and WITH ITS MODS (off by default, remembered in the profile under presets/withSound and presets/withMods ): loading one also switches the machine to its sound, and sets its MODS, only the parts the preset names (as MY SOUNDS does): a preset with no MODS leaves the machine's MODS as they are. Turning SOUND on turns MODS on too (a sound is heard with its MODS); MODS then turns off on its own, and on alone it brings a preset's MODS to the sound already playing. Both off, only the pattern loads. A source or kit this device does not have leaves that part of the sound as it is. The samplers' presets keep no sound (theirs is in their banks), nor do the shipped ones; a preset copied to a stick carries its sound in its file. Beside it, WITH ITS BARS (on by default, presets/withBars ): off, a preset keeps the pattern's bar count instead of bringing its own, laid over it from the first bar (a shorter preset repeats to fill it, a longer one is cut), so the bar pages stay as they are. The presets dialog is organised as the sound pickers are: a GROUP chip per genre, SORT (as listed / A–Z) and ★ favourites (a long press, the ★ at a preset's corner, ALT + SELECT), kept per instrument by the preset's name, so a stick's preset and the same one taken in share their ★; it opens on ALL when the group last shown would hide the preset on screen.

Templates. PROJECT ▾ → TEMPLATES (beside NEW) lists project templates: a template is how a project starts, its tempo, swing, key (root and scale) and LIVE FX knobs (PHASER, ECHO, HEAVY). SOURCE picks the device's or a USB stick's (read straight from its ravving/presets/templates/ folder), as the pattern presets' dialog does. Choosing one is NEW with those set (asking first over unsaved changes, as NEW does). SAVE TEMPLATE keeps the session's own as one of the device's (DELETE removes it); the USB dialog's PRESETS copies templates either way. Every genre pack ships one beside its patterns (or more: the Vuelo pack has one per key).

h: Sound sources › A new project starts clean
t: A new project starts clean. NEW, and NEW from a template, put every page back to its defaults: an empty pattern on each machine (no preset loaded), its own engine and the default sound, mix, MODS and SOUND EFFECTS, one section "A", the LIVE FX at rest; a template sets only its tempo, swing, key and LIVE FX knobs on top. The shipped demo patterns come back only through a project or a preset.

Demos. Ravving ships three projects to open from PROJECT ▾ → DEMOS: Autumn Leaves (a jazz trio and alto sax at 146 BPM, swung 8ths, sections A1 A2 B C and a solo chorus) and 5AM (dark electronic pop at 188 BPM in D harmonic minor over Dm – Gm – A – Dm, the changes of Grimes' "4ÆM", everything else written for ravving: a 909 two-step on a breakbeat, an acid bass, a pumping pad and a lead hook, in six sections with a four-bar HUSH before the last drop) and B3rlin (dark techno at 135 BPM in G Phrygian: a 909 floor with light layers of drive on the kick, the 909's ride and a rim on a three-bar loop, the 808's toms on a five-bar one, a sidechained bass rumble, a filtered lead sequence falling a minor second, a sinister pad and a stab; INTRO · RUMBLE · RIDE · PEAK ×2 · BREAK (no kick, the bass on, a snare roll) · PEAK ×2 · OUTRO). They are installed read-only with ravving and use only the image's own soundfonts, so they play the same on any Zynthbox. A demo opens like a project; SAVE keeps the changes as a project of the user's under the demo's name, the demo itself never changes, and it cannot be deleted.

A song is more than one loop. A section holds every machine's pattern at once (an intro, a verse, a bridge) and which machines rest in it; the sounds, effects, levels, tempo and key stay the project's, so a change of section never restarts an engine. Sections are live: the one on screen is the one you edit, and what you edit stays in it when you pick another. LOOP | ONCE (on each machine's strip, beside ❚❚, kept per section like it). A section lasts as long as its longest pattern, or its LENGTH. A shorter pattern LOOPs through it by default (2 bars of drums play twice under a 4-bar lead); on ONCE it plays its own bars once and rests until the section starts again. The rest is exact: the machine's clip is told to play the section's length, the bars past its own kept empty, so nothing is cut and a tail rings out. While it rests no playhead shows and a hit played live is heard, not written. When a switch lands: SWITCH · BAR | SECTION (the SONG page, kept with the project). BAR: a section picked while playing takes over on the next bar. SECTION: it waits for the section playing to finish its pass (its key blinks, the one playing stays lit; picking the one playing again lets it go; stopping plays it at once), then switches on that pass's bar line, in LOOP and in SONG (the song jumps to the picked section's entry). A one-bar section ends every bar. In LOOP the picks queue up, up to three : each plays one pass, then the next takes over, the last looping on; the keys wear their place (1 blinking: next), a queued key picked again leaves the queue, the one playing picked empties it, a fourth pick is refused (QUEUE FULL), stopping puts the first in place and drops the rest. In SONG one pick waits, a new one taking its place. A switch always lands on a bar line, never on a beat.

h: Sections and the song › Switching on the bar line
t: Switching on the bar line. A section picked while the transport plays takes over on the next bar, sample-accurately, so no note drops or doubles (a machine whose part does not change keeps playing). Stopped, a pick is immediate.

h: Sections and the song › The plate
t: The plate. The header's project plate wears the section on screen as a square key with its number, in its colour, blinking while it waits for the bar; a tap opens the SONG page. X and Y (the two keys beside the big knob) go to the previous and the next section from any page or dialog, wrapping round, as a section key would pick it (from the next bar while playing, at once when stopped); pressed again before the switch lands, they move the pick on rather than queue another. With one section a toast says to add more on the SONG page. ALT + step keys 9–16 pick sections 1–8 from any page (lit in their colours while ALT is held; ALT + 1–8 stay the LIVE FX pads). With the section keys in the header, ALT + 1–16 pick sections 1–16, and while their group has the focus (the header's ◀ ▶ onto it) the step keys alone pick them, lit in the sections' colours.

h: Sections and the song › The section keys in the header
t: The section keys in the header. A long press on the project plate, or ALT + MODE (MODE lights orange while ALT is held; MODE alone still cycles the entry mode), puts the section keys where the LIVE FX pads are (the same again brings the pads back): the SONG page's keys, at the pads' size, without their dots. A tap picks one (on the next bar while it plays), ▶ marks the one sounding and its progress fills it, a swipe up removes one (it follows the finger and fades; past half its height it flies off; never the last), more than fit swipe sideways (the strip slides to the section that becomes current or that the song reaches), the keys grouped on a slab in the song's colour with ＋ pinned at its end, always in reach.

h: Sections and the song › Seeing the change
t: Seeing the change. As the section sounding changes (a SONG part, or a LOOP pick landing on the bar line) the plate sweeps in its colour and the instrument page glows round its frame in it, once; the section keys (here and on the SONG page) fill with the section's progress. The SONG page , under the header like the MIXER (ALT + 1 from anywhere, again to go back), wears its own nameplate as an instrument does and lays the sections out at a finger's size, in a frame as the instruments' grids: square keys wearing their number with the name under (eight a row, the first row being the ALT keys), a dot per sounding machine; tap picks, double tap renames, hold and drag moves, × deletes (a second tap), ＋ copies the section on screen (A → A′). Under them: RENAME, NEW (empty), COLOUR, LENGTH (1–8 bars or AUTO, the longest pattern), MOVE, ADD TO SONG. The song is a strip of blocks as wide as their bars × repeats: a block picked moves, repeats (×1–×16) or goes. Keys: ◀ ▶ walk, ▲ ▼ between keys and blocks, SELECT or a step key picks, ALT + ◀ ▶ moves, knob 1 the length, knob 2 the repeats, BACK leaves.

h: Sections and the song › SONG mode
t: SONG mode. LOOP | SONG on the SONG page says what PLAY plays: the section on screen, looped, or the song through. In SONG the first part's section is in place before the first note, each next part is cued as the last bar of the one before begins, and the song stops on the bar line after its end; the block playing shows its progress and the plate the part ("6/9"). While the song plays the instrument pages follow it, their note grids locked as whenever the music plays (LOCK, below); unlocked, an edit goes into the section playing. ▶ PLAY FROM HERE starts it at any block; a section picked by hand while it plays jumps to its first part (one the song does not have goes back to LOOP). EXPORT → WHAT: SONG records the whole song in one take, its own length plus the tail; LOOP is BARS × LOOPS. Up to 16 sections, saved with the project. CHORDS also carries the image's pad soundfonts, grouped by name in its picker: Strings (Ensemble, Fat, Digital, Rise, Bowed, Piano), Organ (Phaser, Pipe 16+8+4, House, Extreme) and Alien (the "Ambients & Drones" fonts: The Thing, Strange voices, Crystal voice, Glassy, Winds, Chaos, The Pulse), each from the device's own soundfonts. A sustained, polyphonic machine suits them: the chords hold while the voicing lasts, and the key keeps them in tune with the bass and lead. The sound pickers group their lists (GROUP chips, ★ for the favourites you mark with the star or ALT + SELECT, SORT as listed or A–Z) and remember the group and sort per instrument.

ravving speaks English, Spanish and Japanese, with the words musicians use in each (BATERÍA, BOMBO, COMPÁS; ドラム, キック, 小節). MENU → SETTINGS → LANGUAGE: SYSTEM (the default) follows the device's own language, or pick English, Español or 日本語; the screen changes at once. The keys printed on the device (MENU, ALT, SELECT…) and the machines' names stay as printed. The webpage has Spanish and Japanese pages too (the switcher in its top bar); the docs are in English.

ravving shows its logo while it starts, until the page is ready, then plays a short show into the page. MENU → SETTINGS → STARTUP picks the look, from the next start: ANIME (fast cuts through the five flow-lens logos into the glow one), GLOW (one at random, its halo swelling), STILL (one at random, a fade), ZOOM (the fluid logo rushing out past the screen) or OFF. While the studio loads, the splash is a still picture, so the start stays quick.

PROJECT ▾ → EXPORT writes the project out of the device, into the library's exports/ folder: A track : the whole production as the speakers hear it, recorded while the project plays from its first beat for BARS × LOOPS bars plus a TAIL for the echoes, cut to the sample, in WAV 24-bit, FLAC, OGG Vorbis or MP3, with its tags (title, artist, album / mixtape, genre, composer, comment, date, BPM), a cover drawn for it (from the title and the artist, with MADE WITH RAVVING) and a JSON sidecar. The master's level is kept as it is: a track that peaks over full scale is pulled down to −0.1 dBFS and the sidecar says so. A bundle : a .ravv zip of the project with every sample it uses, for another ravving to play it the same; PROJECT ▾ → IMPORT lists the bundles found in exports/ (and the library's root, where a transfer lands) and makes a project of one. The ARTIST and COMPOSER start from the profile's author (MENU → SETTINGS: USER and AUTHOR); the ALBUM and GENRE last typed are offered again. MENU → SETTINGS → INTERACTIONS: NOTES OUTSIDE THE SCALE (on by default). On, a key played outside the key (a MIDI keyboard's) on the lead, the bass or the chords' NOTES sounds and records in a row of its own on the roll; off, it is muted there and never recorded. The drums, the samplers and the chords played on a degree ignore it.

h: Video recordings and the computer link
t: The control center's LIVE REC card records the session: a tap opens a dialog that asks WHAT, a VIDEO (the screen or a USB camera with the master's sound, an MP4 in the library's videos/ folder) or AUDIO ONLY (the sound alone, a 24-bit WAV among the TRACKS in the exports folder), whether the MIC is in, and START (the dialog is the confirmation, so a stray tap never starts a recording; ending one is a single tap; a new project switches LIVE REC off). While LIVE REC is on, the device's RECORD key starts a recording and STOP ends it (the music goes on), from any page; SETTINGS · VIDEO has the QUALITY (three tiers, none of which costs the sound a thing), the TIMER counted down before a recording, the SOURCE, MIC (the RECORDER's input in the video's sound) and VOICE, the voice-over mix: while the mic carries a voice the music ducks under it (DUCK −6 / −12 / −18 dB, −12 by default) and the voice is lifted (+6 / +12 dB) and made crisp (a low cut and a presence lift), so a voice over the playing is heard on top rather than buried; a voice is the mic 12 dB over what the speakers are heard to leak into it (the beat does not duck itself), the mix goes through a look-ahead limiter rather than clipping, and the mic's LEVEL is metered from the moment VIDEO is on (in SETTINGS and standing on the project plate; MIC TOO HOT when its peaks pass −6 dBFS: turn the RECORDER's GAIN down); with the RECORDER on GUITAR or LINE the input is summed as it is. Both apply to a recording under way. VIDEO SAVED or LIVE REC SAVED, when one ends, offers DELETE at its left (a second tap within three seconds confirms), RENAME (the file keeps its extension) and SEND… through one dialog that lists every USB stick, every computer and the phone; an audio recording also has METADATA…, the export dialog over the file, which tags it (title, artist, album, genre, composer, comment), draws its cover, writes it in the format chosen (WAV, FLAC, OGG, MP3) and sends it on, through the track export's own finishing; the same SEND… is on the music player's tracks, in FILES and in the presets dialogs, and the export dialog can send a new track or bundle to a computer as it is written. SETTINGS · COMPUTERS holds any number of computers (laptops or PCs on the network, over SSH): ADD A COMPUTER asks for its host, user and password, the password is used once to install the device's one key there, and files land in that computer's Downloads folder; each has CHANGE (set up again, TEST, FORGET).

Every SEND… button (the FILES browser, VIDEO SAVED, the music player's tracks, the presets dialogs, the sound picker) has a third destination beside the USB sticks and the computer: PHONE · QR CODE . It opens a dialog with a QR code of a link to the file, served by ravving itself at a random, unguessable address; point the phone's camera app at the screen, open the link it shows, and Safari or Chrome saves the file to the phone's Downloads (Files on an iPhone). The phone must be on the same Wi-Fi as the device (the link is the device's Wi-Fi address; the dialog says when the device is on no network); no pairing, no app and no account are needed, which makes it the way to an iPhone (Bluetooth's file push does not exist there). The link lives while the dialog is open, 15 minutes at most; closing it stops the server. One file at a time: given several, the first one goes and the dialog says so. The dialog shows the link in words too (to type it), and WAITING FOR THE PHONE / SENDING n % / DOWNLOADED ✓ as it goes; a toast says when the whole file has reached the phone. The same server carries the ravving page (the instructions, the features and every hardware shortcut): SETTINGS → HELP → OPEN shows its address as a QR code ( http://<device>:8098/help/ ), since the device has no browser of its own; a phone's camera opens it, a laptop types it. The same page is public at https://ravving.github.io/ (the dialog's QR code is that one, reachable from anywhere; the device's own address is under it for a Wi-Fi without internet).

The control center's FILES card browses everything in the library by kind (projects, templates, presets, samples, takes, the RECORDER's takes, recordings, tracks, bundles, soundfonts, MIDI files, videos, received files), newest first, each entry with SEND… (the standard dialog: a USB stick's ravving folder, one of the computers or the phone) and DELETE. It is the one place files leave the device or are deleted; the PROJECT dialog opens, saves and exports, and the USB page brings a stick's files in. PHONE · BROWSE in its header shows a QR code of the same library as pages for a phone (or a laptop) on the Wi-Fi: every kind with its count, each kind's files with their detail, size and date, and a DOWNLOAD per file, served by ravving itself (the link lives until 15 minutes pass with no request from the phone, the dialog closed or not); a project or anything that is a folder is listed as "on the device"; a link that ran out says so on the phone.

A stick plugged in shows up as a USB row in the export dialog (a Zynthbox runs udisks but mounts nothing by itself; ravving mounts the stick when it needs it): the track or bundle is written to the library as always and copied to the stick's ravving/ exports/ or ravving/projects/ folder, then EJECT (in the dialog or on the USB page) flushes, unmounts and powers it off so it can be pulled. To put a saved project on a stick, send it from FILES (SEND… bundles it for the stick); PROJECT ▾ → IMPORT lists the bundles found on every stick (its ravving/projects/ and its root) beside the device's own. The project dialog also keeps favourites (★, a long press). The drawer's USB card opens the USB page : ON USB lists what the stick holds by kind (SAMPLES, SOUNDFONTS, PROJECTS, TRACKS, MIDI FILES: found anywhere on it, its ravving/<kind> folders first, system folders skipped), each with IMPORT (✓ ON DEVICE once the library has it); FROM DEVICE lists the library's, each with TO USB. Samples land in samples/imported/<stick>/ keeping the stick's folders, soundfonts in soundfonts/ , MIDI files in midi/ , tracks in exports/ (the music player lists them), projects through the bundle import. One copy at a time, through a part file, a copy onto the stick synced before it counts. The presets dialog (a pattern toolbar's PRESET) has a SOURCE row when a stick is in: DEVICE, or USB · , which lists that machine's pattern presets in the stick's ravving/presets/<drums|bass|lead|chords>/patterns and plays the one picked straight from there, without taking it in (one UNDO puts the pattern back). The dialog opens on the source the pattern on screen came from (the stick a preset was played from, while it is in), with that preset marked. IMPORT ALL beside the folder path brings every new file of the folder on screen and its folders in one go (a sample pack is one tap: IMPORTING 12 / 229 · STOP, one look through the stick and one message at the end; 229 samples in well under a minute). ◀ ▶ the kinds, ALT + ◀ ▶ the side, ▲ ▼ the files, SELECT copies, EJECT in the header. With more than one stick (or partition) plugged in, the card names each stick and a tap asks which one to open. A read-only stick (an installer's ISO image, a locked stick) says so: nothing is offered to copy to it, exports and TO USB skip it, and its page shows FORMAT, which erases the whole stick into one writable FAT32 partition labelled RAVVING (EJECT and FORMAT both want a second press within three seconds). A soundfont brought in is used at once: one that looks like a drum kit (three drum roles or more in its sample names) joins the kit picker under IMPORTED, and every preset of every imported font is a chords / bass / lead source, " · ", grouped by font in the sound pickers.

MENU → BLUETOOTH has the switch, SCAN (a short scan of classic devices; it starts on its own only while no speaker plays, since a scan breaks up a playing Bluetooth link on the Pi's shared radio), and VISIBLE (the device can be found for three minutes, so a phone can send it a file); the devices connected first, then paired, then in range. A tap on one opens its row: PAIR (a passkey to confirm or a PIN to type is asked in the head), CONNECT / DISCONNECT, SEND… (an exported track or bundle, picked next; the progress runs along the bottom), PLAY THROUGH for a speaker or headphones (the whole studio's sound switches to it, DEVICE OUTPUT brings it back; the same choice sits in the drawer's AUDIO OUTPUT card with the jacks and HDMI) and FORGET. Files sent to the device land in the library's incoming/ folder: a bundle shows in PROJECT ▾ → IMPORT, a track in the music player under "Received". A stock Zynthbox needs a little setup for Bluetooth, which ravving's setup applies. A speaker that does not answer (asleep, waking up, or busy with a phone) is called again three more times over about 35 s (the row reads "waking…"; DISCONNECT stops it) before COULD NOT CONNECT. One audio device plays at a time: connecting a second one while another plays hands the sound over (SWITCHING FROM · the other device, which is disconnected). PLAY THROUGH routes once the connection is made. When Bluetooth comes on (a start, the switch) the output kept is connected again, once, if nothing else plays. MENU → MUSIC PLAYER (and DASHBOARD to come back) is a full-screen player for the exported tracks and the ● recordings: TRACKS (sorted), ALBUMS and ARTISTS on the left, the cover, transport, position and volume on the right over the QUEUE. Keys 1 2 3 switch the views, ▲ ▼ pick, SELECT plays, PLAY pauses, STOP stops, the big knob is the volume and knob 1 the position, BACK leaves. Opening the player stops the transport and leaving it stops the player.

MENU → AUDIO OUTPUT picks where the studio's sound goes: the device's jacks (the default), HDMI, or any Bluetooth speaker or headphones connected in the BLUETOOTH dialog. The sound is glitch-free and comes out of one place only. The choice is kept: when the output goes away (headphones turned off) the sound falls back to the jacks, and it goes back to the output once it is there again (a restart, a reconnection; a Bluetooth output's address is kept with it, so that Bluetooth can connect it when it comes on); picking the jacks forgets it. The dialog's list follows what is plugged in while it is open. The music player, which plays beside the master, follows the output picked too. The drawer's OUTPUT slider (knob 2) sets the amplifier's level on the jacks and the chosen sink's own level otherwise. Each paired speaker or headphones has its own SBC-XQ chip in the BLUETOOTH dialog (open its row): off plays it on plain SBC, sturdier over a weak link, whatever SETTINGS says for the rest; a device without its own choice follows SETTINGS. While another output plays, ravving listens to what it sends there: if the music goes out but nothing plays for six seconds, it routes the sound again once, and if it is still silent the issues center says the output plays no sound.

MENU → RECORDER is a full-screen page (as the music player) for recording the input freely, as played. The transport keeps going, so a take can be played over the beat. The input is a tab (MIC · GUITAR · LINE); under the bar, MONITOR and its LEVEL, the jack lights, the GAIN with the meter, ● REC beside a graph of the incoming level, KEEP TAKES IN (SAMPLES: samples/recordings , the samplers' browsers list them; TRACKS: the library's recordings , the music player lists them) and the EFFECTS made for the input (on GUITAR the amps and pedals: AMP, OVERDRIVE, FUZZ, TUBE, WAH, HOT AMP, from the guitarix LV2s on the image). A take is kept as it came in: no compression, no trim, no SMART stop. On the right the RECORDINGS of both places, newest first: ▶ PLAY, TRIM and NORMALISE (a new recording beside it), TO SAMPLE KING / TO PADS (into a slot or a pad), CHOP… (onto SAMPLE KING's bank or the pads, the samplers' wave editor), TO TRACKS / TO SAMPLES, RENAME, DELETE (twice). On GUITAR the page has a TUNER, on the dry input (before the effects): the note heard and its cents on a ±50 scale, the strings of the tuning as buttons. AUTO goes through the strings from the lowest: a string held within 3 cents for 0.8 s is marked ✓ and the next one is up, until ALL STRINGS IN TUNE; MANUAL keeps the string tapped. TUNING picks a tuning (guitar standard, half and full step down, drop D and C, DADGAD, open D, G, E and C; bass 4 and 5 strings, drop D; ukulele GCEA and baritone), A4 the reference (430–450 Hz). The tuner runs only while it is on screen. Keys: ◀ ▶ the input, ▲ ▼ the recordings, RECORD a take, SELECT or PLAY hears the recording picked (STOP stops it), the number keys move the knobs between INPUT (1), TUNER (2) and EFFECTS (3), the big knob is the gain, BACK leaves.

MENU → the ISSUES icon card (beside MUSIC PLAYER, SETTINGS and the USB card) says what is wrong on the device right now, in plain words, with what to do about it: ALL GOOD, or the count lit in the worst severity's colour, and the full list in the dialog, worst first, each with its detail, a suggestion and an action button where one exists (RESTART RAVVING, GDB OFF · RESTART). Every component runs its own check pass and reports: the sound engine missing, an engine that could not start, audio connections that never appeared, audio dropouts (counted every minute), the device's keys dying (zyncoder's GPIO thread, read off stderr), the music player without its PulseAudio bridge, Bluetooth unavailable, an export that failed, a USB stick that would not mount, storage nearly full, the gdb aid left on. New errors and warnings also show as a toast. Under the list, the last warnings ravving printed.

ravving keeps to its own folders: it reads the device's sample library and writes only to these places: Root On the device What config ~/.config/ravving settings (the input set-up, the UI's choices) state ~/.local/state/ravving the live session ( session.json , the sequence); removed by a purge cache ~/.cache/ravving rebuildable: reversed samples, raw takes, the LV2 port cache library /zynthian/zynthian-my-data/ravving the user's work, kept across reinstalls: projects/ , presets/ , samples/ (takes in samples/takes/ , the RECORDER's in samples/recordings/ , imported bundles' samples in samples/imported/ ), recordings/ (the master's and the RECORDER's TRACKS), exports/ On a desktop the library is ~/.local/share/ravving .

Nineteen secret pattern packs in all, none of them installed with ravving: seventeen genre packs (classical, hip-hop, pop, rock, trap, reggaeton, punk, tropical, cumbia, folk, heavy metal, black metal, post-punk, Gregorian (old gothic), vuelo (Flight Facilities' nu-disco), solos (six ballad solos after Coltrane's Ballads and Chet Baker) and bebop (six fast horn solos after Parker, Coltrane and Baker)), the jazz pack, and piig, a smaller style pack. Each genre pack has five pattern presets for each of the drums, the bass, the lead and the chords (solos and bebop six, piig three). To play one, copy a pack's ravving folder to the root of a USB stick: the presets dialog's SOURCE · USB plays them straight from there ( PresetExchange::stickPatterns / loadStickPattern ), and the USB page can import them. data/secret/<genre>-presets/build.py the generator (python3 build.py) data/secret/<genre>-presets/ravving/presets/<drums|bass|lead|chords>/patterns/<Genre> · <Name>.json data/secret/patternkit.py shared by the genre build.py files (not the jazz one) data/secret/validate.py checks every pack against ravving's parsers Each file is {"ravving": "preset", "type": "pattern", "library": "<x>-presets.json", "preset": {"name", "genre", "chart", "sound"}} . The chart is the shipped libraries' format. sound is the sound the pattern was written for: {"soundSource": …} for the bass, lead and chords, {"kit": …} for the drums (a subset of Machine::soundState() ).

h: The genre packs › The notes are scale degrees
t: The notes are scale degrees. They follow the session's root and scale. Each genre is written for one scale, so its four instruments play together: Natural Minor: hip-hop, trap, reggaeton, piig, heavy metal, black metal, post-punk, vuelo. Major: classical, pop, rock, punk, tropical, cumbia, folk, solos, bebop. Dorian: Gregorian. Tropical's minor styles (salsa, bachata) and cumbia's (villera, chicha) sit on degree 6, the relative minor, so each pack stays in one key. In C major they play in A minor. Notes from outside the scale use ALTER (for example rock's ♭3/♭7, trap's ♭2 and raised 7th). Chords from outside the key use chromatic c voicings. Tempo and swing are not stored in a pattern. The tables give each preset's tempo, in quarter-note BPM on the 16-step grid. Every preset plays straight (SWING 50) except these: Preset SWING Hip-Hop · Golden Era Swing 58–62 Hip-Hop · Boom Bap, Lo-Fi Lazy and their bass, lead and chords 54–60 if wanted; straight works Hip-Hop · Jazz Rap, Jazz Rap Walk 60–66 Rock · Half-Time Shuffle about 66, the triplet shuffle Piig · every preset 56–60, the lazy MPC swing Solos · every preset 54–58 with SWING on the EIGHTHS (the templates set it), a ballad's lilt; straight works Bebop · every preset 58–64 with SWING on the EIGHTHS (the templates set it); Trane Countdown and Trane Drive straight to 54, their sixteenths are the swing Set the same swing on every machine playing along. Each pack ships a template, or more ( pack.template(…) , patternkit.write_template() ; the projects dialog's TEMPLATES, ravving/presets/templates/<genre>.json on the stick, a second one under its own name= ): the tempo, swing, key and LIVE FX its presets are best played with. Choosing one starts a new project with them. The tempo is the middle of the pack's preset tempos; the key is the one a pack was made for where it says so, else a usual key of the style. h: The genre packs › The waltz trio is in 3/4
t: The waltz trio is in 3/4. Classical · Waltz, Waltz Oom and Waltz Pah-Pah are three 16-step bars long, which hold four 12-step waltz bars, so the three loop together.

Every sound named is a source in data/kits.json (or a kit path), and validate.py checks this. I added two kinds of entries to kits.json , all from the FluidR3Mono_GM.sf3 already on the device ( /zynthian/zynthian-data/soundfonts/SF2 Instruments/ ): Chords sources: Harpsichord 0:6, Guitar · Clean 0:27, Guitar · Overdrive 0:29, Guitar · Distortion 0:30, Marimba 0:12, Steel drums 0:114, Accordion 0:21, Brass section 0:61, Pizzicato strings 0:45. Bass sources: Picked bass 0:34, Slap bass 0:36, Sine sub 8:80, Contrabass 0:43, Cello 0:42. Lead sources: Violin 0:40, Harpsichord 0:6, Trumpet 0:56, Guitar · Overdrive 0:29, Marimba 0:12, Steel drums 0:114, Pan flute 0:75, Accordion 0:21, Music box 0:10, Guitar · Clean 0:27 (champeta's soukous lead). Bass source "808 · Monosynth": a jalv source on Calf Monosynth, the lead machine's own engine (a second instance on the bass track). Its controls are real port values, checked against the plugin's lv2info dump in engine-mods/calf_monosynth_mod/docs/engine-symbols.txt : Sound: osc 1 Sine ( o1_wave 3), plus 15 % of a triangle an octave up ( o2_wave 4, o2_xpose 12, o12_mix 0.15) for the harmonics an 808's saturation gives. Filter: 12 dB low-pass at 400 Hz that follows the key, opened by a 60 ms filter envelope ( env2cutoff 2400 cents): the click of the attack. Amp envelope: 1 ms attack, 1.8 s decay to 0.3, 250 ms release. Glide: legato 3 (Fingered Legato) with portamento 80 ms, so only overlapping notes (a SLIDE) glide. Off: LFO-to-pitch, LFO-to-filter, the mod wheel; master 0.5. What it cannot do:
No pitch drop. The Monosynth's modulation matrix is LV2 state, not ports (the mod's RESEARCH.md), so kits.json can't set a pitch envelope.

No drive port. Turn on the bass machine's DRIVE for the saturation. The bass page's knobs (Nekobi's) don't apply to it. presetKits: Power #128:16 Orchestra #128:48?TOM=48&HAT=43&OPEN=81&CYMBAL=57&PERC=54 . The rows land on: Row Sound KICK concert bass drum SNARE concert (field) snare CLAP castanets TOM timpani on C (key 48) HAT timpani on G below (key 43) OPEN triangle CYMBAL concert crash (clash cymbals) PERC tambourine The timpani suit a key of C: drum kits don't follow the session's key. - Cumbia · timbal #128:0?PERC=73&TOM=65&CYMBAL=56&CLAP=63 : PERC the güiro, TOM the high timbale, CYMBAL the cowbell (campana), CLAP the high conga (llamador). - Cumbia · room #128:8?PERC=74&TOM=66&CYMBAL=56&CLAP=63 : the room kit, with the long güiro and the low timbale. - Latin · congas #128:0?SNARE=63&CLAP=62&TOM=64&HAT=75&OPEN=70&CYMBAL=56&PERC=73 , for salsa: SNARE open conga, CLAP conga slap, TOM tumba, HAT claves, OPEN maracas, CYMBAL cowbell (campana), PERC güiro; KICK stays the kick. - Latin · güira #128:0?SNARE=60&TOM=61&CLAP=62&OPEN=64&HAT=70&CYMBAL=56&PERC=69 , for merengue and bachata: SNARE high bongo, TOM low bongo, CLAP conga slap, OPEN tumba (the tambora's low stroke), HAT maracas, CYMBAL cowbell, PERC cabasa (the metal güira). - All the Latin keys were named from the font and rendered; every one sounds.

h: Sounds › Nothing needs installing on the device
t: Nothing needs installing on the device. The device's font is MuseScore 2.3.2's FluidR3Mono_GM.sf3. It matches by sha256 cfcd66d89e8386823400eca64934b14fbea7bf48ba1f00d21189af1262794ec2 , the hash in zynthbox-qml's config/soundfonts.json , entry SF_00022. A byte-identical copy is in ~/Downloads/ravving-soundfonts/fluidr3mono/ , from https://github.com/musescore/MuseScore/raw/v2.3.2/share/sound/FluidR3Mono_GM.sf3 . Its licence is MIT (Frank Wen 2000–2002, mono version Michael Cowgill 2014–16; see LICENSE-FluidR3Mono.md there).

h: Sounds › How the new sounds were checked
t: How the new sounds were checked. Every new preset was rendered offline from that copy with tools/soundfont.py render . All of them sound, with peak levels from 0.02 to 0.20 and none silent. The kit rows were also worked out with a port of DrumKit::fromSoundfont . validate.py checks that every FluidR3Mono bank:program in kits.json exists, whenever the copy is present. Limits of these sounds: FluidSynth sources don't glide; a SLIDE only overlaps the notes. The 808 lines therefore use "808 · Monosynth", which does glide. "Sine sub" (8:80) stays registered, but no preset uses it.

h: Piig: Natural Minor, with the Dorian IV and the harmonic V
t: After the candle-lit lo-fi hip-hop and neo-soul of Biig Piig's early EPs ( Big Fan of the Sesh , A World Without Snooze , No Place for Patience ): lazy 2- and 4-bar loops, muted drums (rim, shaker, brushes, soft kicks), a round legato bass, Rhodes and jazz-guitar 7th and 9th chords, and saxes in the background. h: Solos: Major (ballads after Coltrane's Ballads and Chet Baker)
t: Made for Eb major (a tenor's ballad key; the lead's degree 1 is Eb4, so the tenor sings "5-".."1+" and cries up to "2+", the soprano floats "5".."3+", the trumpet stays "7-".."6"). The minor moods sit on degree 6 (C minor), and Devotion vamps on degree 2 (F Dorian). Six original ballad solos for the LEAD, each with the brushes, the bass and the chords it is heard over. They are moody, prolonged and passionate, with no fast passages. The model is the John Coltrane Quartet's Ballads (Impulse!, 1962/63: Tyner, Garrison, Jones), plus Baker's slow trumpet. Nothing is quoted: the album's standards and the recorded solos are copyrighted. The style was studied ( tools/genre-research/solos.md ), and every line, progression and rhythm is new. The playing: Tempo 56–70. Long held notes, 6–12 steps, with a beat or half a bar of air between phrases. A swell written across each phrase in velocities: @60 rising to @100–110 and falling back. The MODS soften each note's attack (ATTACK +2400 timecents on the sax, +3600 on the trumpet) and lengthen the release. Every long note sits 8–16 % of a step late, the rubato lean. Flurries only as ornaments: three or four sixteenths pushed early and climbing into a long note. A scoop or slur (~) into a long tone. The chords are Tyner-style: rootless 9ths and 13ths, the So What fourths, fourths planed over a pedal, Lydian clusters, the minor iv (Abm6) and the backdoor Db9, each held a bar or half a bar and then re-voiced. The bass is Garrison's two-feel, whole notes and pedal. The drums are brushes only, darkened with TONE/CUTOFF, with a crash rolled up into the downbeat for the cymbal swell. Natural Minor; A minor is Arty Boy's key, C# minor Crave You's (the two templates, both at 120: Crave You is 120 on every listing, Arty Boy's groove sits there too). The lines are original: nu-disco drums (a 909 four on the floor with claps and open hats on the off-beats, an 808 for Crave You's laid-back pulse, a Linn disco shuffle with 16th hats, a build with a snare roll into a crash), octave disco basses riding between the kicks, a slap riff, a sub with slides, the funk guitar riff with muted 16ths (@42), a Rhodes hook, a string rise written as a velocity swell, an 80s synth lead on slides, a lazy sax behind the beat (>8). h: Bebop: Major (horn solos after Parker, Coltrane and Baker)
t: Fast horn solos and their comping, in their own group ( Bebop · … ). Made for Bb major (the horn key; the lead's degree 1 is Bb4, so the alto plays "1-".."7", the tenor "5-".."4", the soprano "1".."4+", the trumpet "6-".."7"). Six original solos for the LEAD, each with the chords, the bass and the drums it is heard over: nothing is quoted (the players' recorded solos and tunes are copyrighted), the vocabulary was studied ( tools/genre-research/bebop.md ) and every line, progression and rhythm is new. The progressions are generic schemes: a rhythm-changes-type A section (I VI7 | ii7 V7 | I VI7 | ii7 V7 | I I7 | IV7 ♯iv°7 | iii7 VI7 | ii7 V7), an 8-bar bop blues (I7 | IV7 | I7 | v7 I7 | IV7 | ♯iv°7 | I7 vi7 | ii7 V7), the Countdown reharm of a ii–V–I (ii7 ♭II7 | ♭VImaj7 VII7 | IIImaj7 V7 | Imaj7, chromatic voicings), a modal vamp on the ii7 with two bars of V7sus (quartal "So What"-type voicings), a ballad's I vi ii V | iii VI ii V, and a cool medium's I | ii V | iii vi | ii V | IV | iv ♭VII | iii VI | ii V. The chords are rootless A and B forms. SWING swings the EIGHTHS here (the templates set it): the ride's "ding ding-a" and the bebop eighths sit on the 16-step grid two steps apart. The playing: Parker's lines run in eighths on the chord tones with chromatic approach notes and enclosures, the off-beats a touch louder (@ +8), the approach notes snapped in early (<8), the blue ♭3 scooped into the 3 (~), a breath between phrases, a motif stated then displaced a beat. Coltrane's sheets of sound are sixteenth 1-2-3-5 cells up and their mirror down on every chord, each run swelling to its top; the modal solo is pentatonic cells, stacked fourths up to the Eb6 and a high note cried four times, on the soprano. Baker's lines are few notes, long and soft (@62–88), every one behind the beat (>8–14), a scoop, and air: the trumpet with its cutoff down a little and a longer release.
