h: Input flow: the Hardware attached property
t: The device's keys and knobs reach QML the way the keyboard does through Keys : as events delivered to the item with active focus , bubbling to its parents until a handler accepts them. device button ─► HardwareSwitches (zyncoder poll, 20 ms) └► MidiRouter.enqueueCuiaCommand("SWITCH_STEP3_RELEASED") MIDI-mapped CUIA ─► MidiRouter ─► cuiaEvent ─► ZynthboxBridge ─► Ravving::handleCuia ─┐ device knob ─► HardwareKnobs (zynpot poll) ─► Ravving::handleKnobTurn / handleKnobMove ─┤ keyboard (dev) ─► Main.qml Shortcuts ─► ravving.simulateCuia / simulateKnob ────────────┤ ▼ HardwareEvent ─► Hardware::dispatch(window): activeFocusItem, then each parent, until one accepts it import Ravving FocusScope { Hardware.onKnob1Up: event => level += event.delta // knob 1 clockwise Hardware.onBigKnobDown: event => select(index - 1) Hardware.onKnob2Moved: event => cutoff = event.value // Z2_V5B fixed pot, 0..1 Hardware.onStepPressed: event => grid.toggle(event.index) Hardware.onUpPressed: event => { if (atTop) event.accepted = false } // bubble on } Signals: knob1Up/Down … knob3Up/Down , bigKnobUp/Down , knob1Moved … knob3Moved , generic knobTurned / knobMoved , up/down/left/right/select/back/menu/play/stop/record/metronome Pressed , stepPressed (index 0–15), numberPressed (index 0–4), and pressed for anything else. As with Keys , the specific signal goes first and the generic one gets whatever is still not accepted. A handler that runs accepts the event unless it sets event.accepted = false . Focus model: - The open page (a RavePage , i.e. a FocusScope) has the focus. ▲ at a page's top edge is left unaccepted, bubbles to Main.qml , and focuses the header's first group. - In the header, ◀ ▶ move between the KnobGroup s and ▼ / BACK return to the page. Step keys always go to the page. A number key nobody handles still switches the page (C++ fallback). - A KnobGroup (FocusScope) hands its targets to the knobs: knob n → targets[n], the big knob → targets[3] or fine steps on targets[0]. It can also hold navItems , which its navKnob (the big knob by default; knob 1 for INSTRUMENTS) steps through and SELECT activates. Targets show a KnobBadge (a tiny knob icon: the knob number, value arc, pulsing while a Z2_V5B pot waits for pick-up). - Inside a page the big knob is always the volume of the machine on screen ( RavePage.module , MachineModule.nudgeLevel() ); the fader wears the big-knob badge while it is. Groups in a page ( ParamCard , the machine strip) set ownsBigKnob: false so it passes through to the page. Popups and the header, outside the page, keep using it. - A machine's strip (role, PAN knob, VOL RaveFader ) is a KnobGroup : tap it and knob 1 pans, knob 2 sets the level; BACK or a tap in the grid give the knobs back to the rows ( StepGrid.knobsActive is off while the strip has them). - ▲ ▼ walk one vertical order per machine, owned by MachineModule : header → strip → SOUND MODIFIERS cards (only while open) → the editor → SOUND EFFECTS cards (only while open). The sections move the focus themselves ( ParamCardRow.released(dy) , coming back to the card last used with enter() ); a page calls focusUp() / focusDown() when its editor has no further to go (the drums: past the top row / the ACC row; the bass roll: past its top / bottom note row). focusUp() returns false from the strip, so ▲ bubbles to the header; ▼ from the header lands on the page's focusTop() (the strip). - RECORD on an instrument page is that machine's take (the strip's ● shows ● / count-in beat / … / ■); RECORD with the header focused, or ALT + RECORD anywhere, is the global recording (the header's ●, red RECORD LED). - The metronome is libzynthbox's (SyncTimer audibleMetronome ) with zynthbox-qml's tick/tock wavs: ZynthboxBridge::setMetronomeSounds() builds the two ClipAudioSources through the exported constructor (no meta-object factory exists) and SamplerSynth's global-sketch1 outputs are wired to the master. - An external MIDI controller plays the machine on screen (on every page; LIVE, which may be left on another machine, is the step keys' only) through the same path as the step keys, so REC records it: GM drum notes 35–59 by role ( DrumKit::roleForGmNote ), any other note cycling through the rows from C2, velocity ≥ 100 an accent. Plugging one in or out shows a Toast (a dark pill, bottom centre). Debug: QT_LOGGING_RULES="ravving.midi.debug=true". - The key lights ( Main.qml 's ledColors ): ▲ ▼ SELECT BACK ALT MENU always light in a soft white ( navigationLight ; ALT white while held, MENU while the menu is open); ◀ ▶ light while they switch something on the open page ( RavePage.sideKeysLit : the CHORDS views with the editor focused, the drum machines, the sampler banks); PLAY dim green when stopped, bright while playing; STOP dim when stopped, lit while playing; RECORD dim red when ready, red while recording (global or a sampler take), a machine's colour during its take. - ALT + ◀ / ▶ undo and redo the pattern of the machine on screen (the toolbar's ↶ ↷). - ALT + ▲ gives the focus to the app header at once, from wherever it is (a page's rows, a section's cards, the strip): Ravving.headerRequested , raised in C++ before any dispatch. - ALT + 1 opens the SONG page from anywhere, and again goes back to the page ( Ravving.songRequested , raised in C++ before any dispatch, its press swallowed too). - The header's INSTRUMENTS chips light the machine on screen only: none while the MIXER, the SONG page, the music player or the RECORDER covers the pages ( Session.pageCovered ). - AUTO: the header's AUTO arms recording ( Studio.recordAutomation ): while playing, a SOUND MODIFIERS or SOUND EFFECTS knob turned is written into its machine's pattern at the step playing ( Machine automation lanes, step → value, undoable, saved); the toolbar's AUTO plays them back (lit, "•" while there are some; a long press clears them). - SOUND EFFECTS cards (open): SELECT switches the focused card's effect on or off, BACK closes the section and the focus goes back to the editor above ( ParamCardRow.selectAndBack ). Closed, ▼ past the editor lands on the bar ( FxChain.focusBar() ): ◀ ▶ ring the chips, SELECT switches the ringed effect, ▼ opens the section on its card, ▲ / BACK go back up. A tap on the ▸ SOUND EFFECTS heading opens it on the effect last touched (the heading is the one way in by touch; the bar has no OPEN button). - Dialogs ( RavePopup : ChoicePopup, InputPopup), drop-down lists and the menu darken the page behind them ( ModalDim ); a dialog takes the keys while open and gives the focus back. Dialogs wear one card look (gradient #1e1c24 → #131118, hairline border, radius 16, DialogHeader : spaced title, hint, ✕); the menu drawer is a settings panel (gradient #211f28 → #16141c, hairline-split sections under small captions, flat wells that light yellow, #f0c832). - MENU opens the control center ( ControlCenter in the drawer): MIXER, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, MIDI, SYSTEM cards, the power row (REBOOT and POWER OFF need a second press within 3 s), OUTPUT and BRIGHTNESS sliders on knobs 2 and 1; ◀ ▶ walk the actions, SELECT runs one. - ✱ ( starPressed ) opens and closes the MIXER ( MixerPage , the StackLayout's sixth view, Main.mixerOpen ); a number key leaves it for that page. In it ◀ ▶ or step keys 1–9 pick a strip, knob 1 is its level, knob 2 its pan, the big knob fine level, SELECT mutes, ALT + SELECT solos, BACK or ✱ go back; the step LEDs show the strips (muted dim, picked white). - MODE switches LIVE on the open page's instrument (from anywhere; the MODE LED shows it). ALT is a modifier held in C++ ( Ravving.altHeld ): ALT + big knob is the master volume wherever the focus is ( masterTurned , never dispatched), badged on the MASTER dial, and ALT + knobs 1–3 go straight to Ravving.altKnobTarget (the header's FX SENDS: PHASER, ECHO, HEAVY), a KnobGroup borrowed while ALT is held (badges, frame, pick-up). - A machine's ❚❚ pauses its written pattern ( DrumMachine.paused → Sketchpad.setTrackPaused : its clip stops in PlayfieldManager and is left out of the launch at play; resuming rejoins on the next bar); it stays playable live. - LIVE (one machine at a time, Session.liveMachine ) turns the step keys into pads ( Hardware.onStepDown on the press, onStepPressed on the release): on the drums keys 1–8 play the rows and key 9 held makes accents; with REC on while playing a hit is written at the nearest step ( Machine::recordLive , timed against the measured step length), in STEP entry while stopped at the cursor ( writeAtCursor ). With the toolbar's Q off ( Machine.quantise ) the hit keeps its distance from that step as the subnote's delay (SyncTimer ticks, negative when early), so it plays back as played; the machine keeps these offsets itself ( timing in its state) and puts them back whenever its model rewrites the pattern ( syncTiming ). The LEDs show the pads (rows in the machine's colour, key 9 red, white while held) and drop the playhead ( RavePage.stepKeysArePads ). libzynthbox's own live recorder is not used: it only hears controller ports, and pads sent through SyncTimer arrive as sequencer traffic. - The toolbar's ⟲ ( Machine.loopBar ) plays only the bar on screen: the pattern's playback window moves to it ( bankOffset = that bar, patternLength = one bar) while bars keeps the real length, and paging with ‹ › moves the loop. Not saved; attach and restore put the window back.

libzynthbox doesn't install headers, and its headers pull in all of JUCE. So ZynthboxBridge : dlopen s libzyncoder.so and calls init_zynlib() . libzynthbox needs zyncoder's MIDI router first, the same order as zynthbox-qml. dlopen s libzynthbox.so and resolves three symbols: Plugin::instance() , Plugin::initialize() and Plugin::registerTypes() . Gets the MidiRouter QML singleton and connects to cuiaEvent through the meta-object system. Both libraries are opened with RTLD_LOCAL . RTLD_GLOBAL lets libzynthbox's bundled JUCE/tracktion symbols interpose on libraries loaded later, and the app crashes in Kirigami's platform-plugin lookup.
See building.md , testing.md and debugging.md (tools/: deploy, keys, screenshots, MIDI, measuring, logging) and extending.md (new machines, engines, controls, effects).

ravving ships as a Store AppImage that bundles ravving, the data and ravving-setup ( setup/ ), the page the AppImage opens over zynthbox-qml to install ravving and pick the UI the device runs; both lean on tools/default-app.sh . See packaging.md .

ravving wears one theme, set in code: RAVVING_THEME in the top-level CMakeLists.txt names the folder under data/plasma/desktoptheme/ that ships with the app ( ravving-theme : the Miko theme). The app makes its bundled config/plasmarc its only plasmarc, so neither zynthbox-qml's theme chooser ( ~/.config/plasmarc ) nor any user file can change it; the journal line ravving: theme … says what a run wears. To change the look, change the theme folder or RAVVING_THEME , and rebuild.

Nothing of ravving's goes into zynthbox-qml's folders, and nothing of zynthbox-qml's is written: ravving reads the device's sample library and writes only to its own places ( src/backend/paths.h ), following the XDG base directories: Root On the device What config ~/.config/ravving settings (the input set-up, the UI's choices) state ~/.local/state/ravving the live session ( session.json , the sequence); removed by a purge cache ~/.cache/ravving rebuildable: reversed samples, raw takes, the LV2 port cache library /zynthian/zynthian-my-data/ravving the user's work, kept across reinstalls: projects/ , presets/ , samples/ (takes in samples/takes/ , the RECORDER's in samples/recordings/ , imported bundles' samples in samples/imported/ ), recordings/ (the master's and the RECORDER's TRACKS), exports/ On a desktop the library is ~/.local/share/ravving . Files of an older layout are moved into this one at start ( Paths::initialise() ), and the session's and projects' sample paths with them.

StartupSplash (qml/Splash.qml and SplashLook.qml) shows the logo from the moment libzynthbox is up until the page is ready, then plays a short show into the page. MENU → SETTINGS → STARTUP picks the look, from the next start: ANIME, GLOW, STILL, ZOOM or OFF. While the studio loads the splash is a still picture, since a moving one keeps the screen redrawn every frame and slows the start; the show plays in the page's own window (kwin keeps a full-screen window above a "stay on top" one). The logos are the effect SVGs drawn without their backgrounds (data/branding/make-splash.sh); the album art's wordmark is data/branding/ravving-wordmark.svg.

h: The phone share and the help page
t: FileShare ( share ) is ravving's one-file HTTP server, on port 8098 or the next free one: SEND… → PHONE · QR CODE offers one file at a path of 128 random bits for as long as the dialog is open, 15 minutes at most; FILES → PHONE · BROWSE serves the library as pages ( FileShare.openBrowse , a random path that lives until 15 minutes pass with no request); the same server carries the webpage ( site/ , installed as share/ravving/site ) at http://<device>:8098/help/ , which SETTINGS → HELP shows as a QR code ( get share helpUrl ). Over the fifo: call share offer /path/file , get share url , get share status , get share browseUrl , call share stop ; tools/share-test.sh checks it from the laptop ( testing.md ).

Backend classes : every class of src/backend/ . QML components : the shared base types, the pages and their parts. The undo history : what is undone, steps, the History API, making a feature undoable. Bluetooth : devices, pairing, files and audio output. Live recordings : video and audio recording, the voice over, the computer link.

Every class of the backend library ( src/backend/ ), what it does and how the others use it. Each class has its full reference in the API reference. The drums play through libzynthbox exactly the way zynthbox-qml's sketchpad does, with ravving's C++ objects standing in for the Python ones libzynthbox talks to: Class Role Stands in for / ports Studio backend root ( studio in QML): builds the machines from data/kits.json , transport (play/stop, tempo, swing, step), saves the sequence after edits; a preview clock on a desktop; the sampler's browser ( sampleFiles() : kits.json sampleFolders , folders labelled short) and hold-to-hear previews ( previewSample() / stopPreview() : a one-shot clip on SamplerSynth's global lane) sketchpad song + transport glue Machine the base of every machine: track (level, pan, effects, mute, ❚❚, kick cuts), pattern (bars, view bar following the playing bar while playing: follow , off when a bar is picked mid-play, back on when stopped; playhead, STEP cursor), presets, LIVE play/record, UNDO / REDO of the pattern ( canUndo , undo() , canRedo , redo() : every edited whose content differs is a step back, 50 deep, changes within 0.5 s of the last joining its step (a knob turned, a handle dragged); the mix, sound and effects are left out, and so are a subclass's viewKeys() such as the sampler's bank; beginEditGroup() / endEditGroup() make a take one step; a project open starts it afresh); subclasses give steps, sound and velocities; SECTIONS: sectionContent() (the pattern part less soundState() 's keys and the viewKeys() , plus ❚❚ and ONCE) and applySectionContent() (laid over the machine's own by withSection() , the history started over; an empty map empties the pattern), sectionBars() / sectionSounds() ; the samplers keep their banks' hits, not their samples ( SamplerBanks ) Its own length ( bars , m_bars ) is kept apart from what its clip plays: applyPlayLength() is the one place that sets the clip's patternLength and bankOffset , from playedBars() : one bar under ⟲ (the bar on screen), the section's span under ONCE ( once , setSpan() from the studio; the bars past its own emptied by clearRest() ), else its own; while it rests the playhead hides and a live hit is not written. new MonoMachine a mono line (one note per step) with ACCENT and SLIDE (the note lasts 1.5 steps and a legato engine glides into the next): page 3's AC 303 ( bass , DISTRHO Nekobi: accent velocity 127 vs 80, Nekobi accents above 90) and page 4's THERE LEAD ( lead , Calf Monosynth, legato + portamento); base note and velocities from kits.json; presets in scale degrees ( bass-presets.json , lead-presets.json ), RANDOM, octave; follows the header's key: a ROOT or SCALE change snaps every note to the nearest note of the new key (upwards on a tie), and the line's key is saved with it new ChordMachine page 2's POLY-6 on TAL NoiseMaker (6 voices, Juno chorus); a custom voicing is scale degrees, or chromatic (semitones from the chord base, chart letter c ) when a note is outside the key, so a chart can carry a C7 in E♭ major; setStepNotes(step, "48,52,55,58") for scripts; live keys below 1000 are chord degrees, from 1000 on single scale degrees ( noteKey , noteKeyForNote , noteOfKey : the NOTES tab's LIVE, written one note into the step's voicing by a take or STEP entry): each step holds a voicing, a diatonic chord (a degree stacked in thirds from the scale, triad or seventh per degree by the chord set: Classic, Triads, Sevenths) or a custom set of scale degrees (built in NOTES); a run of one voicing is one held chord; everything is in scale degrees, so a key, set or octave change revoices it all. exit with _exit() (see the exit row below).

Kits. data/kits.json holds every machine: drumMachines (track, Zynthian channel, engine, default kit and preset) and machines by kind ( mono : bass on track 3, lead on track 5; chords : track 4), each with its engine (type, LV2 URI, fixed controls ), its sound (SOUND MODIFIERS), presets file, defaultPreset , baseNote and velocities. Studio builds them generically and publishes the non-drum ones as studio.machines.<key> . Also the kit folder (the 40 drum-machine soundfonts in zynthian-data). Grid rows are not written by hand: DrumKit reads them out of the kit (soundfonts are not General MIDI: the 909's clap is on 50, the Linn's on 39). Tapping a machine's nameplate opens ChoicePopup with every kit; DrumMachine::loadKit() moves each hit to the new kit's note for its role (keeping accents), the engine reloads the soundfont ( SoundEngine::reconfigure ), and the choice is saved in the session ( session.json ). A double tap on the nameplate goes back to the default kit ( resetKit() ). A new engine type is one SoundEngine subclass plus a line in SoundEngine::createEngine() . Presets are factory beats (House, Techno, Electro, Breaks, Hip Hop, Groove, Empty) that replace the pattern. They are drum charts written per role ( "KICK": "X...x..." , X = an accented hit), so every preset plays on every kit. The toolbar's PRESET button shows the loaded preset (• once edited) and opens a ChoicePopup by genre; SAVE CURRENT AS NEW stores the pattern as "My Beat N" in Paths::presets()/drum-presets.json , and DELETE removes a user preset. The other machines save the same way into their own file, named by the factory file's userName ("My Bassline N", "My Progression N", "My Melody N", "My Pattern N").

Row mix. Each row's level, mute and solo are kept per role (they survive kit changes) and live in the hits' velocities: level 0.8 → velocity 100, an accent hits ×1.27 harder, and a muted or soloed-out row gets velocity −1, PatternModel's "do not play". Accents are kept by the machine and saved in the session with the row mix, never read back from velocities. The session lives in Paths::state() ( ~/.local/state/ravving ; an explicit path: libzynthbox's MidiRouter renames the application to "zynthbox-qml" while it initialises).

The pattern interface. StepGrid and PatternToolbar only draw and forward to a pattern object: rows, stepCount, steps, accents, playhead, bars, viewBar, presets, presetName, presetEdited, canSavePresets, rowLevels, rowMuted, rowSoloed, toggleStep(), toggleAccent(), clear(), loadPreset(), saveAsPreset(), removePreset(), setRowLevel(), setRowMuted(), setRowSoloed(), audition() . The studio's DrumMachine and SamplerMachine implement it; PatternState.qml implements it in memory for pages whose backend is still to come (the melodic toolbars).

The QML components in qml/ : the shared base types, the pages and their parts. They follow the UI rules . Studio machines are shown by MachinePanel (a MachineModule backed by a Machine: level, pan, ❚❚, effects, sound, REC/takes, STEP cursor, LIVE pad and keyboard bookkeeping), extended by DrumMachinePanel (step grid; pads = rows, key 9 = accent), MonoMachinePanel (mono PianoRoll with pattern: machine ; in LIVE all 16 step keys play the scale from the root upwards and ▲ ▼ shift the octave (with STEP on, playing or not, they walk the rows, each heard: previewSelection , and SELECT writes the row: writeSelection / selectionKey , shared in MachinePanel ); with showRibbon the lead's Ribbon : its notes go through the same LIVE path, a slide starts the next note before ending the last so the engine glides, drag up = vibrato) and ChordMachinePanel (the nameplate shows the loaded TAL sound's title, POLY-6 for its own; a tap opens the sound picker, a double tap rebuilds its own sound from TAL's start-up sound, the engine's controls and the default knobs; CHORDS / NOTES / SLOTS tabs: ChordRoll , a poly PianoRoll on the same steps, ChordSlots ; ◀ ▶ switch them while the editor has the focus ( moveView , viewCount ); the step keys and ▲ ▼ work on the view on screen; CHORD SET, chord keys played as pads that also fill an armed slot; LIVE follows the tab: on CHORDS / SLOTS pads 1–7 = the degrees' chords, on NOTES all 16 pads play single scale notes (note keys), ▲ ▼ the octave while LIVE (the rows with STEP on; SELECT writes the selected chord or note); ▲ ▼ = octave while LIVE) and SamplerMachinePanel ( SampleScreen with the slot's waveform and trim handles, a KnobGroup itself: a tap on it or ▲ from the grid's top row gives knob 1 to the start handle and knob 2 to the end, ▼ gives the knobs back to the rows, LOAD with hold-to-hear previews, ▶, CLEAR, REVERSE, ● REC and INPUT ( InputPopup ), PITCH; the step grid over the bank's slots; BANK A–D chips and ◀ ▶; pads 1–8 = slots, key 9 = accent; knobs 1–3 = the selected row's mute, solo, level). All of qml/ is one QML module, Ravving , built by qt_add_qml_module into the binary (qmlcachegen bytecode, typed bindings compiled to C++) and loaded with loadFromModule("Ravving", "Main") ; Hardware and HardwareEvent join it through QML_ELEMENT . Every file imports Ravving ; there are no relative imports. For development, RAVVING_QML_DIR makes QmlSourceOverride (a URL interceptor) serve the .qml files from a source tree instead, so QML edits need only a restart. How ravving undoes and redoes edits: the History class, what is recorded, and how a new feature becomes undoable. The classes are in the API reference. Ravving has one undo history for the project, History ( src/backend/history.* ), published to QML as studio.history . Everything that can be undone goes through it; nothing keeps an undo stack of its own.

The patterns : every machine's notes, steps, chords, slots, accents, slides, lengths, automation, live timing and its preset's name ( Machine::historyState() ). Not the sound (source, factory sound, MODS), the mix (level, pan, mute), the effects or the project's settings (tempo, swing, key). Anything can join by becoming a participant (below). And the arrangement ( Sections::historyState() , "SECTIONS"): which sections there are, in which order, their names, colours and lengths, and the song. A section removed is put aside with its content ( Sections::m_removed ), so undoing the removal brings it back whole, in its place and in the song; redoing it hands over to the neighbour as REMOVE did. What is not in it: the section on screen (a pick is no step, so an undo never switches what plays; a section added and then undone is the one exception, the first section takes over) and the machines' content (theirs). The removed sections are forgotten when a project is opened.

What it undoes Where The timeline the project's last step, whichever machines it touched the header's ↶ ↷, ALT + ◀ ▶ on the machine pages; a toast names it ("UNDO · CHORDS + BASS") One machine that machine's last change only, wherever it is in the timeline the pattern toolbar's ↶ ↷ ( machine.undo() / redo() , machine.canUndo / canRedo ) A machine can go back on its own because the participants' states are independent of each other: putting back the bass's last pattern cannot break the chords'.

h: What becomes one step › One turn of the event loop
t: One turn of the event loop. Everything recorded before control goes back to the event loop is one step. An action that changes several machines at once is undone in one go without any call: CLEAR (every machine), a key change that snaps the bass and the lead into the new key.

h: What becomes one step › Quick changes of one participant
t: Quick changes of one participant. A change within History::MergeMs (500 ms) of the same participant's last one joins its step: a knob turning, a handle dragged, a SELECT move repeated.

h: What becomes one step › A group
t: A group. Everything between begin(label) and end() (they nest), for an action spread over several turns. Machines also have their own groups for a recorded take ( Machine::beginEditGroup() / endEditGroup() ): the take is recorded once, at its end. A step stores, for each participant it touched, the state before and after; nothing else. The history keeps History::Depth (100) steps.

forget(participant) : its state is replaced wholesale, so its steps go (a section picked: undoing into a section that is not on screen would be a surprise; an engine attached again). clear() : a project opened or NEW ( Studio::applyProjectState() ).

C++ ( History ): add(p) / remove(p) register a participant (its state now is where it starts) / take it out record(p) after each change: a step, or part of the open one, when its state differs forget(p) , clear() see above undo() , redo() , canUndo , canRedo , undoText , redoText the timeline undoIn(key) , redoIn(key) , canUndoIn(key) , canRedoIn(key) one participant begin(label) , end() a group signals changed() , undone(what) , redone(what) QML: studio.history.undo() , .redo() , .canUndo , .canRedo , .undoText , .redoText , .begin() , .end() , .clear() ; a machine's own: machine.undo() , .redo() , .canUndo , .canRedo .

Implement HistoryParticipant (four functions): - historyKey() : a name unique among the participants ("bass", "song"); - historyLabel() : how the user reads a step of it ("BASS", "SONG"); - historyState() : its state as plain data, equal when nothing that matters changed (leave out what only says what is on screen: a bar shown, a tab); - applyHistoryState(state) : become that state (it may emit its change signals as usual: the history does not record what it puts back). Register it: studio.history → history->add(this) once it exists (Studio does it for the machines, Machine::setHistory() ). Call history->record(this) after each change the user makes (a machine does it on its edited() signal). Changes that are not the user's (a state restored, a project loaded) call forget(this) instead. Its own ↶ ↷, if it has any, call history->undoIn(key) / redoIn(key) ; their enabled state is canUndoIn(key) / canRedoIn(key) , refreshed on changed() . Nothing else: the timeline, the grouping, the toasts and the header's buttons come with it.

historyState() is computed after every change, so keep it cheap (a map of the content); the machines' is their contentState() less the sound and the view. One machine's undo clears the timeline's redo (what it would redo does not match what is there); the timeline's undo of a step a machine was part of is redone by that machine's ↷ too (it falls back to the timeline's redo).

How ravving uses BlueZ and PipeWire for Bluetooth: devices, pairing, file transfer and audio output. The classes are in the API reference; the system setup is on Running on a Zynthbox. Ravving's Bluetooth does what a phone's does: pair, connect, send a file, play through a speaker or headphones, receive a file. What a Zynthbox needs for it is in packaging.md ("Bluetooth on a fresh device"), the tests in testing.md and the troubleshooting table in debugging.md . Backend Bluetooth ( src/backend/bluetooth.* , QML bluetooth ), on BluezQt: the adapter (power, discovery, discoverable for three minutes), the devices (connected first, then paired, then by signal; private-address phones without a name hidden until paired), a pairing Agent (DisplayYesNo: a passkey to confirm or a PIN to type lands in pairing , answered with answerPairing ), pair → trust → connect, forget, OBEX Object Push sending ( sendFile , progress in transfer ), an ObexAgent accepting pushes into the library's incoming/ folder, and the audio switch ( useAsOutput ).

Discovery. The Pi has one radio for Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, and an inquiry breaks up a playing A2DP link, so a scan lasts 12 s ( DiscoverySeconds ) and starts on its own only while no audio device is connected. It scans classic devices only ( setDiscoveryFilter {Transport: bredr} ): a dual-mode speaker paired from its LE advertisement gets no A2DP sink, and the Pi's firmware has no LE Audio.

Audio. When an audio device connects, WirePlumber makes a sink node bluez_output.<address>.1 (and an input / capture node for HFP). useAsOutput hands it to AudioOutputs ( outputs , also the control center's AUDIO OUTPUT card), which does not make it the default sink: that would clock the whole JACK graph by the Bluetooth transport in 256-frame chunks (glitches) and leave the master's links to the jacks in place (sound from both). Instead the jacks keep the clock, a pw-loopback of ravving's own ( ravving-out , a virtual sink whose playback stream targets the Bluetooth sink with a 2048-frame buffer) is started, the master's two output ports are linked to it with pw-link (its inputs have no JACK name, so libzynthbox's JackConnectionHandler cannot) and the jacks are muted, not unlinked: an unlinked jacks sink is suspended and the Bluetooth transport would become the graph's clock. Off, on disconnect, forget or exit, the loopback stops and the jack links come back. A device connected on the headset profile only ( playback_MONO ) gets a mono mix-down.

The codec. PipeWire offers a2dp-sink-sbc_xq beside plain SBC (ravving's WirePlumber drop-in sets bluez5.enable-sbc-xq ) but WirePlumber connects with plain SBC. SETTINGS · BLUETOOTH · SBC-XQ ( AudioOutputs.preferSbcXq , on by default) switches the output in use to SBC-XQ when it offers it, or back to plain SBC, once per connection ( wpctl set-profile ); each paired device can override it with its own chip in the BLUETOOTH dialog ( AudioOutputs.sbcXqByDevice , setSbcXqFor() ), since a device may advertise the bitpool and still not sustain it. A codec switch replaces the sink node under the same name: AudioOutputs notices the node id changing and routes to the new one; a Bluetooth output gets its codec first and is routed to once its new sink is there.

The silence watch. While another output plays, OutputWatch listens to what goes into the loopback and what comes out: music going in with silence coming out for six seconds is routed again once (a fresh loopback), and if it is still silent the issues center says the output plays no sound.

h: Bluetooth › One audio device at a time
t: One audio device at a time. BlueZ keeps one local A2DP endpoint per codec, shared by every device, and a local endpoint carries one stream; PipeWire registers one SBC source (SBC-XQ reuses it). So while one device streams SBC, a second SBC device cannot set up its audio ( Unable to select SEP , br-connection-create-socket ). When a device the user is connecting answered but could not connect while another audio device is connected, ravving shows SWITCHING FROM · the other , disconnects it, waits 1 s for BlueZ to free the endpoint and connects again; ravving's own reconnect never takes the link from a playing device.

Pages retried. A page timeout ( Host is down ) is retried after 2, 5 and 10 s (about 37 s with BlueZ's 5.12 s page; the row reads "waking…"; disconnecting or forgetting stops it) before COULD NOT CONNECT with the hint NOT ANSWERING: FREE IT FROM A PHONE, OR TURN IT OFF AND ON. PLAY THROUGH's sink poll (15 s) starts once the connection is made.

h: Bluetooth › The kept output comes back
t: The kept output comes back. AudioOutputs keeps the Bluetooth address of the output picked. When Bluetooth comes on (a start, the switch), that device is connected once, 3 s later, if it is paired and nothing else plays. Never in a loop: paging a speaker in standby wakes it up.

Files. Sending opens an OBEX session ( Target: opp ) and pushes the file; receiving needs the device VISIBLE (discoverable + pairable, three minutes) and lands under library/incoming/ , which PROJECT ▾ → IMPORT lists as "received" and the music library as the album "Received".
UI. BluetoothPopup from the control center's BLUETOOTH card.

How LIVE REC records the screen or the sound: the JACK tap, FFmpeg, the microphone and voice over, the keys shown on a video, and the computer link. The classes are in the API reference. LIVE REC records the session: the screen (or a USB camera) with the master's sound, as one MP4 in the library's videos/ folder ( Paths::videos() ), or the sound alone as a WAV among the TRACKS ("Audio only" below). Code: src/backend/videorecorder.* ( video ), src/backend/audiotap.* , src/backend/computerlink.* ( computer ), qml/components/ComputerPopup.qml , LiveRecPopup.qml , VideoSavedPopup.qml , the LIVE REC card in ControlCenter.qml . The rule it is built on: the sound comes first. A video may cost the audio nothing it can hear, and the audio in the video must never drop.

h: How a recording is made › The sound is tapped, not recorded through AudioLevels
t: The sound is tapped, not recorded through AudioLevels. AudioTap is ravving's own JACK client ( ravving-video , stereo in) connected to the master's last outputs (what the speakers get: the LIVE FX inserts included, which the header's ● WAV recording misses). Its process callback copies each cycle into a ring of 2^20 frames (21.8 s at 48 kHz) and touches nothing else; a plain thread drains the ring into a named pipe ( $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/ ravving-video-<stamp>.pipe , 1 MB of kernel buffering) as raw 32-bit float stereo. ffmpeg reads the pipe as -f f32le . Why not libzynthbox's AudioLevels (the WAV recorder's and the exporter's path): it runs one recording at a time, and a video session must leave the header's ● and the samplers' record-to-pad free. Why not ffmpeg's own -f jack input: its ring is 16 periods (85 ms at 256 frames), so an encoder or SD-card stall longer than that drops sound; this ring holds 21 seconds, and what it could not hold is counted ( audioDroppedMs , a warning in the issues center) rather than lost quietly.

h: How a recording is made › The picture is ffmpeg's
t: The picture is ffmpeg's. x11grab of the display ( -draw_mouse 0 ), or v4l2 of the camera, encoded with libx264 on two threads at nice -n 10 : the Pi 5 has no hardware H.264 encoder (ffmpeg lists h264_v4l2m2m , but the Pi 5's V4L2 nodes are its ISP and HEVC decoder). The tiers ("Limits", below) all run with 0 xruns.

h: How a recording is made › Sync without a shared clock
t: Sync without a shared clock. ffmpeg stamps every grabbed frame with the wall clock ( -use_wallclock_as_timestamps 1 ; on this ffmpeg x11grab's default stamps are the wall clock too). The tap takes the wall-clock moment of its first sample on the audio thread, from the cycle's own start ( jack_get_cycle_times : the cycle began now − (jack_get_time() − cycle_usecs) ago), and ffmpeg is told it with -itsoffset on the audio input. With -copyts both streams sit on the same absolute clock in the file, to the millisecond.

h: How a recording is made › Matroska first, then one remux
t: Matroska first, then one remux. The recording goes to .recording-<stamp>.mkv : a Matroska is readable even if ravving or ffmpeg dies (an MP4 without its index is not). On STOP the tap closes the pipe (ffmpeg's audio input ends), ffmpeg gets SIGINT and finishes its file, and ffprobe reads the two streams' start times: the audio began while ffmpeg was starting (~0.45 s before the first frame), so ffmpeg -ss <video start − audio start> -i rec.mkv -c copy -movflags +faststart cuts the head to the first video frame, writes the MP4 with its index up front and its title / date tags, and the Matroska is removed. The remux copies packets: a few seconds for a long recording ("SAVING" on the card and the plate). If the remux fails the Matroska is kept under the final name.

SETTINGS · VIDEO · MIC: the RECORDER's input, as it is set up there (MIC / GUITAR / LINE, the jack in use, its GAIN, its effects), mixed into the video's sound. Nothing of the input is repeated for the video: InputRecorder::setListener(ports) adds the tap's two mic ports ( ravving-video:mic_l / mic_r ) as one more destination at the end of the input chain ( JackWiring::setInputChain 's listeners , beside the monitor lane and the take recorder; a mono input feeds both), the input counts as in use while a listener is set (its effects run), and the audio thread adds the ports to the master's sound as the video hears it. The master itself is untouched: the speakers get the mic only with the RECORDER's MONITOR on, in which case the video hears it twice (louder), so one or the other. tools/video-test.sh records once with MIC on and checks the link; tools/video-mic-check.sh is the listening test: a recording with the music stopped while someone speaks, then the file's audio measured.

With MIC on, the tap mixes the master and the mic as a voice over ( AudioTap::setVoiceOver , SETTINGS · VIDEO · VOICE), since a plain sum leaves a voice at a normal distance some 25 dB under the master: the mic is made crisp: a 120 Hz high-pass and a +4 dB high shelf from 3 kHz (RBJ biquads on the audio thread), then lifted by VOICE LIFT (+6 dB by default, +12 or flat); its envelope is followed (instant attack, 250 ms release); while it is above the voice threshold the master is turned down to VOICE DUCK (−12 dB by default, −6 or −18; 0 is off) in 20 ms and comes back over 600 ms once the voice stops, so the music sits in the background exactly while someone speaks; the threshold follows the music: it is −34 dBFS at least, and 12 dB over what the speakers are expected to leak into the mic right now, i.e. the master's envelope (as ducked) times a leak ratio the tap learns as the mic's level over the master's: down within a second, up over 8 s, never past −26 dB of the master (0.02, −34 dB, to start; from the moment VIDEO is on, since the mic is wired then). Against the expected leak only a voice counts, so the beat does not duck itself through a mic near the speakers. The learning is slow upwards so that a steady tone under the threshold does not become "leak". A mic that hears the speakers louder than −26 dB of the master (the mic in front of the speaker) still ducks itself, and a leak between the start value and the cap ducks the beat for a second or two at its start, until the ratio has climbed. The RECORDER's GAIN scales the voice and the leak alike, so the ratio holds when it is turned; the sum goes through a look-ahead peak limiter (1 ms ahead, ceiling −1 dBFS, 150 ms release): the mix runs through a 1 ms delay line, the loudest sample in the line sets the gain, which gets down over a quarter of the line, so a hot mic over a loud beat is turned down before the peak comes out, never clipped, and never with the click of a gain step. The 1 ms sits inside the 3 ms of audio offset; the master without the mic is not delayed. The RECORDER's GAIN still sets how hot the voice comes in, and the recorder watches it: while VIDEO is on with MIC the input is wired into the tap at once (not only while recording) and its peak is metered ten times a second ( micLevel , before the lift). SETTINGS · VIDEO shows it on a LEVEL bar with the −6 dB mark, and the project plate carries it standing in its right corner while VIDEO is on (red while hot, a blue dot at its foot while the music ducks). A peak over −6 dBFS within the last two seconds is micHot : the bar turns red and the settings say MIC TOO HOT, turn the GAIN down; a mic peaking around −12 dBFS leaves the mix room and the limiter idle. The voice over is for a voice: with the RECORDER on GUITAR or LINE the input is summed as it is (through the limiter), nothing ducks under a guitar, and the VOICE rows say so. The settings apply at once, on a recording under way too. With DUCK and LIFT both 0 the mix is tools/video-voice-check.sh measures it: a steady 300 Hz tone at −12 dBFS into the tap's master ports as the music (so the measure does not depend on the project open; MUSIC=project plays the project instead), a 1 kHz tone in bursts (tools/tone.py, −20 dBFS, TONE_DB for another level) into the tap's mic ports as the voice; second by second, the music must be DUCK dB quieter while the tone is on, the tone must come out LIFT dB louder, the file must show no clipping (its peak under −0.5 dBFS, no run of samples stuck at the ceiling), and the meter must read the tone ( video.micLevel near −20 dBFS while a burst plays, micHot false; a −3 dBFS burst sets micHot ).

h: The hardware keys and the UI
t: The LIVE REC card (control center): a tap opens the LIVE REC dialog ( LiveRecPopup.qml ): WHAT, a VIDEO (the screen or a USB camera with the master's sound, an MP4 among the VIDEOS) or AUDIO ONLY (the sound alone, a 24-bit WAV among the TRACKS, see below); MIC, the RECORDER's input in the sound; and START, which switches LIVE REC on and begins after the TIMER (the dialog is the confirmation, so a stray tap never starts one; the drawer closes first, so it is not in the picture; the TIMER counts down on an overlay that is not recorded either, since ffmpeg starts after it). ◀ ▶ pick WHAT, ▲ ▼ toggle the MIC, SELECT starts. The card reads LIVE REC · READY / REC IN n / REC mm:ss / LIVE REC · SAVING and is lit while LIVE REC is on; a tap while on ends the recording and switches LIVE REC off. A new project (NEW in the project menu) switches LIVE REC off too, a recording under way saved first ( Projects::created ). While VIDEO is on, RECORD and STOP are the video's before any page sees them ( Ravving::handleCuia → VideoRecorder::takesKey ): RECORD starts when idle (a toast says ■ stops when it is already recording), STOP ends the recording (and stops the music with it: the session is over) or cancels the countdown; STOP with nothing recording is the transport's again. The header's ● and ■ do the same ( Session.toggleRecording / Session.stop ). The project plate shows the video's state while VIDEO is on (VIDEO READY · ● RECORDS, VIDEO IN 3, ● REC 01:23, VIDEO · SAVING); the RECORD LED glows dim red when ready, orange during the countdown, red while recording; STOP lights while there is something to end. While a video records, every device key pressed (ALT combos as "ALT + MODE", knob turns as "KNOB 1 ▲", "BIG KNOB ▼") is named in a short red notice at the screen's bottom ( Ravving::keyShown → Main.qml's second Toast), so the video shows what was played; SETTINGS · VIDEO · KEYS turns it off ( video.showKeys , on by default). An audio recording shows none: there is no picture to explain. VIDEO SAVED / LIVE REC SAVED (when a recording ends): the file, its length, size and picture size; DELETE at the left (a ConfirmButton: the second tap within three seconds removes the file, VideoRecorder::remove ), RENAME and SEND… at the right (SendPopup: a USB stick's ravving/videos or ravving/exports , a computer, the phone); an audio recording also has METADATA… (below). A failure (ffmpeg missing, no space, the encoder giving no frames in 12 s, ffmpeg dying) is a toast, an issues-center entry and video.error ; what ffmpeg wrote before dying is still saved when it has frames.

LIVE REC's AUDIO ONLY ( video.mode "audio", VideoRecorder::audioOnly ) is the same recorder without the picture: the tap feeds ffmpeg as before, but the command has no video input and no encoder, only -c:a pcm_s24le -f wav into .recording-<name>.wav in the exports folder ( Paths::exports() , the TRACKS the music player and FILES list), so nothing is encoded and nothing has to be lined up (no -copyts , no -itsoffset ). The first bytes out (ffmpeg's out_time_us in the progress report) stand for the first frame; stopping renames the WAV to <project> - <date>.wav (no remux, nothing to cut: the sound begins where it began). The MIC, the voice over and the limiter apply as to a video. The key notices are not shown. When it ends, LIVE REC SAVED offers, besides DELETE, RENAME and SEND…, METADATA…: the export dialog over the file ( ExportPopup.openForFile , the same form without WHAT and the lengths; SAVE WITH TAGS), which calls Exporter::finishRecording(rawFile, metadata) : the WAV is written whole in the FORMAT chosen (WAV 24-bit, FLAC, OGG, MP3) under the NAME given in the exports folder, tagged with the TITLE, ARTIST, ALBUM, GENRE, COMPOSER and COMMENT, its cover drawn and saved beside it, its sidecar JSON written, the raw WAV removed, and the files copied to the stick or sent to the computer picked. That is the track export's own finishing ( Exporter::writeAndTag , one path for both), so a live recording and an exported track are the same kind of file afterwards. The tagged track then stands for the recording in LIVE REC SAVED ( VideoRecorder::adopt ), so RENAME and SEND… act on it. Without METADATA… the plain WAV stays, playable and listed as any track.

SETTINGS · COMPUTERS holds the laptops or PCs exports and videos can be sent to over SSH: any number ( Computers , computers , a list of ComputerLink s, each its own group computers/<id> of the settings file; a single-computer set-up of an older version is moved into c1 ). ADD A COMPUTER asks for the host name or address, the user there, and that user's password; a computer already in the list as the same user@host is set up again rather than added twice. The password is used once: it opens the first connection so the device's own key ( ~/.config/ravving/ssh/id_ed25519 , made on the first CONNECT) can be installed with ssh-copy-id ; it is never written to the settings. The password reaches ssh through SSH_ASKPASS (a helper script of ravving's printing a file readable by root alone, made for the set-up's seconds and removed after, SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force so no terminal is involved). The computer's host key is kept in ravving's own known_hosts (accepted on the first connection, refused if it changes; FORGET removes that computer's entry with ssh-keygen -R , the others stay). The Downloads folder is asked of the computer ( xdg-user-dir DOWNLOAD , else ~/Downloads ); files go there with scp , one at a time ( busy / phase / progress ), and sent(ok, count, label) ends it with a toast. Statuses: unset, setting-up, ready, unreachable, refused (the key refused by the computer: CONNECT AGAIN with the password), failed ( error says why: a wrong password, a name that does not resolve, SSH refused or no answer, a changed host key). Where it is used: one standard SEND… button ( SendPopup , the destinations there are: every writable USB stick's ravving/ folder through RemovableDrives::copyFiles , each computer, and a phone by QR code: see "Sending to a phone" in the manual) in the FILES browser (every kind: a project is bundled for the destination by Exporter::exportProjectFile , a preset written out as one JSON file by FileBrowser::presetFile ), on VIDEO SAVED, on each track in the music player, in the pattern presets dialog and the sound picker; and the export dialog's COMPUTER row (a chip per computer, one lit), which sends a new track or bundle as soon as it is written ( Exporter::sendToComputer , the metadata's computer = the computer's id). The computer needs an SSH server: Linux openssh-server (Arch: systemctl enable --now sshd ), macOS "Remote Login"; Windows' OpenSSH server has no $HOME/Downloads in its default shell and is not supported.

Recordings end with SIGINT, once (a second signal makes ffmpeg quit without its trailer); -t is never used, since it compares against the absolute timestamps -copyts keeps. The pipe input is not probed ( -probesize 32 -analyzeduration 0 ), or ffmpeg would read 5 s of raw audio before opening the output; the video input's queue is 64 frames. A step of the system clock during a recording (the Pi has no RTC; timesyncd steps it on the first network sync after boot) puts a jump in the video's timestamps: start recording once the device has been online for a moment. The screen recording shows exactly what is on the display: a dialog opened during the recording is in the picture; the countdown overlay and the drawer are not. USB cameras are found in /sys/class/video4linux (the node with index 0 on a USB device); the capture size follows the tier (640 × 480 for LOW, 1280 × 720 otherwise). The quality tiers (SETTINGS · VIDEO · QUALITY): HIGH full screen 30 fps (veryfast, crf 21), MEDIUM full screen 15 fps (veryfast, crf 23, the default), LOW 640 × 400 30 fps (veryfast, crf 26); AAC audio at 192 kb/s. All three run with 0 xruns on a Pi 5; tools/video-encode-impact.sh measures them (mirror any change to the encoder arguments there).

What ravving relies on for each engine and where each fact comes from. The port facts come from the engine mods' research (each mod's docs/RESEARCH.md , decoded from the engine's own source); read the mod before changing an engine's engine.controls in data/kits.json or its MODS profile in data/engines.json .

h: The MODS: one profile per engine (data/engines.json)
t: What a page lets the user tweak of an engine (its SOUND MODIFIERS, the MODS cards, and its expressions, such as the lead ribbon's vibrato) is the engine's , not the machine's: one profile per engine in data/engines.json , found by the engine itself ( type , and for jalv the plugin uri ; EngineProfiles ). Every source that plays an engine shows its knobs, on any machine: Profile Engine Shown for tal-noisemaker TAL-NoiseMaker (jalv) CHORDS' own synth nekobi Nekobi (jalv) BASS' own synth calf-monosynth Calf Monosynth (jalv) LEAD's own synth, BASS' 808 · Monosynth source fluidsynth FluidSynth every soundfont source (one set for all of a machine's soundfonts: its knobs are offsets to the preset's own sound) A source starts its knobs where its own engine.controls put those ports (the 808's cutoff 400 Hz shows as the CUTOFF knob at 400), so loading a source never changes its sound; without such a control a knob starts at the profile's default . The project keeps each set apart: sound (the own engine's), sourceSound (the soundfonts'), sourceSounds (each other plugin source's, by name); AUTO lanes are sound/… , source/… and sources/<source>/… .

h: The MODS: one profile per engine (data/engines.json) › An engine with no profile shows no MODS
t: An engine with no profile shows no MODS. A machine or a source that brings its own sound in kits.json keeps it (a special case; the profile is the rule).

h: The MODS: one profile per engine (data/engines.json) › Checked against the engines' real ports, twice
t: Checked against the engines' real ports, twice. On the laptop, tools/check-engines.py ( ctest -R engines ) checks every knob, choice, expression and kits.json control against the plugins' ports, ranges included, from tests/data/lv2-ports.json . Run tools/check-engines.py --refresh to read them again from the device's lv2info after adding an engine or upgrading plugins. On the device, when an engine starts, SoundEngine::hasControl() checks the MODS of the source playing, and a knob on a control the engine lacks is an issue in the issues centre ("BASS MODS: Calf Monosynth lacks 1 of their controls"). Adding an engine's MODS: add its profile to data/engines.json (the cards as SoundControls reads them: symbol , min , max , default 0..1, "curve": "log" , or choices for a switch), refresh the ports if it is a new plugin, run tools/check-engines.py , then hear each knob on the device ( device.sh call <machine>.activeSound setValue CARD KNOB 0..1 ).

http://distrho.sf.net/plugins/Nekobi , a TB-303 clone. Research: nekobi_acid_mod . Fact What ravving does waveform : the plugin's own labels are wrong : 0 renders a square, 1 a sawtooth WAVE switch: SAW = 1, SQR = 0 decay is a rate : higher % = shorter (τ 2.3 s at 0 %, 42 ms at 100 %) DECAY runs 100 → 0, so turning it up lengthens notes accent is velocity > 90 (forced short decay, filter "wow" from resonance) plain 80, accent 127 glide is always on (τ ≈ 13 ms) when notes overlap SLIDE = the note lasts 1.5 steps cutoff 0–100 % ≈ 0–5 kHz (capped ~6.5 kHz), resonance 0–95 %, env_mod , accent , tuning ±12 CUTOFF, RESO, ENV MOD, ACCENT, TUNE as LV2 ranges volume is linear ( v/100 ); Zynthbox's jalv wrapper pins it, ravving's jalv does not volume 100

http://kunz.corrupt.ch/products/tal-noisemaker . Research: noizemakr_mod . Fact What ravving does every port is a bare 0..1; enums quantise as floor(v·(n−1) + 1.5) (1-based): write i/(n−1) voices 1 (6 voices), portamentomode 1 (On: chords glide too), lfo1destination 1/7 (Filter), lfo1waveform 0 (sine), transpose 0.5 (0 oct), filtertype 0 (LP 24 dB; its den is 11) osc1waveform : Saw, Pulse, Noise; osc2waveform : Saw, Pulse, Triangle, Sine, Noise WAVE: SAW, JUNO (pulse, osc1pw 0.75), SQR (pulse 0.5), TRI (osc 2) lfo1amount is bipolar and cubic: (2(v − 0.5))³ , 0.5 = none LFO knob spans 0.5 … 1 lfo1rate = (e^(0.2 + 3v·ln20) − 1) / 19 Hz 0.3 ≈ 0.9 Hz, a slow sweep envelopes are one-poles, very steep: release 67 ms at 0.3, 0.5 s at 0.45, 1 s at 0.5, 3.5 s at 0.6, 12 s near 1; attack 16 ms at 0.15, 0.77 s at 0.45 (computed with the mod's own formulas; its summary table is off) ATTACK spans 0 … 0.55 (3.6 ms … 3.2 s), LENGTH 0.15 … 0.65 (10 ms … 5.8 s) chorus1enable , chorus2enable (the Juno chorus I / II) CHORUS switch OFF / I / II detune , cutoff (log inside the engine), resonance , portamento SPREAD, CUTOFF, RESO, GLIDE volume 's curve is undocumented; measured steeper than linear (0.55 → 0.51 RMS, 0.25 → 0.068) volume 0.25 256 factory presets in the bundle's presets.ttl (78 leads, 53 basses, 34 FX, 28 drums, 26 pads, 15 arps, 13 keys, 7 chords: the name's prefix), each with its port values next to the JUCE state (the mod's research reached them only through the programs extension, which jalv does not surface) SOUND ▾ on CHORDS loads one by setting its ports ( Machine::loadSoundPreset ), keeping voices , volume , transpose ; the SOUND MODIFIERS follow it ( SoundControls::adopt )

http://calf.sourceforge.net/plugins/Monosynth . Research: calf_monosynth_mod (+ its engine-symbols.txt ). Fact What ravving does two envelopes: EG1 → cutoff ( env2cutoff , default 8000 cents), EG2 → amp ( adsr2_amp = 1) LENGTH drives adsr2_r ; adsr2_s 1 (a held note sustains); ENV is env2cutoff 0 … 4800 cents logarithmic ports: cutoff, every EG time, portamento, LFO rates CUTOFF 300 … 9000 Hz, GLIDE 1 … 400 ms, LENGTH 10 … 3000 ms with "curve": "log" o1_wave 16 waves: 0 Sawtooth, 1 Square, 3 Sine, 4 Triangle… WAVE: SAW, SQR, SIN, TRI; o12_mix 0 (osc 1 only) legato 0 Retrig, 1 Legato, 2/3 finger modes; pbend_range up to 2400 cents legato 1 (overlapping notes glide), pbend_range 1200 one LFO1 drives lfo2pitch and lfo2filter vibrato only: lfo_rate 5.5 Hz, lfo2pitch played by the ribbon (expression vibrato , 0 … 60 cents) master 0..1 (Zynthbox's wrapper pins it; ravving's jalv does not) master 0.3

FluidSynth 2.4.4 (a process, not an LV2), one per drum machine with its kit's soundfont. Research: fluidsynth2_mod . Fact What ravving does level CCs (7, 11) and velocity attenuate as 40·log10(v/127) dB, twice the usual law row levels go through velocity (level 0.8 → velocity 100 ≈ −4 dB; accent ×1.27 → 127) reverb / chorus CCs are sends of at most 20 %; the effects' settings have no CC none sent: with FluidSynth's own reverb and chorus on or off, a snare's tail is silent either way (CC 91 stays 0 and the 909 kit sends none): the drums carry no hidden reverb started like zynthbox-qml: -g 1 , synth.polyphony=64 , MMA bank select the same command line The drums' SOUND MODIFIERS are the kit's own (engines.json's kitSound , EngineProfiles::resolveKit): TONE (CUTOFF, RESO), SHAPE (ATTACK, LENGTH: the release) and PITCH (TUNE in semitones, FINE in cents), SF2 generator offsets sent as NRPNs like the soundfont sources' MODS. A kit is one soundfont on one channel, so they act on the whole kit; per drum would need a channel per row. Acoustic kits inside a General MIDI font (kits.json presetKits , the picker's ACOUSTIC group): a kit's path may name one preset of a soundfont, <file>#<bank>:<program> , and after it choose a row's key, ?CYMBAL=51&HAT=44 . FluidR3's kits sit at bank 128 (Jazz 32, Brush 40, Standard 0, Room 8) and keep the General MIDI map, so a key whose sample name says nothing ("Md Studio", its toms) takes its GM role. "Jazz · ride" and "Brush · ride" put the ride (51) on CYMBAL and the hi-hat foot (44) on HAT (shown as PEDAL); the plain "Jazz · crash" keeps the crash, for breaks. FluidSynth gets the file and the bank and program; the path with its choices is what a project saves.

libzynthbox's own sampler: no process, clips (ClipAudioSource) played in the audio thread. Facts from libzynthbox's source ( SamplerSynthVoice.cpp , ClipAudioSourceSliceSettings.cpp , AudioLevels.cpp ). Fact What ravving does a slice's envelope defaults to {attack 0, decay 0, sustain 1, release 0} only the release is set (8 ms, the choke's fade) a stock libzynthbox fades every voice in over ~165 ms (started at gain 0, ramped 0.0001 a frame) needs a patched libzynthbox (a voice starts at its gain; only aftertouch changes ramp) a one-shot retriggered on the same clip and slice stops its previous voice ( SamplerSynthVoice.cpp:392 ) the slots choke themselves; no exclusivityGroup needed one-shots cannot play backwards (only loops and granular do) REVERSE plays a reversed copy of the file a track's channel_N-sampleM ports exist only while a clip is registered on that slot wired per loaded slot ( setSampleOutputs ) ClipAudioSource::play(…, velocity) : 64 is unity gain previews play at 64 on the global lane AudioLevels' track gain (a machine's VOL) runs −40…+20 dB, 0 at gainAbsolute 0.667; the lane's sends leave before it the sends are scaled by VOL's gain in ravving ( TrackEffects::setSendLevel )

h: The audio input (HiFiBerry DAC+ADC Pro, PCM1863)
t: Fact What ravving does the five jacks, left to right: 1 headphones, 2–3 line outputs (speaker icon), 4–5 inputs (mic icon); jack 4 is the left channel (ADC input VINL1), jack 5 the right MIC and GUITAR record the jack with the signal ( activeJack : picked between takes when one jack is 10 dB over the other and above −45 dBFS; mixing both added the empty input's noise, audibly), so either jack works; LINE is stereo; INPUT lights each jack's level (AudioLevels' capture meter, rewired to the real inputs); monitor on headphones in jack 1 the HiFiBerry's JACK capture ports are named like a Dummy card's, and which gets the serial suffix changes between boots found by the card each start ( InputPorts ) input noise is mostly the room around the cables (a ground loop through a USB-Ethernet link to a charging laptop is the usual suspect); screen brightness, mic bias, one or two ADC inputs make no difference — the ADC's input mux is ADC Left/Right Input ; ADC … Capture Source does not change what is heard the selection is left as Zynthbox sets it PGA −12…+40 dB in 0.5 dB steps ( PGA Gain Left/Right ), mic bias on/off; Zynthbox selects VINL2 + VINL1 MIC +30 dB with bias, GUITAR +10 dB (a strummed electric peaked −5 dBFS at +18), LINE 0 dB; the selection left as Zynthbox sets it the open input's noise is −69 dBFS at +30 dB a take under −50 dBFS is refused, not normalised into noise input → monitor ≈ 11–16 ms (256 frames at 48 kHz); the capture node follows the output's clock (no resampling) MONITOR through track 9's lane with its own LEVEL

Ports from lv2info on the device; the chains are in the presets file. A silent mic at +40 dB PGA picks up noise in bursts, mostly under 300 Hz: CLEAN cuts it with a 24 dB/octave high-pass and a gate. Plugin Facts the presets rely on Calf Compressor stereo; threshold is linear (0.06 ≈ −24 dBFS), ratio 1–20, attack / release ms, makeup 1–64 (×) Calf Saturator stereo; drive 0.1–10, blend −10…10, mix 0–1, pre/post high- and low-pass in Hz Calf Multi Chorus stereo; amount (wet) and dry 0–4, voices 1–8, mod_rate Hz, mod_depth ms Calf Vintage Delay stereo; timing 0 = BPM (from the bpm port), subdiv 4 with time_l / time_r 3/4 = a dotted eighth / a quarter; amount (wet) 0–4, feedback , medium 1 = tape Calf Ring Modulator stereo; mod_freq 1–20000 Hz (20–600 for a robot), mod_amount 0–1, mod_mode 0 = sine Calf Filter stereo; mode 4 = 24 dB/octave high-pass, 7 = 12 dB band-pass; freq Hz, res 0.707–32 Calf Gate stereo; threshold linear (0.01 = −40 dBFS), range the most it closes (0.03 = −30 dB), ratio , attack / release ms Dragonfly Plate stereo; dry_level and its wet level (the port is named early_level ) 0–100, decay s, predelay ms, low_cut / high_cut Hz MaPitchshift (DISTRHO) mono in , two outs; ratio 0.25–4 (0.5 = an octave down), window ms, blur ; no dry mix SwankyAmp stereo, its own cabinet ( cabonoff ); every port 0–1 ( preampdrive , powerampdrive , inputlevel , outputlevel …) A mono plugin in the chain takes both sides summed and feeds both sides of what follows ( JackWiring::setInputChain ). Each plugin of a chain is a jalv process of its own, about 1–2 % CPU each.

Calf Saturator (DRIVE), Calf Crusher (CRUSH), Calf Phaser (PHASER), Dragonfly Room (REVERB), TAP Echo (DELAY) have no mods; their ports come from lv2info and were calibrated by measurement ( tools/lv2probe.sh , see debugging.md ). The beat repeat (STUTTER, LOOP) is ravving's own JACK client.

What ravving wires, how to look at it and how to measure it. The graph is PipeWire's, seen by libzynthbox and the engines through PipeWire's JACK library ( pw-jack ), the way zynthbox-qml runs. tools/graph-check.py (run with tools/device.sh graph … ) does the checks below in one go.

JackWiring (src/backend/jackwiring.*) asks libzynthbox's JackConnectionHandler for every link and retries until the ports exist (engines and passthroughs make their ports a moment after they are requested). Per machine (z: its Zynthian channel, t: its sketchpad track): ZLRouter:Zynthian-Channel{z} ─MIDI─> ravving-<key>-midi:midi_00 (FluidSynth) ravving-<key>:<lv2 midi in> (jalv) ravving-<key>:output_FL/FR ──> [DRIVE insert] ──> SynthPassthrough:Synth{z+1}-input{L,R} SynthPassthrough:Synth{z+1}-dryOut ──> TrackPassthrough:Channel{t+1}-lane1-input TrackPassthrough lane dryOut ──> AudioLevels:Channel{t+1} ──> GlobalPlayback:input TrackPassthrough lane wetOutFx1 ──> ravving-reverb ──> GlobalPlayback:input (send 1) TrackPassthrough lane wetOutFx2 ──> ravving-delay ──> GlobalPlayback:input (send 2) SamplerSynth:channel_{t+1}-sample{n} ──> the track's lane (the samplers' slots) SamplerSynth:global-sketch1 ──> GlobalPlayback:input (the metronome's ticks) GlobalPlayback:dryOut ──> ravving-repeat ──> ravving-crush ──> ravving-phaser (the master inserts: LIVE FX) ──> system:playback_1/2 (or ravving-out, a loopback, when the sound goes to Bluetooth / HDMI: [architecture.md](bluetooth.md)) jacks 4/5 (the HiFiBerry's capture, HardwarePorts) ──> [input inserts] ──> a track's lane (monitor) and / or AudioLevels:SystemRecorder (record); AudioLevels:SystemCapture meters the input The link PipeWire makes on its own from every new engine to the speakers is removed, as zynthbox-qml's autoconnect does, so all sound goes through its track (level, mute, FX). Clock: every JACK client (libzynthbox's nodes, jalv) runs at the graph's rate and period, 48000 / 256 on a Zynthbox. FluidSynth's audio goes through its PipeWire driver (a stream, so its node can run on its own clock): ravving tells it the graph's rate and period ( AudioGraph , read once through a throwaway JACK client) so it is not resampled.

ravving never trusts a hardware port's JACK name: pipewire-jack names a device's ports after its node's description, or system: for the default device, and two cards sharing a description take turns at the plain name and a -<serial> one from one start of PipeWire to the next. On a Zynthbox the kernel's snd-dummy and the HiFiBerry are both "Built-in Audio Stereo", so a name alone can point the input at the silent Dummy. The device: data/wireplumber/50-ravving-hardware.conf hides the Dummy from PipeWire, so the HiFiBerry is the only "Built-in Audio Stereo", and (by its priority, 10000 against 1000) the system: device, on every start. libzynthbox and zynthbox-qml wire that name too. ravving: HardwarePorts finds a card's ports by the card. In pw-dump each port's port.alias is " : " (kits.json input.portsCard ), and its JACK name is the JACK port whose UUID carries that port's object serial (pipewire-jack makes a port's UUID as (1 << 32) | (serial + 1) ). The input ( captureOf ) and the speakers ( playbackOf , JackWiring::setSpeakers ) are found that way at start; the input again each time it is armed (the RECORDER or INPUT opening). Seeing it: pw-jack jack_lsp -U (the UUIDs) against pw-dump (the serials and aliases); the journal says ravving: input ports … and ravving: speakers … .

Tool What it shows Use pw-top -b -n 2 every node: driver (no + ) or follower, QUANT/RATE it runs at, WAIT/BUSY per cycle, W/Q B/Q (fractions of the period), ERR (xruns), format the first thing to look at; tools/graph-check.py parses it pw-dump the whole graph as JSON: nodes with props ( node.rate , node.latency , api.alsa.* ), ports, links, devices with profiles scripting; pw-dump ID for one object pw-dot + dot -Tpng the graph as a picture pw-dot -o /tmp/g.dot; dot -Tpng /tmp/g.dot > g.png (graphviz on the laptop) pw-link -l / -o / -i links by PipeWire names (the only names some nodes have: the loopback's inputs) pw-link A:out B:in , pw-link -d to remove pw-jack jack_lsp -c / -l JACK names with connections / latency ranges ravving's and libzynthbox's names pw-mon events as they happen (nodes, links, params) watching an engine start or a link appear pw-metadata -n settings 0 the defaults ( clock.quantum 1024, clock.rate ) and forced values NOT the running clock: that is the driver row in pw-top pw-cli info ID one node's params (Props: channelVolumes…) volumes, formats wpctl status / inspect / set-profile WirePlumber's view: devices, profiles, defaults the sound card's profile (below) pw-jack jack_iodelay round-trip latency through a cable from an output jack to an input jack the only true end-to-end audio latency measurement pw-jack jack_midi_latency_test MIDI round trip through a loopback (a cable between a MIDI out and in, or a2j's Midi Through) MIDI path latency and jitter pw-jack jack_bufsize / jack_cpu_load the period, the DSP load JACK sees tools/mididump.py the MIDI an engine really receives on a port silent-engine investigations tools/meter.py RMS on any ports is sound passing a link tools/graph-check.py rates/periods vs the graph, xrun deltas, linked-but-idle nodes, the ravving links the routine check

rates : every audio node's rate and period against the running driver's. A node at another rate is resampled; a node with a larger period is buffered by that much. idle : nodes with links that are not running: a link that passes no data looks like this (an engine linked while still registering: re-make the link). xruns -s N : each node's ERR counter now and N seconds later. Compare idle vs playing, and before vs after a change. links ravving : what is linked, grouped by output port, to check against the map above.

FluidSynth is started with -r <graph rate> -o audio.period-size=<period> -o audio.periods=2 : its node runs at the graph's rate, not resampled, buffered by two periods (48000 / 512, 10.7 ms). The ring is what keeps a busy engine from starving the graph. Thread priorities ( graph-check.py threads ): PipeWire's data loops run FIFO 88 (daemon) and 83 (clients: libzynthbox's, jalv's, FluidSynth's); FluidSynth's own render thread ( fluid_pipewire ) is not realtime (its audio.realtime-prio 60 covers the synth thread only), jalv's main thread is not (it has no audio work); libzynthbox's SyncTimerThread runs FIFO 99 while the transport has run. RAVVING_GDB=1 runs ravving under gdb -batch , which stops the whole process at every fork and thread start or exit: the graph then counts 20 to 40 xruns a minute. It is for crash hunts only: systemctl --user unset-environment RAVVING_GDB and a restart for a device that is used; tools/device.sh deploy says so when it finds it set. The same applies to any debugger or profiler attached to zynthbox-qml. With nothing attached the graph has room to spare: a full project playing runs with 0 xruns, the busiest node (TrackPassthrough) at about 6 % of the period.

Sequenced notes: libzynthbox's SyncTimer schedules them on the JACK frame clock and ZLRouter puts each machine's on ZLRouter:Zynthian-Channel{z} , linked to the engine's MIDI input (above). tools/mididump.py PORT SECONDS prints what a port carries. External keyboards: MidiRouter's hardware pass-through ( MidiInput , port 3) feeds the LIVE machine; raw notes reach no engine on their own (the current sketchpad track is parked at 9). Midi Through arrives twice, through a2j and through PipeWire's Midi-Bridge, so copies closer than 4 ms are dropped ( architecture.md ). Bluetooth MIDI: bluez_midi.server is PipeWire's BLE MIDI node, idle unless a BLE MIDI device connects. Latency: a MIDI round trip is measured with pw-jack jack_midi_latency_test between a hardware MIDI out and in joined by a cable (or a2j 's Midi Through for the software path alone); an audio round trip with pw-jack jack_iodelay and a cable from an output jack into input jack 4 or 5.

The sound card's playback node is the driver ( priority.driver 10000 from /etc/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/99-default-soundcard.conf ). It stays the driver whatever output is picked: with the sound routed to Bluetooth / HDMI the master's links to the jacks stay in place and the jacks are muted, since an unlinked playback node suspends and another node (the card's capture, or the Bluetooth transport) would become the clock.

ravving speaks English, Spanish and Japanese. Every text on its screen goes through KI18n , KDE's gettext layer, and the webpage (site/) is translated from catalogs of its own. The docs stay in English. Language App catalog Webpage catalog Spanish (es) po/es/ravving.po po-site/es/ravving-site.po Japanese (ja) po/ja/ravving.po po-site/ja/ravving-site.po

The domain. Localization (src/backend/localization.cpp) sets the application domain ravving right after the QGuiApplication is made, as the KI18n guide asks, and adds the build tree's locale/ folder so a build runs translated before it is installed. The installed catalogs are /usr/share/locale/<lang>/LC_MESSAGES/ravving.mo (CMake's ki18n_install(po) ; the AppImage's default-app.sh install copies them too).
QML. KLocalization::setupLocalizedContext(&engine) (KF 6.8 and later) puts i18n , i18nc , i18np and i18ncp on the root context, so QML calls them bare.
SETTINGS · LANGUAGE. SYSTEM (the default) follows the device's own language; English, Español and 日本語 pick one. The choice is kept in the profile settings ( ui/language ).

Live switching. A change sets KLocalizedString::setLanguages , sends QEvent::LanguageChange to the application and calls QQmlEngine::retranslate() : every binding that calls i18n… is evaluated again, so the screen changes at once. C++ models whose rows carry display text (the video tiers, FILES, the USB page, the audio outputs) catch the LanguageChange event, as the Qt guide does for plain QObjects, and emit their NOTIFY.

h: How it works › Numbers and dates
t: Numbers and dates. C++ formats them through KI18n ( subs(value, 0, 'f', 1) ); QML uses Rave.num(value, decimals) , the locale of the language picked. Dates use QLocale of the first language KI18n uses.

Only display text is translated. A text that is stored, compared, sent or looked up stays English: the machine roles, preset and kit names, scale names, group names, the effect and knob names in data/engines.json, the menu ids, the fifo names, the CUIA names. The display is translated where it is drawn. QML: Rave.kli18nc(context, key) marks a key for extraction and returns it unchanged (the QML side of KI18n's kli18nc , as Qt's QT_TR_NOOP ). The helpers translate at draw time: Rave.group , Rave.drumRow , Rave.param , Rave.paramGroup , Rave.effect , Rave.choice , Rave.tuning , Rave.stringInstrument , Rave.inputMode . Menus dispatch by id , never by the text shown. C++: tables of display text are KLazyLocalizedString ( kli18nc ), turned into text with .toString() when read, so a language change shows at once. A message with values is a KLocalizedString template ( ki18nc(…).subs(…) ) passed on and finished where it is shown. List models carry a display role beside the key, as Qt's QAbstractListModel examples do: the key for the logic, the display text for the screen.

Data. tools/i18n-data.py writes the vocabulary of the data files (drum rows, the engines' knobs and cards, effects, scales, tunings, groups) as i18nc calls into the extraction, as KDE's rc.cpp does, under the same contexts the helpers use.

Every call is i18nc with a context saying what the text is, starting with a KDE UI marker: @action:button , @option:check , @option:radio , @label , @title:window , @title:group , @item:inlistbox , @info , @info:status , @info:placeholder . The context names the music meaning when a word has several ("SONG" the page, "SONG" the PLAY mode). All sound vocabulary shares one context, so a knob name is translated once. Names printed on the device stay English in every language: MENU, ALT, MODE, BACK, SELECT, PLAY, STOP, RECORD, X, Y. So do product and machine names (SAMPLE KING, PAD SAMPLER, POLY-6, the engines and kits), MIDI, USB, HDMI, SBC-XQ and LIVE FX. tools/check-ui.py 's text-translatable rule finds a display text that skips i18n… ; its keep list holds these.

The translations use the words musicians and producers use in each language. English Spanish Japanese DRUMS BATERÍA ドラム BASS BAJO ベース CHORDS ACORDES コード LEAD LEAD リード SAMPLER SAMPLER サンプラー PADS PADS パッド SONG CANCIÓN ソング SECTION SECCIÓN セクション PATTERN PATRÓN パターン PRESET PRESET プリセット KICK / SNARE BOMBO / CAJA キック / スネア SCALE / ROOT ESCALA / TÓNICA スケール / ルート BAR / STEP COMPÁS / PASO 小節 / ステップ LIVE REC REC EN VIVO ライブ録音 RECORDER GRABADORA レコーダー TRACK PISTA トラック SETTINGS AJUSTES 設定 knob / big knob perilla / perilla grande ノブ / 大ノブ Japanese uses katakana for the studio words (ドラム, リバーブ, スケール) and kanji for plain ones (保存, 削除, 設定). Spanish has two plural forms, Japanese one.

Spanish runs about a third longer than English. ActionButton and Chip shrink their text to fit, down to 75 % of its size; a text still too long is elided. Look at every page in Spanish after adding text.

sh tools/i18n-extract.sh # sources → po/ravving.pot and po-site/ravving-site.pot, merged into every catalog # translate what it marked: empty or fuzzy entries (Lokalize, Poedit or a text editor) python3 tools/check-translations.py # the ctest translations-current python3 tools/site-i18n.py render # po-site → site/es/ and site/ja/ check-translations.py fails when a template is stale, a catalog does not compile ( msgfmt --check ), a text is untranslated or fuzzy, a translation drops a placeholder ( %1 ) or a markup tag ( <b> , <a> ), or the rendered pages are older than their catalogs.

tools/site-i18n.py extract collects every block of text in site/index.html (a heading, a paragraph, a row's words, with their inline , and
), the alt , title and aria-label attributes, and site.js's captions and marks, into po-site/ravving-site.pot. render writes site/ /index.html and site.js with the links pointing one folder up; the language switcher in the page's top bar links the three. , and anything marked translate="no" stay as they are. The page's catalogs live in po-site/, not po/, because ki18n_install compiles every catalog in po/ into the device's install.

msginit --no-translator --no-wrap -l <lang> -i po/ravving.pot -o po/<lang>/ravving.po , and the same from po-site/ravving-site.pot into po-site/ /ravving-site.po. Translate both, following the glossary above (add a column for the new language). Add the language to the Languages table in src/backend/localization.cpp, by its own name. Add its link to the switcher in site/index.html and its hreflang alternate. Run the workflow, then look at every page in the new language on the device.

Before every release, someone who reads the language reviews what changed in each catalog since the last release: new and changed texts, and the screens they appear on. Run git diff v<last> -- po po-site , take the screenshot tour in each language, and check that ctest -R translations-current passes. A release does not ship with fuzzy or untranslated texts.

ravving's screens share one look: machines with side rails and a face in their own finish, controls grouped on strips, work areas recessed in wells, a dark header band on top. These rules keep every new screen in it. tools/check-ui.py checks them over the QML (a laptop test, ctest -R ui-rules , and tools/static-analysis.sh ui ); tools/ui-rules.json holds the rules and their exceptions, and is where a new rule goes.

Use the component; never redraw it. What Component Where it is A page's body: the rails and the face in its finish Chassis every page ( MachineModule wears it for the machines) The top band of controls (row 1: transport, plate, ✕; row 2: the deck) PageHeader the dashboard ( RaveHeader ), every full-window page The recessed display in a header's first row HeaderPlate the project name, the track playing, the take A row of buttons on its grouping strip ToolStrip the pattern toolbars, the SONG rows, the player's and the RECORDER's groups A recessed panel for a work area Well the RECORDER's input, tuner, effects, the lists An action ActionButton everywhere (squared, the standard height) An action that cannot be undone (asks twice) ConfirmButton DELETE, REMOVE, CLEAR SONG, FORMAT, EJECT A state (on/off with an LED, or one of a set) Chip / StripButton modes, tabs, banks, sorts The way out CloseButton (the ✕) every dialog (DialogHeader) and every full page An empty list or view EmptyNote every list and grid A dialog's title row DialogHeader every dialog The way a file leaves the device: a SEND… button opening the destinations (USB sticks, the computer, the phone by QR code) SendPopup ( QrPopup for the phone) the FILES browser (every kind), VIDEO SAVED, the music player's tracks, the presets dialog, the sound picker

Squared ActionButton : it does something once and leaves no state. LOAD, CLEAR, SAVE, RENAME, NEW, −/+, ◀ ▶, PLAY FROM HERE, TRIM, TO PADS, the transport keys, a picker showing its current value (it opens a list). Rounded Chip / StripButton : a state you can see. An on/off toggle wears its LED (SET, STEP, LIVE, S/M, MONITOR, REPEAT); one choice out of a set wears none (BANK A–D, the views, SORT, the input tabs, KEEP TAKES IN). It stays lit while the state is on, so it always binds checked (or is checkable). Checked: chip-shows-state . ConfirmButton for what cannot be undone: the first tap arms it (AGAIN? and a countdown bar), a second one within three seconds does it. All of them at the standard size (see Button sizes). Checked: actions-are-actionbuttons (no bare QQC.Button ).
