One height: Rave.controlHeight (36 px) for every button, action or state, so a row of them lines up and a finger always finds the same target on the 1280×800 touch screen. A smallest width: Rave.controlWidth (48 px, square) for a glyph (◀ ▶ − + ⟳ ✕) and Rave.actionMinWidth (88 px) for a word (LOAD, SCAN, SAVE): a short word is no smaller a target than a long one. A longer label grows past it. ActionButton applies both on its own ( minimumWidth ); a button may ask for more (the dialogs' main action, SAVE at 150, SCAN at 130 so SCANNING… does not shift the row), never for less. A row that wants bigger buttons sizes them all from one property (the SONG page's rowButtonHeight , wordButtonWidth ), never with numbers on each button. Checked: button-standard-size (no number under the standard on a button's height or width).

h: Controls in a group take the device knobs
t: Dials, switches (WaveCycler) and sliders that sit together are a KnobGroup with them as its targets : the group takes the focus (a tap on it, ◀ ▶ between groups), the device's three small knobs then drive its controls in order (the big knob, one more), and each control wears its KnobBadge (1, 2, 3) saying which knob moves it, with the pick-up diamond on the fixed-pot kit. A group shows its frame while it has the knobs. ParamCard (the MODS and SOUND EFFECTS cards) and the header's TEMPO, FX SENDS and MASTER are the model. So nothing a finger can turn is out of reach of the hardware, and the badges say which knob is which without a manual. Checked: grouped-controls-take-knobs (a file with dials, switches or sliders and no KnobGroup).

h: Rows of controls sit on bands (dialogs and pages)
t: A page's or a dialog's row of controls sits on one ToolStrip , the darker rounded band a pattern toolbar is (the preset, OCT, undo / redo on one band): one row, one continuous band , never split into a band per group. The groups in it (a GroupLabel first, then its chips) are told apart by the space between them, as the toolbar's are. In the presets and sounds dialogs (ChoicePopup): SOURCE at the left and LOAD at the right share their row's band; GROUP and SORT share theirs (the groups wrap in what SORT leaves them, SORT keeps the top right). A row of one group hugs it (SAVE PATTERN AS's KEEP, NamePopup's options under optionsLabel ). A page's toolbar rows too: the SONG page's top bar (its title, SWITCH, PLAYS), its section and song rows, the pattern toolbars. So a dialog reads in rows and groups at a glance, as a page does, and a wrapping row never leaves a lone chip on a line of its own. Checked: dialog-groups-on-bands (a GroupLabel in a *Popup.qml outside a ToolStrip); one band per row is the reviewer's to see.

One ✕, the CloseButton , everywhere. A dialog gets it from DialogHeader ; a full page puts it at the end of its header's first row. Checked: close-is-closebutton . A view under the header has no ✕ (the SONG page, the MIXER): the header stays on screen, and the control that opened the view closes it (the project plate, ✱), as BACK does. No CLOSE / CANCEL / DONE buttons: the ✕ and BACK already leave. A button that stops work under way (CANCEL an export) is an action, and a question's answers (NO / YES while pairing) are answers; both are listed as exceptions. Checked: no-close-text .

Every page wears a Chassis in its own finish. Checked: page-wears-chassis . A page that takes the whole window (MUSIC PLAYER, RECORDER) has a PageHeader like the dashboard's: row 1 its transport, a HeaderPlate saying what is on, its own toggles, the ✕; row 2 its deck of grouped controls ( ToolStrip s). The view sits under it on the Chassis . Checked: full-page-has-header . Its controls go on ToolStrip s by group, its work areas in Well s.
An empty list or view says why and what fills it, with an EmptyNote ("no recordings yet · ● REC records the input as played"), never a Text of its own. Checked: empty-says-why .

Every page has a finish of its own in Rave.qml ( Rave.machines , songFinish , playerFinish , recorderFinishes ): chassisTop , chassisBottom , rail , well , ink , dim , accent , glow , dark . A new one:

h: Palettes › Starts from a researched palette, not a guess
t: Starts from a researched palette, not a guess. Pick its family from a reference palette set (the Radix / Tailwind / Material colour scales, Adobe Color's or Coolors' tested schemes, or a brand's own): a dark chassis from the scale's 950–900 steps, its well one step darker, the rail a mid step of the same hue, the ink from the scale's 50 step, the dim from 400, the accent the family's 400–500 (or its complement for contrast), the glow a lighter step of the accent. Is readable (WCAG 2.x contrast), against both chassis colours: ink ≥ 7:1 (AAA body text), dim ≥ 4.5:1 (AA text), accent ≥ 3:1 (AA for non-text) on the chassis or the well it lights in. Checked: palette-readable (the ratios are printed when it fails). Is distinct from the pages beside it: the player is violet, the RECORDER's inputs wine, amber and teal, the SONG page a matte slate night.

h: Text is translatable, keys are not
t: Every text a screen shows goes through i18nc with a context (docs/translations.md); a key that is stored or compared stays English and is translated where it is drawn (the Rave display helpers, Rave.kli18nc to mark it). The device's printed key names and the product names stay as printed. Translations run longer (Spanish about a third): ActionButton and Chip shrink their text to fit, down to 75 %, so give words room and look at every new screen in Spanish. Checked as text-translatable : a text: given a literal string without i18n… , outside the keep list in tools/ui-rules.json.

Write it here, under its heading, with why. Add it to tools/ui-rules.json : a pattern (a regex no QML may match) or a check (a function in tools/check-ui.py , registered in CHECKS ), with the files allowed to break it and why. A known breach still to fix is allowed with "migrate": true : it shows as a warning, and the list only ever shrinks. Run python3 tools/check-ui.py --verbose ; fix what it finds or list it.

The recipes for growing ravving. Read architecture.md first for the layers; this is the how-to. The code rules hold throughout: reuse a part before writing a new one, keep each class to one job, and give every public API its QDoc block in the .cpp ( writing-code-docs.md ) and every non-obvious line an inline comment that says why.

The drums and the bass share everything except what is specific to them. A new machine (CHORDS, LEAD, SAMPLER) follows the same path. Backend: a Machine subclass ( src/backend/machine.h ). It inherits the pattern, bars, presets, level/pan/pause/mute, effects, LIVE play and STEP entry. Implement: - onAttached() : write the machine's own state into its libzynthbox pattern; - refresh() : publish the bar on screen to QML (its own Q_PROPERTYs + stepsChanged ); - revoice() : rewrite every step's velocity (mute/solo/kick modes changed); - clearOwnSteps() , applyChart(chart) , chart() : its preset format (a chart is a map of strings, one character per step, so preset files stay readable); - placeHit(position, key, accented) , liveNotes(key) , liveVelocity(key, accented) : what a live key writes and plays (a list of notes: one for a row or a mono note, a whole chord for ChordMachine); - state() : everything it keeps (call Machine::state() and add to it: its steps, kit, sound…); a project file is exactly this, so it must be complete; - restoreContent(state) : take that back while running (opening a project) and write the pattern; an empty state means its defaults (the default preset, kit, sound). Call it from the constructor too, so start-up and opening share one path (MonoMachine and ChordMachine do). A missing key means "default", a present but empty one means "empty" (a cleared pattern stays cleared). Write steps through addSubnote / setSubnoteMetadata (velocity −1 = silent, duration in pattern ticks via stepTicks() ), and call markEdited() after a user change. Data: an entry in kits.json's machines ( key , kind , track , zynthianChannel , engine , sound , presets , defaultPreset , baseNote …; tracks and channels must be unused) and a presets file ( data/<machine>-presets.json , {presets: [{name, genre, chart}]} ), installed by CMakeLists.txt. A new instance of an existing kind (another mono synth) needs nothing else on the C++ side. Studio ( studio.cpp , loadKits() ): a new kind is one more kind == branch creating it; addMachine() then wires saving, ❚❚, the track lane, sends, the engine, DRIVE, SOUND MODIFIERS and expressions generically ( attachMachine() ), and it appears as studio.machines.<key> . QML: a MachinePanel subclass (see MonoMachinePanel.qml , ChordMachinePanel.qml ): the toolbar and editor as children, and the overrides MachinePanel declares: stepLeds , liveKeyDown/Up (what pads do while LIVE), stepKey , moveSelection(dy) (▲ ▼ in the editor; false at the edge), keyForNote / padForKey (what a keyboard note plays and which pad lights). Light live notes from heldKeys . QML: the page : a MachinePage declaring its panel (see pages/ChordsPage.qml ); it forwards the device and an external keyboard to it. Add the C++ files to src/backend/CMakeLists.txt and the QML files to src/CMakeLists.txt ( RAVVING_QML_FILES ), a screenshot step in src/main.cpp , and the machine to Rave.machines (finish colours: strings).

Engines are SoundEngine subclasses ( soundengine.h ): start() , reconfigure(config) , midiInputPort() , audioOutputPorts() (left, right), optional setControl(symbol, value) , and the started signal. SoundEngine::createEngine() picks one by the type of the kits.json engine object: "jalv" ( JalvEngine ): any LV2 instrument , e.g. {"type": "jalv", "uri": "http://distrho.sf.net/plugins/Nekobi", "controls": {"volume": 75}} . Ports and control indexes come from lv2info (cached per URI); a mono output is sent to both sides. Nothing else is needed for a new LV2 synth. "fluidsynth" ( FluidSynthEngine ): soundfonts (the drum kits). A new kind (setBfree, sfizz, a sampler…) is one more subclass run through ConsoleProcess (libzynthbox's ProcessWrapper: restarted on a crash, startup commands, a console prompt) and one more type in createEngine() . Choose an engine by measuring it first ( debugging.md : synthprobe/analyse): velocity response, glide, CPU ( top ), level.

h: SOUND MODIFIERS: an engine's own controls
t: A machine's SOUND MODIFIERS are data: its sound in kits.json, which Machine turns into a SoundControls ( machine.sound ). Cards of knobs, each driving an engine port by its LV2 symbol, a 0..1 knob mapped onto min..max (linearly, or "curve": "log" for ports the engine treats as logarithmic), with a 0..1 default: "sound": [ { "title": "FILTER", "knobs": [ { "name": "CUTOFF", "symbol": "cutoff", "min": 300, "max": 9000, "curve": "log", "default": 0.55 } ] }, { "title": "TONE", "knobs": [ { "name": "WAVE", "default": 0, "choices": [ { "label": "SAW", "controls": { "osc1waveform": 0, "osc1pw": 0.5 } }, { "label": "JUNO", "controls": { "osc1waveform": 0.5, "osc1pw": 0.75 } } ] } ] } ] A knob with choices is a switch (its value snaps to choice i of n at i / (n − 1)) and shows as a WaveCycler (SAW, SQR, TRI, SIN are drawn); each choice sets its controls (several ports; give every choice the same ports) or a value for the knob's symbol . Ports with no knob go in engine.controls . A live control a page plays (the ribbon's vibrato) is an expression : "expressions": {"vibrato": {"symbol": "lfo2pitch", "max": 60}} , played with machine.setExpression("vibrato", amount) .

h: SOUND MODIFIERS: an engine's own controls › Get the ports right from the mods
t: Get the ports right from the mods. Every engine Zynthbox ships has an engine mod whose docs/RESEARCH.md decodes its ports from the engine's own source: which are logarithmic, how enums quantise (TAL: i / den , rounded, 1-based), which envelope drives what (Calf: EG1 → cutoff, EG2 → amp), what a port called volume really does. Read it before writing a machine's engine.controls and sound , and record what ravving relies on in engines.md . Studio connects the controls to the engine and sends them all whenever it (re)starts; values are saved with the machine. Read a plugin's port ranges with lv2info and check what its numbers mean in its source: an LV2 range is not always the unit its own GUI shows.

On the track lane (EQ, COMPRESSOR, SIDECHAIN, PAN): an entry in EffectChain::effects() (name, knobs, defaults, shared or per machine) and its mapping in TrackEffects::apply() onto the JackPassthrough lane's properties. An insert (DRIVE): a JalvPlugin per machine created in Studio::attachMachine() , given to TrackEffects (which maps the knobs onto its controls and starts it on first use) and to JackWiring::addSynth(…, insert) ; TrackEffects::driveSwitched → JackWiring::setInsertActive() moves it into the path only while on, so the dry sound never depends on the extra process. Calibrate its gain staging with lv2probe.sh . A send (REVERB, DELAY): one shared JalvPlugin in GlobalEffects , fed from every lane's wet outputs ( JackWiring::addSends ) and returned with addEffectReturn . On the master (LIVE FX: CRUSH, PHASER, STUTTER/LOOP): LiveFx and JackWiring::setMasterInserts , which takes any AudioInsert . Your own DSP (BeatRepeat): an AudioInsert subclass opening its own JACK client (libjack, linked through pkg-config; PipeWire's at run time). Keep the process callback lock-free: atomics from the GUI thread, buffers allocated in the constructor, no Qt calls. For musical timing, ZynthboxBridge::timerTickAtFrame(jack_frame_time()) gives the transport position sample-accurately.

Handle keys with the Hardware attached property (like Keys ); an unaccepted event bubbles to the parent. See architecture.md for the signal list. A machine's vertical order (strip → SOUND MODIFIERS → editor → SOUND EFFECTS) lives in MachineModule : pages only call focusUp() / focusDown() at their editor's edge. Knob-driven controls go in a KnobGroup (targets need value , from , to , knobStep , fineStep , knobBadge , knobPending : RaveKnob , RaveFader , WaveCycler have them). Menus: RaveComboBox (drop-downs) and ChoicePopup (grids: kits, presets) already take the arrows, the big knob, SELECT and BACK, and hand the focus back on close.

Build clean (no warnings), run the desktop screenshots (no QML warnings), deploy, check on the device (screenshot + measurement), update the docs this change touches (and the page's features or shortcuts), rebuild the site's pages, then commit. A gotcha met on the way is written down for the maintainers, not in these docs. A change the user can undo goes through the project's history: see "The undo history" in architecture.md .

h: Reporting a problem to the issues center
t: Every component owns a check pass: at start, and whenever something fails or recovers, it tells the center ( src/backend/diagnostics.h ): #include "diagnostics.h" Issues::report(QStringLiteral("wiring"), QStringLiteral("sound"), QStringLiteral("warning"), QStringLiteral("Some audio connections are missing"), // the title, the user's words QStringLiteral("some ports never appeared…"), // the detail: what was seen QStringLiteral("Pick the sound again, or restart ravving."), // what to do QStringLiteral("restart")); // an action button, or "" Issues::clear(QStringLiteral("wiring")); // once it works again Rules: a stable id per problem (reporting it again updates and counts it); error when something does not work, warning when it works worse or will stop, notice for what is worth knowing (a desktop without device keys); always a suggestion the user can follow; clear it from the same place that would see it recovered. A library's stderr line can become an issue through StderrWatch 's pattern table (src/stderrwatch.cpp). tools/issues-test.sh exercises the center over the fifo.

ravving's C++ (the app in src/ , the backend library in src/backend/ , the setup program in setup/ ) is documented with QDoc, Qt's own documentation tool, and published as the API reference beside these pages: site/api/ , generated by tools/build-api-docs.py . The QML in qml/ is not documented there yet: it moves into plugin base types first.

Document with QDoc. Every public C++ class, struct and namespace has a /*! ... */ block with \class ( \struct , \namespace ), \inmodule Ravving , its \ingroup and a \brief ; every Q_PROPERTY a \property block; every public method, slot, Q_INVOKABLE and signal a block; every public enum an \enum block with a \value for each value. Be concise, precise and technical about what the current code does : its inputs and outputs, units (dB or linear gain, milliseconds or seconds, steps or ticks, 0..1), ranges and clamping, the thread it runs on (GUI thread, audio thread, a worker), who owns what it hands out, its invariants and its side effects (what it saves, emits, starts). Never write history or AI-style context , in a QDoc block or in any // comment: no used to , was changed , previously , no longer , now X instead of Y , no dates ( found 2026-10-12 ), no the user asked , no story of a past bug or of why something was changed. A // comment inside the code is welcome only when it explains a non-obvious technical reason that is true of the code as it is ("muted rather than unlinked, so the jacks' sink keeps clocking the graph"). A measurement that justifies a constant is a fact and may stay, stated plainly ("30 %: the lowest still readable in a lit room"). Every new or changed C++ API comes with its QDoc in the same commit , and python3 tools/build-api-docs.py is run so site/api/ follows (it is committed, like site/docs/ ). ctest checks both (below).

The documentation lives in the .cpp files, next to the definitions, as Qt's own sources have it; the headers hold the declarations and short // notes on private members only. A block right before a function's definition documents that function. Parameters are named with \a , every one of them (QDoc warns about a missing one), and a function that returns something says so with "Returns". What has no definition in the .cpp (a signal, a pure virtual, an inline function in the header, a static constant) gets a block anywhere in the .cpp with \fn and the full signature (or \variable ). The class's own block, its \property , \enum and \fn blocks go together after the includes. When the definition's parameter names differ from the header's, start the block with the \fn signature as the header has it, so \a names what the reader sees. A header with no .cpp of its own ( audioinsert.h , zbcall.h , filesuffixes.h ) is documented in doc/src/header-only.qdoc ; the header says so in one line. Overrides of Qt's virtuals ( rowCount() , data() , paint() ) and of ravving's own base classes are \reimp , with a line on what this one adds when it adds something. /*! \class History \inmodule Ravving \ingroup ravving-studio \brief The project's undo history, published to QML as \c studio.history. Participants register once with add() and report each change with record(). ... */ /*! \property History::undoText \brief the name of the step undo() would undo; empty when there is none. */ /*! \fn void History::undone(const QString &what) Emitted after undo() went back over a step; \a what is its name. */ /*! Registers \a participant. Its state now is where its history starts. The participant must outlive the history or be removed with remove() first. */ void History::add(HistoryParticipant *participant) A property's \brief is a noun phrase that QDoc puts after "This property holds": "the name of...", "whether ...". The groups ( \ingroup ) are the areas of the reference's landing page: ravving-app , ravving-studio , ravving-machines , ravving-engines , ravving-audio , ravving-system , ravving-setup (defined in doc/src/index.qdoc ).

python3 tools/check-cpp-docs.py (ctest cpp-docs ) finds every public class, struct, namespace, property, method, signal, enum and free function the headers of src/ and setup/ declare and fails on any without a QDoc block (the READ, WRITE and NOTIFY members of a documented property, destructors and deleted functions are exempt). It also reads every comment of src/**/*.cpp|h and setup/ for history: dates, used to , previously , no longer , any more , was changed / replaced / removed , now X instead of Y , the user asked , found on ... , fixed in , regression and the like (the list is BANNED in the script). --rule api or --rule comments runs one rule; --list prints every entity with its state. python3 tools/check-docs-history.py (ctest docs-history ) applies the same list to the published docs (the pages tools/build-site-docs.py renders), outside code spans. python3 tools/build-api-docs.py --check (ctest api-docs-current ) generates the reference into a temporary folder and fails when QDoc printed a warning (an undocumented parameter, a link to nothing, an \fn that matches no declaration) or when site/api/ differs from it. It is skipped (exit 77) where no Qt 6 qdoc is installed, and when the committed pages were made by another qdoc version ( site/api/qdoc-version.txt ), whose output differs.

python3 tools/build-api-docs.py # site/api/, from doc/ravving.qdocconf python3 tools/build-api-docs.py --check # what ctest runs It needs Qt 6's qdoc (Arch: qt6-tools ; Debian: qdoc-qt6 ): $QDOC , else Qt 6's host bin or libexec folder ( qmake6 -query ), else qdoc6 or qdoc on the PATH, whichever reports a 6.x version ( /usr/bin/qdoc is Qt 5's on some systems). QDoc parses the headers with clang, so the include paths of Qt, KF6 (KI18n, BluezQt), JACK and the project are passed in a generated cxx-includes.qdocconf ; without them a class page loses its members silently. doc/ ravving.qdocconf the project: sources, headers, the include paths global/ravving.qdocconf shared settings (warnings, the template) global/html-ravving.qdocconf the page chrome: the webpage's top bar, the sidebar, the footer global/style/ravving.css the theme: site.css's tokens and fonts, a light and a dark mode global/ravving-api.js the theme switch, the sidebar (nav.js) and the search (search.js) src/index.qdoc the landing page and the class groups src/header-only.qdoc the header-only classes and functions The generator runs QDoc, wraps each documented member in a box (QDoc writes them as loose siblings), writes nav.js (the sidebar: the classes by area) and search.js (every class, property, function, signal and enum) from QDoc's index file, and copies the script beside the pages. The pages reach the webpage's fonts and wordmarks through ../assets/ , so site/api/ works on the public page and on the copy the device serves alike.

What ravving is made of, all taken from the device (nothing is bundled, by the AppImage either): ravving runs on the Zynthbox QtQuick Controls style ( qml-style-zynthbox , picked by name in main.cpp , so there is no build-time check: a missing style shows the Basic look and unthemed controls), and that style imports io.zynthbox.ui (ZUI, from qml-module-zynthbox : Button, CheckBox, Switch, Menu and TextField read their theme from it) and the KDE Frameworks it draws with (Kirigami, KSvg, Plasma). The audio engine comes from libzynthbox ( io.zynthbox.components ) and zyncoder , both loaded at run time. So the order is: libzynthbox + zyncoder, qml-module-zynthbox, qml-style-zynthbox, then ravving; on a stock Zynthbox they are the installed libzynthbox , qml-module-zynthbox and qml-style-zynthbox packages, and a rebuilt module or style must be installed before ravving is tried. The music player plays through Qt Multimedia ( qt6-multimedia-dev to build; libqt6multimedia6 with its FFmpeg plugin at run time, both on the image; its sound goes out through PulseAudio, so ravving's service wants pipewire-pulse.service , which a Zynthbox has but leaves off; the player's stream runs at its own adapted quantum and leaves the graph at 256 frames, 48 kHz), and the exports use TagLib ( libtag1-dev ), zlib and libsndfile with its FLAC, Vorbis and LAME encoders. The sound itself comes from programs and data the Zynthbox image ships, started and wired by ravving at run time and bundled by nothing: jalv (the LV2 host) with the LV2 plugins the machines and effects name by URI in data/kits.json and src/backend/ (TAL NoiseMaker, DISTRHO Nekobi, Calf Monosynth, Calf Crusher and Phaser, Dragonfly Room Reverb, TAP Echo; tools/lv2probe.sh checks a URI on the device), FluidSynth 2 for the drum kits and the soundfont sound sources, the soundfonts under /zynthian/zynthian-data/soundfonts (the SFZ Drum Machines kits, SF2 Instruments with FluidR3Mono_GM.sf3 and ACBass.sf3 ), and PipeWire's JACK ( pw-jack ) with Zynthbox's MIDI routing (ZLRouter, a2j). A machine whose plugin or soundfont is missing starts silent and says so in the journal; engines.md has what each engine does and expects.

On the device (Debian 13 arm64, as a Zynthbox image is) the build needs, by Debian name: For Packages the toolchain cmake , ninja-build , g++ , pkg-config Qt 6 (Core, Gui, Qml, Quick, QuickControls2, Concurrent, Network, DBus, Multimedia) qt6-base-dev , qt6-declarative-dev , qt6-multimedia-dev Bluetooth (KDE's BluezQt over BlueZ's D-Bus API) libkf6bluezqt-dev the audio processors and the graph probe (JACK's API; PipeWire's library at run time) libjack-jackd2-dev exports: the audio files, their tags, the .ravv bundles libsndfile1-dev , libtag-dev (TagLib 2; libtag1-dev on older images), zlib1g-dev the tools ( tools/*.py ) and syncing a checkout python3 , rsync Everything else ravving needs it finds at run time on a stock Zynthbox: libzynthbox and zyncoder, qml-module-zynthbox and qml-style-zynthbox with the KDE Frameworks they draw with (Kirigami, KSvg, Plasma), libqt6multimedia6 with its FFmpeg plugin, PipeWire with pipewire-jack ( pw-jack ), pipewire-bin ( pw-loopback , pw-link , pw-dump , pw-top ) and pipewire-pulse (left off by the image; ravving's service wants it), udisks2 and util-linux (USB sticks: udisksctl , lsblk ), jalv with the LV2 plugins and FluidSynth with the soundfonts named below. Bluetooth needs three packages the image lacks, bluez-obexd , libspa-0.2-bluetooth and libkf6bluezqt6 , plus two drop-ins ravving installs: tools/bluetooth-setup.sh does all of it ( packaging.md , "Bluetooth on a fresh device"). tools/device.sh deploy # from the laptop: sync, build, install, restart, wait # or by hand (rsync without -a: older laptop mtimes would make ninja skip changed files) rsync -rlp --checksum --exclude build --exclude .git ./ root@milo.local:/root/ravving/ ssh root@milo.local cd /root/ravving cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr cmake --build build && cmake --install build systemctl --user daemon-reload systemctl --user start ravving # try it once: stops zynthbox-qml (the services conflict) systemctl --user start zynthbox-qml # and back To make ravving the device's UI (it starts at boot, and zynthbox-qml is masked so nothing brings it back), and to return to stock Zynthbox with nothing of ravving left in systemd: /usr/share/ravving/default-app.sh ravving /usr/share/ravving/default-app.sh zynthbox # add --purge to uninstall ravving too /usr/share/ravving/default-app.sh status From the laptop, tools/device.sh default ravving|zynthbox|status does the same. default-app.sh run ravving|zynthbox switches for the session only (the boot default stays), which is what ravving's own menu offers under POWER → ZYNTHBOX.

The QML is compiled into the binary (the Ravving QML module: qmlcachegen bytecode and C++ for typed bindings), so a QML change is a rebuild like any other, and QML errors show at build time. To try QML on the device without rebuilding, copy the qml/ folder over and start ravving with RAVVING_QML_DIR pointing at it.

cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja && cmake --build build RAVVING_WINDOWED=1 RAVVING_NO_ZYNTHBOX=1 RAVVING_STYLE=Basic ./build/ravving # or straight from the source tree's QML, no rebuild between QML edits: RAVVING_WINDOWED=1 RAVVING_NO_ZYNTHBOX=1 RAVVING_STYLE=Basic RAVVING_QML_DIR=$PWD/qml ./build/ravving On a desktop without a terminal, Qt logs to journald; add QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1 to see QML warnings. Keys (they send the same events as the device): 1 – 5 number keys · q w e r t y u i a s d f g h j k the 16 step keys · arrows · Enter select · Esc back · Space play · Backspace stop · o metronome · m menu · z / x , c / v , b / n knobs 1–3 down/up · , / . big knob.

Variable Effect RAVVING_WINDOWED=1 windowed instead of fullscreen RAVVING_NO_ZYNTHBOX=1 skip libzynthbox (UI only) RAVVING_STYLE Quick Controls style (default Zynthbox ) RAVVING_QML_DIR read the QML from this folder (a source tree's qml/ ) instead of the copy compiled in RAVVING_DATA_DIR read kits.json and the theme ( plasma/desktoptheme/ ) from this folder (desktop: $PWD/data ; the plasmarc then comes from build/config/ ) RAVVING_HOME one folder for everything ravving writes ( config/ , state/ , cache/ , library/ ), for a sandboxed run RAVVING_LIBRARY the library alone (projects, presets, samples, recordings) somewhere else RAVVING_PROJECT_DIR the session folder alone (default ~/.local/state/ravving ) RAVVING_SCREENSHOT_DIR capture every page to PNGs there, then quit RAVVING_GDB=1 (service) run under gdb, backtrace to the journal QT_LOGGING_RULES="ravving.cuia.debug=true" log every hardware event (CUIA, knobs) For the service, set them with systemctl --user set-environment NAME=value and clear them with unset-environment .

One CMake project, its targets each with the CMakeLists.txt of their sources (the source files themselves are where they were: the split is of the CMake files only): File Owns CMakeLists.txt the project: version, C++ standard, AUTOMOC, qt_standard_project_setup , the dependencies ( find_package Qt6 / KF6BluezQt / ZLIB, pkg_check_modules jack / sndfile / taglib), RAVVING_DATA_INSTALL_DIR and RAVVING_THEME , the build options ( RAVVING_QML_AOT , RAVVING_PCH , RAVVING_TIME_TRACE , RAVVING_UNITY , RAVVING_IWYU , RAVVING_TESTS ) with ravving_build_settings(<target>) , their per-target side; the add_subdirectory calls; the generated files ( VERSION , config/plasmarc ) and the install rules of the project as a whole ( data/ , the theme, systemd and WirePlumber drop-ins, the desktop entry and icons) src/backend/CMakeLists.txt ravving_backend , the static backend library ( src/backend/* and src/zynthboxbridge.* ): its sources, its PUBLIC include directories ( src/ , so the app includes backend/xxx.h ; src/backend/ , so its files include each other bare), its PUBLIC link set (the Qt modules, JACK, sndfile, TagLib, zlib, BluezQt), the RAVVING_* compile definitions, the unity build src/CMakeLists.txt ravving , the app: src/*.cpp , the Ravving QML module over qml/ at the repository root (each file's path from there is its resource alias, so the resources stay qrc:/qt/qml/Ravving/qml/… and the module's qmldir stays at build/Ravving ), RAVVING_QML_AOT , the branding resources and the shaders, the link to ravving_backend , the binary's install rule; the binary itself stays at build/ravving setup/CMakeLists.txt ravving-setup , the AppImage's setup program ( build/setup/ravving-setup ) tests/CMakeLists.txt the laptop-side tests, built with -DRAVVING_TESTS=ON Target names, options, output paths and the install layout are those tools/device.sh , tools/build-appimage.sh , tools/static-analysis.sh and tools/build-profile.sh rely on; a new backend class goes into src/backend/CMakeLists.txt , a new QML file into src/CMakeLists.txt 's RAVVING_QML_FILES .

Folder Where What for Settings build/ laptop and device the development loop: tools/device.sh deploy , ctest RAVVING_QML_AOT=OFF , RAVVING_PCH=ON build-release/ device the Store AppImage ( tools/build-appimage.sh , configured there on each run) Release at -O2 (no debug information; binaries stripped at install), RAVVING_QML_AOT=ON , RAVVING_PCH=ON , prefix /usr Neither is ever removed by the tools: device.sh deploy syncs the source with --exclude '/build*' (so its --delete leaves both alone on the device), REMOVE RAVVING and the release check uninstall only what cmake --install put on the system, and the AppImage build clears only its staging trees ( build-release/stage , build-release/appimage ). Keeping them is what keeps builds incremental.

The development build ( build/ ) compiles about twice as fast as the release build: the QML as bytecode only and the Qt headers precompiled. The device (a Pi 5, 4 cores) takes about as long as a 4-core laptop for the same work. RAVVING_QML_AOT (default ON). qmlcachegen compiles each QML file's bindings into C++, which then has to be compiled: on the Pi that is 40 % of a build. OFF keeps the QML precompiled but as bytecode only ( --only-bytecode ): the bindings run in Qt's interpreter and JIT, which is fine to develop with; a release keeps ON ( build-release/ ). RAVVING_PCH (default ON): the Qt headers nearly every file includes (QObject, QString, QVariant, the containers, QDebug, QJsonDocument…) parsed once instead of in each of ~90 files. ccache is used when it is installed ( CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER ): a file compiled before with the same flags comes from its cache (after a reconfigure, switching branches). The device builds at the lowest priority ( nice -n 19 ionice -c 3 in device.sh deploy ): not faster, but a build beside the music does not take the audio's time.

h: Faster builds › The backend is a library of its own
t: The backend is a library of its own. src/backend (and zynthboxbridge ) build as the static library ravving_backend , outside the QML module: Qt's type registration reads the metadata of every QObject class in the QML module's target, so a backend header inside it would regenerate every QML file's compiled C++. QML reaches the backend through context properties ( studio , ravving …), which need no registration; the LOOP / SONG values of Sections are two numbers in Rave.qml ( Rave.sectionsLoop , Rave.sectionsSong ). A backend header edit recompiles no QML.

h: A corrupted ninja log rebuilds everything
t: ninja: warning: premature end of file; recovering means build/.ninja_deps was cut short (a build killed mid-run, two builds at once in one folder): ninja then trusts nothing it built and plans every step on every build. ninja -C build -t recompact , then one full build, puts it right. Never run two builds in one build folder; let a build finish rather than kill it.

tools/build-profile.sh [OUT_DIR] [-- cmake options] builds ravving from clean with clang and -ftime-trace ( RAVVING_TIME_TRACE ) in analysis/build-profile/build (never build/ ), then: analysis.txt , ClangBuildAnalyzer 's report: the slowest files to parse and to compile, the most expensive headers (where they come from, how often), the costliest template sets and functions; trace.json , ninjatracing over .ninja_log : the build's timeline, one lane per job; open it in https://ui.perfetto.dev (or chrome://tracing) to see what holds the four cores up (moc's mocs_compilation.cpp , a slow file at the end, qmlcachegen's steps). The tools: clang (Arch's), ClangBuildAnalyzer and ninjatracing in ~/.local/bin (built from their git checkouts in ~/.local/src ), include-what-you-use from the AUR ( yay -S include-what-you-use ). include-what-you-use : cmake -B analysis/iwyu -DRAVVING_IWYU=ON -DRAVVING_PCH=OFF and build ravving_backend there: each file's compile prints what to add, what to remove and which includes a forward declaration would replace ( analysis/iwyu.log ). Precompiled headers off, or it reports their includes as unused everywhere. Read it with care: it knows no Qt mapping (it would swap <QVariantMap> for Qt's internal <qvariant.h> : ignore those), and it does not see moc's generated code, so it calls a header unneeded where a Q_PROPERTY exposes a pointer to that class ( machine.h 's SoundControls and TrackEffects, devicecontrols.h 's Wifi): moc needs the complete type there. Unity builds ( RAVVING_UNITY , the backend only: the app target carries qmlcachegen's and rcc's generated sources, and AUTOMOC's mocs_compilation.cpp stays out of the batches on its own) are there to measure, not on by default: many backend files define file-local constants with the same names ( MaxBars , AuditionMs …), which collide once a batch merges them.

site/ is the page ravving serves at http://<device>:8098/help/ (the shortcuts, the features and the documentation; site/README.md says how it is made and how to retake a screenshot). It is installed as it is ( install(DIRECTORY site …) , this README left out), so it must be plain static files with relative references, and its documentation pages are generated into the repository: python3 tools/build-site-docs.py # docs/*.md, data/secret/README.md → site/docs/*.html python3 tools/build-site-docs.py --list # the pages python3 tools/build-site-docs.py --plain # the script's own converter, as on a machine without python-markdown The same run writes site/docs/search.json , the index behind the SEARCH box in every docs page's sidebar (every section, its heading and text): the search runs in the browser alone, so it works on the public page and on the device's own copy without internet. --check (the site-docs-current test) compares the pages and the index with what the markdown gives. Only the developer docs ( docs/ ) and the packs page are rendered; the webpage's manual is docs/manual-interim.md until the user guide ( guide/ ) replaces it. The script never reads notes/ , guide/_material/ or .claude/ , and two tests keep it so: docs-fences ( tools/check-docs-fences.py ): no page in PAGES lives in those folders, and no rendered page links or includes anything from them; docs-history ( tools/check-docs-history.py ): no page in PAGES tells history or carries the wording of the requests behind a feature (dates, used to , found on milo , the design reference's name…: the phrases of tools/check-cpp-docs.py 's BANNED list and a few more). The page is public at https://ravving.github.io/: sh tools/publish-site.sh copies site/ (this README left out) into a clone of the ravving/ravving.github.io repository, commits it under the source commit and pushes; that repository's workflow deploys its own content as the Pages artifact on every push. Nothing there needs access to this repository and no secret is kept anywhere. Run it once site/ is committed. The rule ("The documentation rules", below): the docs and the page follow every change, in the same commit; python3 tools/build-site-docs.py --check (ctest site-docs-current ) fails when the rendered pages do not match the markdown. The C++ API reference is site/api/ , generated by QDoc from the sources' /*! */ blocks with python3 tools/build-api-docs.py (Qt 6's qdoc; --check is ctest api-docs-current ) and committed the same way; writing-code-docs.md has the rules and the details. Run it after editing a doc and commit site/docs/ with the markdown. It uses python-markdown when it is installed (Arch python-markdown , Debian python3-markdown ) and its own small converter otherwise; PAGES in the script lists the documents, their groups and blurbs.

h: The documentation rules › The docs and the page follow every change
t: The docs and the page follow every change. A feature added, changed or removed is not done until the same commit updates what says it: the developer docs ( docs/*.md ) it belongs in, the manual ( docs/manual-interim.md , until the user guide in guide/ replaces it), and the page in site/ (the SHORTCUTS row of a key, the FEATURES highlight or grouped item of a feature, translated through po-site/), then python3 tools/build-site-docs.py . Push, then sh tools/publish-site.sh puts it at https://ravving.github.io/; the device's copy follows the next deploy.

h: The documentation rules › The docs say what the code does now
t: The docs say what the code does now. No dates, no history, no measurements of the day, no traps met, no wording from the requests behind a feature: those are kept for the maintainers outside the published docs ( ctest -R docs-history enforces the phrases). Every new or changed C++ API comes with its QDoc in the same commit ( writing-code-docs.md ; ctest -R cpp-docs , ctest -R api-docs-current ). Every release has its translations reviewed ( translations.md ).

ravving reaches a device as an AppImage in the Store's Apps category, the way zynthbox-qml installs any app: the Store downloads the file into ~/.local/share/zynthbox/apps/<author>/<name>/ , registers it with libappimage (a desktop entry in ~/.local/share/applications ), extracts it next to itself with --appimage-extract (an <md5>.AppDir ), and from then on launches that AppDir's AppRun from inside zynthbox-qml when the entry is tapped. The bundle is for the Zynthbox device only . It is built on the device, for its architecture, against the Qt, libzynthbox, zyncoder and Zynthbox QML modules the device already has, so it bundles no libraries at all: just ravving, the setup program and the data. In particular the device must have the qml-style-zynthbox package (the Zynthbox QtQuick Controls style ravving selects at startup) and the qml-module-zynthbox package it imports ( io.zynthbox.ui ), as every stock Zynthbox does; see building.md , "What ravving is made of", for the whole chain. What the AppImage starts is not ravving but ravving-setup ( setup/ ), a page over zynthbox-qml that installs ravving from the bundle and picks which UI the device runs.

The bundle carries no libraries, so what ravving needs from the device is listed in one place, data/requirements.json (installed with the data, and in the bundle), and checked twice: The setup page, before installing ( default-app.sh deps DIR [--install] [--json] , which runs check-requirements.py from the bundle): every requirement, and every library the bundle's ravving links to ( ldd 's "not found"). The page lists what is missing, the feature each costs and the Debian package that brings it, with INSTALL MISSING PACKAGES (apt-get, online). A startup requirement or library missing means ravving cannot start there: TRY IT and MAKE IT THE DEFAULT stay dimmed and the list says why. ravving, once started ( Requirements , four seconds after the first frame): the feature requirements by file and program checks only (no process, microseconds), each missing one a warning in the issues centre: "MUSIC PLAYER will not work", what it costs, the package for the device's admins. What ravving needs that a Zynthbox image may not have: Needed for What How it gets there everything the Qt 6 Zynthbox style ( qt6/qml/Zynthbox ) and QML module ( io.zynthbox.ui ) not packaged yet : built from qml-style-zynthbox and qml-module-zynthbox's dev/qt6-port (the Debian packages are Qt 5) everything Qt Quick Shapes, Virtual Keyboard, Kirigami, KSvg (Qt 6 QML) qml6-module-qtquick-shapes , -virtualkeyboard , qml6-module-org-kde-kirigami , -ksvg starting at all libraries ravving links to: Qt 6 Multimedia, KF6 BluezQt, TagLib 2, LAME, Vorbis, libsndfile libqt6multimedia6 , libkf6bluezqt6 , libtag2 , … ( requirements.json "libraries") MUSIC PLAYER Qt Multimedia's FFmpeg backend libqt6multimedia6 BLUETOOTH speakers / SEND PipeWire's Bluetooth plugin, BlueZ's obexd libspa-0.2-bluetooth , bluez-obexd (and tools/bluetooth-setup.sh 's service steps) BLUETOOTH, INPUT ravving's WirePlumber settings (A2DP endpoints, one name per sound card) in the bundle ( etc/wireplumber/… ): install puts them in /etc/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/ , applied from the next start synths, effects, drums jalv, lv2info, FluidSynth, the LV2 plugins and soundfonts the Zynthbox image's own packages SAMPLE KING one-shots libzynthbox's fix for notes cutting each other (exclusivity group −1) a libzynthbox patch not in a stock libzynthbox: there a one-shot is cut when the next starts; not detectable from ravving Adding a feature that needs something new: add it to data/requirements.json (its files, programs, package, the feature and its effect), and to this table.

AppRun nx-apphub's launcher: exec usr/bin/ravving-setup ravving.desktop, ravving.png the entry the Store lists (Name "Ravving", the icon: a 256 × 256 PNG, .DirIcon also .DirIcon, from which libappimage makes the thumbnail zynthbox-qml's Apps grid shows; a PNG, since an SVG one renders blank) usr/bin/ravving the app usr/bin/ravving-setup the page the AppImage opens usr/share/ravving/ kits.json, engines.json, the presets, requirements.json, check-requirements.py, start.sh, default-app.sh, VERSION usr/share/applications, icons the desktop entry and icon, where they came from etc/systemd/user/ravving.service etc/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/50-ravving-*.conf Bluetooth, sound card names usr/bin/ravving , usr/share/ravving and the unit are exactly what cmake --install puts on the device: default-app.sh install DIR copies them from the bundle to the system paths.

Four choices, each a default-app.sh command on the bundle's own copy of the script (so the script always matches the files it installs): Choice What it runs Effect TRY IT (LAUNCH RAVVING once installed) install , then run ravving ravving now; Zynthbox at the next boot, or from ravving's POWER → ZYNTHBOX MAKE IT THE DEFAULT install , then ravving ravving at every boot (zynthbox-qml masked) ZYNTHBOX AT BOOT AGAIN zynthbox zynthbox-qml at boot; ravving stays installed REMOVE RAVVING (press twice) zynthbox --purge the same, and ravving's program and data leave the system; projects, takes and recordings stay The cards above them (installed version, what starts at boot, what runs now) are default-app.sh status , re-read after every action. The two installing tiles read by what the device has: "Install this bundle and …" with nothing installed, "Update the installed X to this bundle's Y and …" with another version, and "ravving Y is already installed: …" with this one, in which case the install step is skipped (TRY IT then reads LAUNCH RAVVING). A tile that would change nothing is dimmed: MAKE IT THE DEFAULT while ravving already boots, ZYNTHBOX AT BOOT AGAIN while Zynthbox does, REMOVE while nothing is installed. The AppImage itself stays in the Store's list until it is removed there. Switching stops the UI that is running, and with it everything it started: the setup page under zynthbox-qml, or the script itself under ravving's ZYNTHBOX button. The script therefore re-runs the switching commands in a transient unit of its own ( systemd-run --user --wait ) and only then touches the services. run APP switches for the session only (the boot default stays; a masked zynthbox-qml is unmasked for the start and masked again), while ravving and zynthbox change what boots.

The builder is NX AppHub CLI ( nx-apphub-cli build ), the tool the Zynthbox kit's other apps use, driven by packaging/appimage/ravving.yml.in , modelled on the kit's vvave bundle (UriHerrera/storage, AppImages/vvave/app_arm64.yml ): deps is empty, so nothing is downloaded; the zbkit repo entry is the kit's and goes unused; our binaries get into the AppDir through the scripts/ folder next to the YAML, which nx-apphub copies into usr/bin before it looks for binarypath ; the data, desktop entry, icon and unit come from the install staging tree through prebuild-commands ; binarypath and exec are ravving-setup : nx-apphub patches that binary's RPATH (with patchelf; the paths it adds do not exist in this bundle, which is harmless) and writes the AppRun for it; runtime: go (go-appimagetool, a type-2 AppImage that --appimage-extract understands). The tool is an AppImage itself and the device has no FUSE 2, so it runs with APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1 , and needs ARCH set because AppRun is a script. From the laptop: tools/device.sh appimage [OUT_DIR] # default OUT_DIR: the Store packages folder beside the repo syncs the source, installs nx-apphub on the device if it is missing ( tools/install-nx-apphub.sh : patchelf and the Python dependencies from Debian, the CLI from its git checkout into a venv), runs tools/build-appimage.sh there and copies ravving-<version>-aarch64.AppImage back. On the device itself: cd /root/ravving && tools/build-appimage.sh dist The version is project(ravving VERSION …) in CMakeLists.txt; it names the file, fills usr/share/ravving/VERSION and shows on the setup page.

Next to the AppImage, the Store listing wants an icon and a gallery: device.sh appimage also renders ravving-icon-512.png from data/icons/ravving.svg (the icon the bundle carries: the 808 plate, the big knob lit in the drums' orange over a step row) into the same output folder; device.sh gallery [OUT_DIR] screenshots each of the five pages of the ravving that is running on the device ( ravving-1-drums.png … ravving-5-sampler.png , 1280 × 800, by the number keys) into the Store packages folder's gallery/ ; pick three for the page. Load a project worth showing first: the shots are of whatever is on screen.

Every release has its translations reviewed: what changed in po/ and po-site/ since the last release is read by someone who reads the language, the screenshot tour is taken in Spanish and Japanese, and ctest -R translations-current passes (no fuzzy or untranslated text, every placeholder kept, the translated pages rendered). docs/translations.md has the steps.

Run it after any release-worthy change (a version bump, a change to the setup page, the scripts or the unit), from the laptop: tools/appimage-test.sh # build on the device, install like the Store, walk everything tools/appimage-test.sh --no-build # the AppImage already in the device's dist/ tools/appimage-test.sh --keep # leave the entry in the device's Apps list afterwards Run it on a freshly booted device. It switches between the two UIs six times in a few minutes; several walks in a row can leave zynthbox-qml hung loading its sketchpad ("Starting engine …"), a Zynthbox / PipeWire wedge after many fast restarts that only a reboot clears. It builds the AppImage ( device.sh appimage ), installs it as the Store would ( tools/store-register.py install , which registers with libappimage, extracts the AppDir and points the desktop entry at its AppRun), checks the AppDir's contents, then walks the page and ravving by touch, asserting default-app.sh status after each step: TRY IT from a purged system: ravving runs, installed is the bundle's version, /usr/bin/ravving is byte for byte the bundle's binary, the boot default is untouched; ravving's POWER → ZYNTHBOX: zynthbox-qml runs; MAKE IT THE DEFAULT: ravving runs and boots, zynthbox-qml is masked; ZYNTHBOX again: zynthbox-qml runs and stays masked for boot; ZYNTHBOX AT BOOT AGAIN: zynthbox-qml boots, ravving still installed; REMOVE RAVVING twice, CLOSE: nothing of ravving left, the page gone. The page is started with tools/store-launch.sh , which puts it in zynthbox-qml's own service cgroup on the device's display: the exact situation of a Store launch, so a switch that kills zynthbox-qml kills the page too, as in real use. Screenshots and the status after every step go to analysis/appimage-test-<date>/ (eyeball the page shots: dimmed tiles, messages). The user's ravving settings ( ~/.config/ravving ) and live session ( ~/.local/state/ravving ) are copied aside before the walk's purge and put back at the end, a failed step included. Whatever the device had before is put back at the end: a dev install by cmake --install , ravving as the boot default by default-app.sh ravving ; the Store entry is removed unless --keep . A failed assertion stops the run and prints the device's status; the device is then left mid-walk, and tools/device.sh default zynthbox or ravving brings it back by hand.

h: Testing an AppImage without the Store
t: By hand on the device, the pieces the release check uses: tools/store-register.py install dist/ravving-0.3.0-aarch64.AppImage camiloh "Ravving 0.3.0" # → prints the AppDir; the entry shows in Apps at once tools/store-launch.sh "$APPDIR" # the page, as zynthbox-qml's Apps list would start it tools/store-register.py remove "~/.local/share/zynthbox/apps/camiloh/Ravving 0.3.0/ravving-0.3.0-aarch64.AppImage" ( store-register.py does what registerAppImage / unregisterAppImage in zynthbox-qml's zynthian_gui_main.py do, minus the UI.) Or in zynthbox-qml: SCREEN_MAIN_MENU ( tools/device.sh cuia ), tap Apps, tap Ravving. The page is touch only; tools/device.sh tap X Y drives it: the tiles are the four quarters of the lower half (TRY IT 337 390, MAKE IT THE DEFAULT 943 390, ZYNTHBOX AT BOOT AGAIN 337 600, REMOVE 943 600), CLOSE 1160 736. A desktop look without a device: QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen RAVVING_WINDOWED=1 RAVVING_BUNDLE_DIR=<a staged bundle> \ RAVVING_SETUP_SHOT=setup.png ./build/setup/ravving-setup

A stock Zynthbox (Debian 13, BlueZ 5.82, PipeWire 1.4, WirePlumber 0.5) cannot start bluetooth.service and registers no A2DP endpoints: Problem Cause Fix (shipped by ravving) bluetooth.service fails at boot (status 203/EXEC), the adapter stays DOWN, the control center says "its service is not running" zynthian-sys's drop-in /etc/systemd/system/bluetooth.service.d/01-disable-sap-plugin.conf starts /usr/lib/bluetooth/bluetoothd , which Debian 13 moved to /usr/libexec/bluetooth/ data/systemd/50-ravving-bluetoothd-path.conf , installed to the same drop-in folder: the same flags ( --compat --experimental --noplugin=sap ) with the path that exists a speaker or headphones pair but will not connect: org.bluez.Error.Failed br-connection-profile-unavailable ; the adapter's UUIDs ( bluetoothctl show ) list no Audio Source / Audio Sink WirePlumber's Bluetooth monitor ( monitors/bluez.lua ) waits for a logind "active" seat before creating the BlueZ handle that registers the A2DP endpoints; the root startx session never reports one, so the monitor never starts and BlueZ has nothing to connect the device to data/wireplumber/50-ravving-bluetooth.conf , installed to /etc/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/ : wireplumber.profiles.main.monitor.bluez.seat-monitoring = disabled no audio over Bluetooth at all libspa-0.2-bluetooth (PipeWire's A2DP / HFP plugin with the SBC, aptX, FastStream, LDAC codecs) is not installed apt install libspa-0.2-bluetooth , then a WirePlumber restart (it loads the plugin at start) no file transfer bluez-obexd (the OBEX daemon, obex.service in the user session, D-Bus activated as org.bluez.obex ) is not installed apt install bluez-obexd the Qt side ravving links KDE's BluezQt ( libkf6bluezqt6 , present on the image; libkf6bluezqt-dev to build) — tools/bluetooth-setup.sh does all of it on a device and checks every step ( --check only checks); cmake --install puts the two drop-ins in place as well. After the setup bluetoothctl show lists Audio Source, Audio Sink, Handsfree and Handsfree Audio Gateway. cmake --install puts ravving's two drop-ins in place; the packages ( bluez-obexd , libspa-0.2-bluetooth , libkf6bluezqt6 ) and the service restarts are tools/bluetooth-setup.sh 's job, which the setup program should run (or the AppImage's first start), and which --check verifies afterwards. After the setup bluetoothctl show lists Audio Source, Audio Sink, Handsfree and Handsfree Audio Gateway. ravving's WirePlumber drop-in also sets bluetooth.autoswitch-to-headset-profile = false (so recording from headphones never switches them to HFP) and bluez5.enable-sbc-xq . One more setting is the device's own, set by hand on a new image since BlueZ reads no drop-in folder: FastConnectable = true under [General] in /etc/bluetooth/main.conf , so a speaker or headphones paging the device connect within a fraction of a second.

The tools that drive, hear, measure and watch ravving on a Zynthbox, from the laptop. The pieces are small scripts in tools/ ; this page is the recipe book that strings them together. For the build loop see building.md ; for what each backend piece does, architecture.md ; for the device recipes and the code checks, debugging.md and quality.md . The rule for every test: iterate with a local build ( tools/device.sh deploy ), never the AppImage; the AppImage and its release check ( packaging.md ) are for minor releases.

Like zynthbox-qml, ravving reads CUIA commands from webconf's fifo ( echo cuia/SWITCH_PLAY_RELEASED > /tmp/webconf-writes-to-this-fifo ), and the call , get and set lines below; tools/device.sh writes them over ssh. Tool What it does tools/device.sh deploy rsync the source, build on the device, install, restart, wait until the audio is wired tools/device.sh cuia NAME… press device keys by CUIA name through the remote-control fifo ( SWITCH_NUMBER_5_RELEASED , SWITCH_ARROW_UP_RELEASED , SWITCH_STEP5_PRESSED + _RELEASED , SWITCH_MODE_RELEASED = LIVE, KNOB0_UP … KNOB3_DOWN , SWITCH_ALT_PRESSED / _RELEASED , SWITCH_PLAY_RELEASED , SWITCH_STOP_RELEASED , SWITCH_BACK_RELEASED , SWITCH_SELECT_RELEASED ) (object names) a machine key, studio , ravving , input , take , or a dotted path into an object's properties: pads.kit , bass.sound ; any other name is a QML item's objectName ( padsModule , samplerModule , padsWaveEditor , samplerWaveEditor ): set padsModule modifiersExpanded true , call padsWaveEditor open 16 , set ravving currentPage 4 , set ravving samplerMachine 1 ; mouse is the MouseWatcher ( get mouse hasMouse ). QML items are found in the item tree (a page's items are visual children, not always QObject children), popups in the object tree. A QML function is called through the script engine, so its arguments arrive as plain numbers, booleans or text ( call chordsModule moveView 1 , call padsWaveEditor open 16 ); a C++ method gets its arguments converted to the parameter types tools/device.sh set OBJECT PROPERTY VALUE set a backend property ( set pads selectedPad 3 ); plain setters are not reachable by call , properties are tools/device.sh get OBJECT PROPERTY read a backend property ( get pads muted , get studio playing ): ravving logs it, the script reads it back tools/device.sh call OBJECT METHOD ARGS… call a backend method: a machine by its kits.json key ( pads , sampler , drums1 , bass , chords , lead ), studio , input , take , exporter , music (and music.library ), profile , drives (USB sticks: call drives eject /dev/sda1 ), usb (the USB page: call usb scan , call usb importEntry samples /media/root/EVS/x.wav , call usb exportEntry soundfonts /zynthian/…/x.sf2 ; usbPopup opens it: call controlCenter run usb ), bluetooth ( call bluetooth startDiscovery , get bluetooth devices , call bluetooth pair AA:BB:… , call bluetooth useAsOutput AA:BB:… true , call bluetooth sendFile AA:BB:… /path ), or a QML item by objectName ( window showPlayer true , window showRecorder true , exportPopup open , settingsPopup open , bluetoothPopup open , projectPicker open then projectPicker actionTriggered 4 for IMPORT (the index counts the dividers: NEW 0, TEMPLATES 1, IMPORT 2, SAVE AS NEW 4, EXPORT 6), playerPage , controlCenter ); any Q_INVOKABLE or slot, arguments converted ( call pads loadSample 0 /path.wav , call pads setFlag 0 looping true , call pads loadPreset "Boom Bap" , call input record , call input record true for a RECORDER take; set input.effects preset OVERDRIVE ; get input.tuner frequency ; call ravving setLogRules "ravving.cuia.debug=true" turns a log category on while running: each key, who took it and the focus chain), video ( set video countdown 0 , call video start / stop / toggle , get video state / lastFile / lastInfo , set video quality high ) and computer ( call computer setup HOST USER PASSWORD 22 , check , send /path , forget ), files (the FILES browser: get files kinds , call files entries videos , call files presetFile "pattern::bass-presets.json::My Bassline 1" ; filesPopup open , filesPopup showKind presets , filesPopup openFolder BASS : the drawer's dialogs open by script only once the MENU drawer has been shown since the start, so press MENU twice first); the journal logs each call tools/device.sh tap X Y a touch at a screen pixel (the panel is 1280 × 800); a hold is xdotool mousemove X Y mousedown 1; sleep 1; xdotool mouseup 1 over ssh with DISPLAY=:0 XAUTHORITY=/root/.Xauthority tools/device.sh shot FILE.png a screenshot, copied here (crop with ImageMagick to read details) tools/device.sh animations every running animation and repeating Timer, with its item, whether it is shown, its QML file and position: what keeps the window drawing (an idle screen should draw nothing) tools/audio-impact.sh [SECONDS] [idle\|playing\|both] what the screen, polls and watchers cost the sound: frames/s, CPU per thread group, realtime-thread page faults, xruns ( quality.md ); idle presses nothing, so it is safe while someone plays tools/device.sh gallery [DIR] one screenshot per page tools/device.sh log [SECONDS] ravving's journal tools/device.sh bt [ADDR] [SINCE] / bt capture [SECONDS] [FILE] why a Bluetooth device does (not) connect or play, read-only (tools/bt-diagnose.sh: config, endpoints, codecs, the device's journal and a tally of failures), and an HCI trace with btmon while you connect it ( debugging.md ) tools/device.sh play FILE.mid play a MIDI file into ravving as an external keyboard ( tools/midifile.py makes one) tools/device.sh default … switch between ravving and zynthbox-qml, install, purge, status tools/meter.py (on the device: tools/device.sh tools copies it to /tmp ) pw-jack python3 /tmp/meter.py PORT --seconds 2 : RMS, brightness and crest of a JACK port tools/record.py , tools/analyse.py , tools/repeatcheck.py record ports to numpy, analyse, check periodicity tools/soundfont.py presets · ranges · render · categorise FILE… look inside an SF2 / SF3 before making it a kits.json sound source ( categorise --json proposes the entries, a category from the name and folder: Strings, Organ, Keys, Bass, Guitar, Winds, Voices, Synth, Alien for the drones, Drums, Other; mute fonts left out): its presets (bank:program), the key and velocity ranges of its zones (a velRange 0–0 font is mute everywhere: SynStrings, LaString, MelloString, Organ on the image), and an offline render of one chord through fluidsynth with the level every quarter second tools/mididump.py PORT SECONDS (on the device, pw-jack python3 ) what an engine really receives on a JACK MIDI port: notes, controllers, program changes, bends (the clock and ticks with --clock ) tools/profile-taps.sh , tools/qml-profile.sh , tools/boot-timing.sh responsiveness, QML profiling, start-up time ( quality.md ) tools/static-analysis.sh clang-tidy / clazy tools/pads-test.sh the PAD SAMPLER feature suite (below) tools/sections-test.sh SECTIONS heard: sections picked at random moments while the master records, tools/sections-test.py checks every 8th sounds once and on time, a change only on a bar line, a rest in whole bars (below) tools/bluetooth-setup.sh [--check] set a device up for Bluetooth (packages, the two drop-ins, services) and check every step ( packaging.md ) tools/soundfont-check.sh every soundfont kits.json uses, checked on the device: exists, can sound, the preset exists, a chord comes out offline ( quality.md ) tools/drums-test.sh the DRUMS page suite (60 checks: 55 on the device, 5 timing checks on the laptop from a recording of the lane): a new project starting clean on every page, the grid (toggle, accent, undo / redo, clear, bars, view bar, cursor and STEP entry), the kit (another loaded, reset), the row mix heard (mute, solo, level, accent, the machine's mute and pause), LIVE (a pad heard, hits recorded while playing), presets (save, load, remove), every SOUND EFFECT on and off with its knobs read back and DRIVE / COMPRESSOR / EQ / PAN heard, the kit's MODS, and tools/hits-timing.py (shared with the chords suite): every 8th within 12 ms, accents louder. It works in a project of its own and puts the previous one back tools/chords-test.sh the CHORDS page suite (54 checks: 50 on the device, 4 timing checks on the laptop): the key and chord sets (names follow ROOT and the set), the CHORDS view (chords, runs, undo / redo, clear), NOTES (toggle, a step's notes, custom voicings), SLOTS (arm, fill, bars, clear, the steps rebuilt), the octave, the sound source (a soundfont, back to TAL), heard (mute, pause, LIVE keys, a hit recorded), presets, every SOUND EFFECT with EQ / PAN / DRIVE heard, and hits-timing.py on two bars of piano stabs (every 8th within 20 ms) tools/video-test.sh the video recorder suite ( architecture.md , "Live recordings"): a recording over the fifo while playing, its MP4 (streams, starts, length, frame rate), the ring's dropped frames, the graph's xruns meanwhile, RECORD / STOP by the keys, the TIMER and its cancel, VIDEO off tools/share-test.sh [FILE] the phone share (SEND… → PHONE · QR CODE) with the laptop as the phone: the newest video (or FILE) offered over the fifo, its link fetched with curl and compared with the device's file (size, md5), a Range request → 206 of the right length, HEAD, a wrong token and the root → 404, the deliveries counted, the help page at /help/ (200 text/html, its CSS, a missing file and ../ → 404, not an attachment, not counted), the library's pages (openBrowse → the index, a kind's page, a DOWNLOAD link as an attachment, a wrong kind and token → 404, closeBrowse → 404), stop → the link 404 while the help page stays; runs on the laptop (it must reach the device's address, as a phone would) tools/computer-link-test.sh the computer link end to end against the device's own sshd (a throwaway local user as the computer): set-up with the password, the key installed, Downloads found, a wrong password told apart, a file sent, the key removed → refused tools/video-voice-check.sh the voice-over mix of a video: the transport playing, tools/tone.py's 1 kHz bursts into the tap's mic ports as the voice, the file measured second by second (the music DUCK dB quieter while the tone is on, the tone LIFT dB louder); DUCK=18 LIFT=0 for other settings; the device must be idle tools/video-sync-check.sh , tools/video-encode-impact.sh , tools/video-mic-check.sh the video sync mechanism alone; the encoder tiers' cost while playing; a recording with the RECORDER's mic heard and measured tools/export-test.sh the exports and music player suite (below): a project saved, changed and reopened, a short track export (WAV, then FLAC) checked to the sample, its tags and cover, a .ravv bundle and its import, the player's queue, playback, pause, seek and stop tools/examples/lofi-say-it.sh a whole project built by script ("Building a project by script", below): the recipe for making music over the fifo tools/appimage-test.sh , tools/store-register.py , tools/store-launch.sh the Store AppImage release check ( packaging.md ) Environment switches: QT_LOGGING_RULES="ravving.cuia.debug=true" (set with systemctl --user set-environment and a restart) logs every hardware event with whether it was accepted and the focus chain it travelled; ravving.midi.debug=true the MIDI input.

A machine's track after its effects is TrackPassthrough:Channel{track+1}-lane1-dryOutLeft (kits.json gives the track: drums 0–2, bass 3, chords 4, lead 5, SAMPLE KING 6, PAD SAMPLER 7, the input monitor 9); the master is GlobalPlayback:dryOutLeft . Always compare runs (silent, playing, silent again), never read a single number: a track playing a beat is ~0.02–0.2 RMS, silence is 0.0.

sh tools/pads-test.sh runs every PAD SAMPLER backend feature as a check on the device (load, one-shot, NOTE ON, LOOP + latch + stopAll, the pattern on both tracks, erase, halve / double, MUTE, copy, a card value, a take with SMART stop when a signal is present, the samplers' exclusivity, the folders), PASS / FAIL / SKIP per line with the measured level, and exits with the number of failures. Run it after any change to the machine, the wiring, the paths or libzynthbox; it needs the reference audio in the library and a kick sample in the device's sketchpads. Add a check for every new feature.

sh tools/sections-test.sh (from the laptop) builds a test project on the device: DRUMS 1 alone, a bar of 8ths at 100 BPM, section A a kick, B a closed hat, REST with DRUMS 1 resting. It records the master while A and B are picked 24 times at random moments (0.6–2.6 s apart: some land, some are replaced before their bar), then A and REST in turn, and tools/sections-test.py checks the recordings by their onsets (a kick is dark, a hat bright): every 8th once (no gap near 600 ms, none under 200), on time (each onset within 15 ms of one grid fitted through them all), the sound changing only on an onset that begins a bar, the rests whole bars from a bar line. What was open before is opened again (saved first when it had changes). Read the timing against the grid, not gap by gap: the detector reads a kick 2.7 ms early and a hat 3.0 ms late (each ±2.6 ms), so a gap across a change carries both errors.

sh tools/export-test.sh runs the exports and the music player as checks on the device against whatever project is open (27 checks): the profile's author fallback, a 2-bar WAV export that starts busy, plays the transport, stops it, lasts exactly 2 bars + 1 s at the project's tempo (to the sample), is 24-bit at the engine's rate, carries its tags (python3-taglib reads them back), its cover PNG and a sidecar that says the start was placed on the audio clock ( headFrom: clock ); a 1-bar FLAC; a .ravv bundle (project.json, metadata.json, cover.png, the samples; zip integrity checked by Python) imported as a new project with its sample paths rewritten; the library listing the tracks, playNow sounding on the master (meter.py), the position moving, pause, resume, seek, enqueue, stop. It removes its "Export Test" files (exports, the imported project and its samples) at the end. A track export by hand over the fifo (JSON in one argument; no | inside): ssh root@milo.local "printf '%s\n' 'call|exporter|exportAudio|{\"title\":\"My Track\",\"artist\":\"Me\",\"format\":\"flac\",\"bars\":8,\"loops\":2,\"tail\":2}' > /tmp/webconf-writes-to-this-fifo" tools/device.sh get exporter phase # preparing · recording · cutting · tagging · done tools/device.sh get exporter lastFile

A project names what it plays instead of holding it: each instrument's sound source and factory sound by name, its MODS knobs as "CARD/KNOB", a drum kit or a sample by path, automation lanes by knob. A change to data/kits.json , data/engines.json or the device's files can leave a saved project pointing at nothing, and it then opens on another sound, silently. Three checks catch it: On the laptop, every change of text: sh tools/i18n-extract.sh , translate what it marks, then ctest -R translations-current ( tools/check-translations.py : templates current, catalogs compile, nothing untranslated or fuzzy, placeholders and markup kept, the translated pages rendered). To test a language on the device: device.sh set localization language es ( ja , en , or empty for the system's), then run the page suites in it: a suite that reads a display text instead of a key fails there. On the laptop, every change: ctest -R projects runs tools/check-projects.py over data/demos against the repo's kits.json and engines.json (sources, MODS knobs, automation lanes, kit roles, sections and the song). Over the device's saved projects: tools/device.sh projects ( -v for every project) runs it on the device against the installed data and files too: kit soundfonts, samples (an older take outside samples/takes/ is found there too, as ravving finds it), imported soundfonts, the TAL factory sounds. Run it after a data change, before a release. In ravving, each time a project opens: the machines note what they could not resolve as they restore it ( ProjectCheck , Machine::checkSaved() : nothing is read twice, nothing runs after), and the issues centre shows one warning listing it ("5AM: 2 of what it plays is missing"), cleared by the next project that resolves.

h: Recipes › A sampler pad from a script
t: A sampler pad from a script. Load, play, loop, latch, stop: sh tools/device.sh call pads loadSample 0 /zynthian/zynthian-my-data/ravving/samples/refs/movie-intro-16s.wav sh tools/device.sh call pads audition 0 # one pass sh tools/device.sh call pads setFlag 0 looping true sh tools/device.sh call pads setLatched 0 true # held looping, as a long press does sh tools/device.sh call pads stopAll # what STOP does

h: Recipes › A pattern on the pads
t: A pattern on the pads. Fill pads 1–4 with a kick, snare, hat and clap from the device's library ( find /zynthian/zynthian-my-data/samples -iname "*kick*.wav" | head -1 ), then call pads loadPreset "Boom Bap" , cuia SWITCH_PLAY_RELEASED , meter the lane, cuia SWITCH_STOP_RELEASED . The step keys write the selected pad's row with LIVE off and play the pads with LIVE on ( SWITCH_MODE_RELEASED toggles it; a step key held past half a second latches its pad).

h: Recipes › A take into a pad
t: A take into a pad. With something on the input jack ( INPUT sets MIC / GUITAR / LINE): call pads setSelectedPad 2 , then call input record ; with SMART on ( studio.input.autoStop , default on) the take ends by itself half a second after the sound stops, else call input stop . The processed take lands on the pad trimmed to its last burst; the journal shows takeReady . Without a signal the take never auto-stops: that is the guard against stopping before anything was played.

The hardware walk. Switch the trace on, then cuia SWITCH_ARROW_UP_RELEASED step by step and read which item accepted each key; ALT + ▲ must land on the header from anywhere. Key 5 opens page 5 and, pressed again, toggles between SAMPLE KING and the PAD SAMPLER; the choice survives restarts, so check the nameplate in a screenshot before sending taps at a panel (a hold on the wrong one writes a step). Reference audio for sampling tests lives in the library's samples/refs/ folder ( /zynthian/zynthian-my-data/ravving/samples/refs/ ).

tools/device.sh graph all -s 60 checks the PipeWire / JACK graph ravving runs in (rates and periods against the driver's, linked nodes that are not running, the audio threads' priorities, xruns over a minute, the ravving links). routing.md has the map of what ravving wires and the tools (pw-top, pw-dump, pw-dot, jack_iodelay…). tools/issues-test.sh checks the issues center end to end (reports over the fifo, order, dismiss, clear, the drawer card and the dialog).

The basic checks: sh tools/bluetooth-setup.sh --check . With a device at hand, over the fifo: tools/device.sh call bluetooth startDiscovery; sleep 10; tools/device.sh get bluetooth devices tools/device.sh call bluetooth pair 84:D3:52:35:80:99 # a speaker pairs without a prompt tools/device.sh get bluetooth pairing # a phone: {kind confirm, passkey} → answerPairing true tools/device.sh call bluetooth useAsOutput 84:D3:52:35:80:99 true tools/device.sh cuia SWITCH_PLAY_RELEASED # heard on the speaker tools/device.sh call bluetooth sendFile AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF "/zynthian/zynthian-my-data/ravving/exports/Lo-fi Say It.wav" What to measure: Metric How, on the device signal (RSSI, dBm: −30 excellent, −67…−70 good, below −80 drops) bluetoothctl info ADDR (RSSI while scanning), hcitool rssi ADDR once connected link quality / packet loss hcitool lq ADDR (255 = best); btmon -w /tmp/bt.snoop during playback and count retransmissions A2DP codec and latency pw-cli info <bluez sink id> ( api.bluez5.codec : SBC by default, aptX / LDAC when both sides have it); pw-top for the sink node's quantum and the graph's (the studio stays at 256 / 48000; the Bluetooth node runs its own) OBEX throughput transfer.transferred over time ( get bluetooth transfer ) what BlueZ sees btmon (HCI trace), busctl --system tree org.bluez , journalctl -u bluetooth what WirePlumber does journalctl --user -u wireplumber , with systemctl --user set-environment WIREPLUMBER_DEBUG=3 and a restart for the monitor's own lines

Tool What it does tools/video-test.sh the feature suite on the device (41 checks): a recording over the fifo while playing, the MP4's streams, starts, length and frame rate, the ring's dropped frames, the graph's xruns meanwhile, RECORD / STOP by the device keys (the music goes on), the TIMER and its cancel, VIDEO off, the computer link's state tools/computer-link-test.sh the computer link end to end against the device's own sshd (21 checks): a throwaway local user stands in for the computer (set up with the password, the key installed, Downloads found, a wrong password told apart, a file sent and compared, the key removed → refused); the user is removed and the previous computer put back tools/share-test.sh [FILE] the phone share from the laptop (31 checks): the newest video offered over the fifo, fetched with curl and compared (size, md5), a Range → 206, HEAD, 404s, the deliveries counted, stop → connection refused tools/video-mic-check.sh [SECONDS] a recording with the mic while the music is stopped, its audio measured (speak when told) tools/video-sync-check.sh the sync mechanism alone (a synthetic audio feeder + x11grab + the remux), PASS when both streams start together tools/video-encode-impact.sh [SECONDS] the tiers' cost while playing; mirror any change to the encoder arguments here and re-measure Scripts: set video countdown 0 , call video start , get video state , call video stop , get video lastFile , get video lastInfo , call video toggle , set video quality high , set video source camera , get video cameras ; call computer setup HOST USER PASSWORD 22 , call computer check , call computer send /path/file , call computer forget .

Everything a finger does on the device, a script can do through the remote-control fifo: load samples, write patterns, pick sounds, set the key and the tempo, save the result as a project. tools/examples/five-am/ (the 5AM demo: sections and the song by script, build.py writing the lines, run.sh sending them) and tools/examples/lofi-say-it.sh (a lo-fi hip hop project built on the changes of "Say It (Over and Over Again)") are complete ones; copy one for the next. A loop in the shell that reads a file line by line and calls tools/device.sh loses all but the first line (the ssh inside reads the loop's stdin): send the lines from one script on the device (run.sh) or use ssh -n .

FIFO=/tmp/webconf-writes-to-this-fifo send() { timeout 2 sh -c "echo \"$1\" > $FIFO"; sleep 0.2; } call() { local line="call"; for a in "$@"; do line="$line|$a"; done; send "$line"; } setp() { send "set|$1|$2|$3"; } get() { send "get|$1|$2"; journalctl --user -u ravving --since '-5s' --no-pager | grep 'fifo get' | tail -1 | sed 's/.*= //'; } A script runs on the device (copy it there, as the example does with itself); every call is one line on the fifo and takes about a fifth of a second, so a full project is a few hundred lines and a couple of minutes. tools/device.sh call|set|get do the same one at a time from the laptop.

Step Calls keep what is there, start clean get studio.projects dirty , call studio.projects saveAs NAME ; call studio.projects newProject tempo, swing, key set studio bpm 74 , set studio swing 0.58 (and set studio swingEighths true for jazz: the off-beat 8ths swing, not the 16ths; the header's SWING 8 / 16, tapped), call header setKey ROOT SCALE (root 0–11 from C, scale an index into Rave.scales: 0 natural minor, 1 major, 2 Dorian…). NEW resets the key to C minor : set it before writing anything in a key drums call drumsN clear , call drumsN toggleStep ROW STEP , toggleAccent STEP ; rows by get drumsN rows ; call drumsN saveAsPreset keeps the beat as "My Beat N" chords set chords bars 8 (the most a pattern holds), set chords viewBar B , then per step call chords setStepNotes STEP "48,52,55,58" (MIDI notes; a note outside the key makes the voicing chromatic). A run of the same voicing on consecutive steps is one held chord ; an empty step ends it. Diatonic shortcuts: setChord STEP DEGREE , or SLOTS: assignSlot SLOT DEGREE + cycleSlotBars SLOT . saveAsPreset keeps a chart as "My Progression N" (a longer form = several presets to switch between) bass, lead set bass bars 8 , set bass viewBar B , call bass setNote STEP NOTE (MIDI;
