C2 = 36 for the bass, C4 = 60 for the lead, see kits.json baseNote ), setNoteLength STEP STEPS (a note lasts one step unless set: a half note is 8, up to 64, into the next bars), toggleAccent STEP , toggleSlide STEP ; any note is accepted, in the key or not, and a preset keeps it exactly (the chart's ALTER and HOLD lanes) drum kits call drums1 loadKit PATH : a kit file, or a preset inside a soundfont with chosen rows ( …/FluidR3Mono_GM.sf3#128:32?CYMBAL=51&HAT=44 , the Jazz kit with its ride and hi-hat foot; engines.md ); call drumsN setRowLevel ROW 0..1 sounds call bass chooseSoundSource Upright (names from get bass soundSources ), call chords loadSoundPreset NAME for TAL's factory sounds, call bass.sound setValue CARD KNOB 0..1 for the synth's own SOUND MODIFIERS pads call pads clearPad N , call pads loadSample N PATH [start length] , call pads chopRegions N COUNT FIRSTPAD , set pads selectedPad N + call pads setValue MIX VOLUME 0.95 , set pads bars 8 , set pads viewBar B + toggleStep PAD STEP ; a long one-shot (a 16 s intro) needs a loop long enough not to retrigger it: 8 bars at 74 BPM is 26 s SAMPLE KING call sampler loadSample SLOT PATH ; set ravving samplerMachine 1 puts the pads on key 5 save call studio.projects saveAs NAME (a name typed in the dialog would do the same); get studio.projects current to check sections and the song the section on screen is what the calls above edit; call studio.sections rename s1 DROP , duplicate s1 (a copy, placed after the section ON SCREEN, which it becomes), setBars ID 1–8 , set MACHINE paused true (it rests in this section), move FROM TO (the list), removeFromSong 0 / appendToSong ID / setRepeats INDEX N (the song), set studio.sections mode 1 (SONG), pick ID (the one on screen when saved)

How to test and debug ravving on the device with the tools in tools/ . Everything here runs from the laptop against the device ( root@milo.local by default; set DEVICE= for another). The device's root shell is zsh: it does not split $var into words (pass a stored argument list as ${=var} ).

Tool Runs on What it does tools/device.sh laptop deploy, press keys (CUIA), tap, screenshot, play MIDI, read the log tools/midifile.py either write a MIDI file holding a note or a chord, to play in as a keyboard tools/meter.py device level, brightness and crest factor of any JACK ports tools/synthprobe.py device play a scripted note list straight into an engine and record it tools/analyse.py device measure a synthprobe recording: segments and a pitch track tools/lv2probe.sh device try an LV2 effect on a live signal before wiring it in tools/record.py device record JACK ports to a numpy file tools/repeatcheck.py either how exactly a recording repeats at a given length (STUTTER / LOOP) tools/default-app.sh device make ravving the device's UI, or go back to zynthbox-qml ( device.sh default … ) tools/boot-timing.sh laptop time ravving's start by phase over restarts or reboots tools/qml-profile.sh laptop record and summarise a QML profiler trace of a start tools/qml-profile-summary.py laptop read a .qtd trace: self time per type, file and event tools/static-analysis.sh laptop clang-tidy and clazy over src/ tools/bt-diagnose.sh device why a Bluetooth device does (not) connect or play, read-only ( device.sh bt [ADDR] ); device.sh bt capture records an HCI trace tools/audio-impact.sh laptop what the rest costs the sound: frames/s, CPU per thread group, realtime page faults, xruns, idle and playing The quality and performance checks (what to run when) are in quality.md , the test suites in testing.md . sh tools/device.sh tools copies the device-side ones to its /tmp . They need python3-jack and numpy there and must run under pw-jack : a plain JACK client (jalv over ssh included) would start its own jackd and break the session's audio.

The service comes back on its own ( Restart=always : startx leaves with 0 even when ravving dies under it, so on-failure would never fire; at most 5 starts in 2 minutes). The next start tells the issues center how the run before ended ( src/backend/lastrun.h ): ravving keeps a marker, ~/.local/state/ravving/running , while it runs and removes it on a clean exit (SIGTERM, a normal return); data/start.sh writes last-exit (" ", 128 + n for signal n). A crash (signal 11, 6), a kill (9), a failure (exit 1: often the display went away) or the session ending first (no exit written: X stopped) each read as such, with the journalctl line to look at. To try it: pkill -SEGV -x ravving brings ravving back 3 s later with the issue "ravving stopped unexpectedly" (error); systemctl --user restart ravving reports nothing.

Deploy and wait. sh tools/device.sh deploy syncs the tree (not build/ ), builds, installs, restarts the service and returns once the journal says audio and MIDI wired , plus a moment for the window. Keys sent while ravving boots are lost.

Go somewhere and look. sh tools/device.sh cuia SWITCH_NUMBER_3_RELEASED # page 3 (BASS) sh tools/device.sh cuia SWITCH_ARROW_UP_RELEASED SWITCH_ARROW_UP_RELEASED sh tools/device.sh tap 255 766 # the bass's DRIVE chip sh tools/device.sh shot /tmp/bass.png # 1280 × 800; crop with PIL to read details The CUIA names are zynthbox's: SWITCH_STEP5_PRESSED / _RELEASED (a step key held, then let go), SWITCH_MODE_RELEASED (LIVE), SWITCH_SELECT_RELEASED , SWITCH_BACK_RELEASED , KNOB0_UP … KNOB3_DOWN (knobs 1–3 and the big one). A step key with LIVE off edits the pattern on release : switch LIVE on (MODE) before using step keys as a test signal, and off again after.

Call a backend method. sh tools/device.sh call pads loadSample 0 /zynthian/…/x.wav , call pads audition 0 , call pads setFlag 0 looping true , call input record : the fifo's call|OBJECT|METHOD|ARGS… line ( src/cuiafifo.h , fields split on | so paths keep their slashes) invokes any Q_INVOKABLE or slot on a machine (by its kits.json key), studio , input or take , converting the arguments; the journal logs each call with its arguments and whether it was found.

h: Recipes › Play notes as a keyboard
t: Play notes as a keyboard. python3 tools/midifile.py /tmp/c2.mid 36 then sh tools/device.sh play /tmp/c2.mid (it goes in through Midi Through, 14:0, which ravving reads like any controller: the bass plays it when it is LIVE, or with nothing LIVE while its page is on screen). A chord: midifile.py /tmp/c.mid 40 52 67 .

Measure a sound. While a note plays ( aplaymidi -p 14:0 /tmp/c2.mid & on the device): pw-jack python3 /tmp/meter.py TrackPassthrough:Channel4-lane1-dryOutLeft # rms 0.0256 hf 0.001 crest 3.44 Compare runs, never single numbers: an effect off, on, off again (the last run must match the first, or something else changed). hf/rms is brightness, crest falls with saturation or compression. Ports worth knowing: Port What it carries ravving-<machine>:<out> the engine itself ( ravving-bass:lv2_audio_out_1 ) TrackPassthrough:Channel{t+1}-lane1-dryOutLeft a machine's track after its EQ/compressor/pan (bass: Channel4) TrackPassthrough:Channel{t+1}-lane1-wetOutFx1Left / Fx2 its reverb / delay send ravving-reverb:lv2_audio_out_1 , ravving-delay:outputleft the send effects GlobalPlayback:dryOutLeft the master, before the LIVE FX inserts Reference levels: the bass track ~0.026 RMS for a held C2, the drums 0.15–0.17 playing, reverb return 0.04 with a send on. A soloed machine (S) mutes the others' sends too: check the INSTRUMENTS chips before suspecting an effect.

Check the wiring. ssh root@milo.local 'pw-jack jack_lsp -c' lists every connection; follow a machine from its engine: ravving-bass:lv2_audio_out_1 → SynthPassthrough:Synth4 → TrackPassthrough:Channel4-lane1 → AudioLevels:Channel4 → GlobalPlayback , with DRIVE on ravving-bass-drive between the engine and the synth slot. JackWiring logs audio and MIDI wired when every connection it wants exists, or some ports never appeared after 20 s.

Try an engine. Before choosing one, run it alone and probe it: pw-jack jalv -n probe http://distrho.sf.net/plugins/Nekobi & # on the device pw-jack python3 /tmp/synthprobe.py probe:lv2_events_in probe:lv2_audio_out_1 \ --notes "0.2:36:40:0.2 0.8:36:127:0.2 2.6:36:100:0.4 2.9:48:100:0.3" python3 /tmp/analyse.py --segment "plain:0.2:0.4" --segment "accent:0.8:1.0" --track "slide:2.85:3.15"

Try an effect. lv2probe.sh URI SOURCE MIDIFILE sym=val … runs a throw-away copy of an LV2 fed from a port and measures it, one setting per call; DRIVE (Calf Saturator: input gain, saturation, makeup) is calibrated with runs like lv2probe.sh http://calf.sourceforge.net/plugins/Saturator ravving-bass:lv2_audio_out_1 /tmp/n36.mid level_in=16 drive=5 . lv2info URI lists a plugin's ports and ranges; lv2ls | grep -i word finds plugins.

Test a time effect. Record the master after the repeat while holding a pad, then check the repeat: pw-jack python3 /tmp/record.py ravving-repeat:out_l --seconds 4.5 & , hold STUTTER ( xdotool mousemove 400 113 mousedown 1; sleep 1.5; xdotool mouseup 1 ; the transport must play), then python3 /tmp/repeatcheck.py --file /tmp/record.npy --bpm 120 --length-steps 1 : ~0 live, 1.000 while held. Dragging a held pad is xdotool mousemove steps of 5 px while the button is down.

Read the saved state. ~/.local/state/ravving/session.json is the whole session (the same format as a project): machines (each one's steps or line , bars , kit , sound , effects , level , paused , preset …), bpm , swing , master , liveFx , globalEffects , ui . It is written 1.5 s after a change and on exit. Projects are in /zynthian/zynthian-my-data/ravving/projects/ ( .current names the open one). To check a save/open round trip: copy session.json, SAVE, NEW, open the project again, and compare the two files' machines (a python one-liner; every machine should be identical). From QML, give studio.uiValue() its fallback with ?? (a JS object does not convert to the C++ default), and know that a JS object passed to C++ arrives as a QJSValue ( setUiValue unwraps it, or it would save as null).

Logging. Categories are off by default: ssh root@milo.local 'systemctl --user set-environment QT_LOGGING_RULES="ravving.cuia.debug=true;ravving.midi.debug=true" && systemctl --user restart ravving' sh tools/device.sh log 30 ravving.cuia prints every key with where it landed ( accepted / unhandled ) and the focus chain; ravving.midi every external MIDI message. systemctl --user unset-environment QT_LOGGING_RULES turns them off again.

Screenshots without the device. RAVVING_SCREENSHOT_DIR=dir RAVVING_STYLE=Basic RAVVING_NO_ZYNTHBOX=1 RAVVING_DATA_DIR=$PWD/data QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/ravving captures every page and a few scripted states (src/main.cpp: add a step there, and find items by objectName with findItem() ). It also shows QML warnings: a clean run prints nothing.

Check the audio input. Read both channels while someone plays or touches the plug's tip (a finger on a working input hums around −30 dBFS; an open one sits near −75): pw-jack python3 /tmp/record.py "Built-in Audio Stereo:capture_FL" --seconds 10 --save /tmp/l.npy amixer -c 3 sset "ADC Left Capture Source" "VINL1[SE]" # try the ADC's other inputs Two cards are called "Built-in Audio Stereo" (the HiFiBerry and a Dummy, always −180 dBFS), and which one gets the number suffix ( capture_FL-92 ) changes between boots : check with pw-dump (the port alias names the card) or ravving's journal line input ports . ravving finds them itself ( InputPorts ).

h: Recipes › Why a Bluetooth device does not connect or play
t: Why a Bluetooth device does not connect or play. Read-only, nothing is connected or restarted, so it is safe while someone listens: sh tools/device.sh bt 6C:5A:B5:49:35:D8 # one device; no address: every known one sh tools/device.sh bt 6C:5A:B5:49:35:D8 -1d # only the last day of the journals sh tools/device.sh bt capture 60 /tmp/lg.snoop # btmon for 60 s: connect the device meanwhile btmon -r /tmp/lg.snoop | less # or open it in Wireshark The report has the adapter and main.conf , the A2DP endpoints PipeWire registered (one per codec, shared by every device), WirePlumber's Bluetooth drop-ins, the PipeWire Bluetooth objects (card, sink, codec) and ravving's loopback, then per device its record (keys hidden), its cached A2DP endpoints decoded (which codecs it takes), the bluetoothd / WirePlumber / ravving journal lines and a tally: link up, Unable to select SEP , create-socket, page-timeout, profile-unavailable, A2DP transports opened. What each failure means is in "Bluetooth troubleshooting" below and architecture.md . In a capture, a page that is never answered shows as Create Connection followed by Connect Complete … Page Timeout ; a link refused for lack of an endpoint shows the AVDTP Discover / Get Capabilities and then a disconnect with no Set Configuration .

Symptom Look at Likely control center: "its service is not running" / bluetooth.state unavailable systemctl status bluetooth → 203/EXEC the bluetoothd path drop-in missing (run the setup) the adapter shows but Powered: no after a power on rfkill list (soft blocked), bluetoothctl power on rfkill: rfkill unblock bluetooth the link comes up, then COULD NOT CONNECT · br-connection-create-socket and DISCONNECTED a second later journalctl -u bluetooth : Unable to select SEP ; device.sh bt ADDR another audio device streams the same codec (SBC): one local endpoint per codec. Disconnect it; ravving hands the link over itself when you connect from the dialog COULD NOT CONNECT · br-connection-page-timeout (bluetoothd: Host is down ) is the device on, in Bluetooth mode, not connected to a phone? device.sh bt capture while connecting it did not answer the page; ravving pages it again for about 37 s ("waking…"). A speaker that was last used with a phone connects only once milo pages it pairs but br-connection-profile-unavailable on connect bluetoothctl show has no Audio Source / Sink WirePlumber's monitor not running: the seat drop-in missing, or WirePlumber started before libspa-0.2-bluetooth was installed (restart it) connected, but no bluez_output.* node in wpctl status journalctl --user -u wireplumber the device connected HFP only, or the A2DP transport failed: disconnect and connect again the issues center: "… plays no sound" (or it went quiet and came back by itself) the journal: "plays silence: routing to it again", then "the output plays again" or not; pw-jack python3 /tmp/meter.py ravving-out:output_FL against ravving-phaser:out_l the loopback passes silence though every node runs and every link is there (after a codec switch replaced the sink): ravving routes again once by itself; if that fails, pick the jacks and the device again, or turn the device off and on PLAYING THROUGH says so but nothing is heard pgrep -af pw-loopback , pw-link -l \| grep -A1 ravving-phaser:out_l (should show ravving-out:playback_FL ), pw-top (the bluez sink R, the HiFiBerry S) the loopback did not start (pipewire-bin missing?) or its links failed: pick the jacks and the device again; the journal has "master linked to ravving-out" when it worked sound from the device and the Bluetooth device wpctl status (is the jacks' sink muted?) the jacks were not muted: pick the jacks and the device again glitchy sound over Bluetooth pw-top : is the bluez sink the driver of ravving's nodes? the default sink was switched by hand ( wpctl set-default ): put the jacks back as default, ravving routes through the loopback instead; Wi-Fi on the same antenna also costs (the Pi's radio is shared) sending fails at once: "COULD NOT REACH" busctl --user list \| grep obex , systemctl --user status obex obexd missing or not activatable; the phone must have OBEX push enabled (Android: accept the incoming file prompt) a phone cannot see milo bluetoothctl show → Discoverable: no VISIBLE lasts three minutes; press it again

The checks to run on ravving every so often (and before a release) and what each tool is for. All the tools live in tools/ ; the laptop ones need no libzynthbox (ravving builds without it), the device ones run against root@milo.local ( DEVICE= for another). When Run Look at after C++ changes tools/static-analysis.sh new lines in analysis/summary.txt against the accepted findings (§1) after changes to a shell script ( tools/*.sh , data/start.sh ) tools/static-analysis.sh shell (ShellCheck, here or on the device) analysis/shellcheck.log : the scripts are kept at zero findings; a finding that is the script's intent (a remote command built on the laptop, a deliberate word split) gets a # shellcheck disable= line with the reason above it after adding a pointer handler (Tap / Drag / Pinch / Point / Wheel) to a page or the header tools/static-analysis.sh handlers zero: each binds enabled: … !Session.inputBlocked , else a drag on a dialog reaches it (§1, "Handlers under dialogs") after QML changes the screenshot tour (§4) QML warnings in its output; pixel diffs against a reference tour after anything that touches startup tools/boot-timing.sh restart 5 the medians against the previous run's before a release tools/boot-timing.sh reboot 3 , tools/qml-profile.sh boot to first frame; what QML creates before it after any UI, animation, poll or watcher change, and in every phase pass tools/audio-impact.sh (§9) idle 0 frames/s; playing ≈ the playhead and meter rates; 0 RT-thread faults from ravving's own code; 0 xruns

tools/static-analysis.sh # both; or `tidy` / `clazy` alone It configures a separate build folder with a compile database ( BUILD , default /tmp/ravving-analysis ; the normal build/ is never touched), generates moc and the QML type registration, then runs clang-tidy with the repo's .clang-tidy and clazy (levels 0–2 without the Qt-idiom noise listed in the script) over src/ only, in parallel. Reports go to REPORTS (default ./analysis ): clang-tidy.log , clazy.log and summary.txt , one count per check. Arch packages: clang (clang-tidy, run-clang-tidy) and clazy . A newer clang-tidy brings new checks: decide for each whether it finds something or restates the house style, and turn the latter off in .clang-tidy with a line saying why.

tools/static-analysis.sh shell runs ShellCheck 0.10 at -S style over every shell script; the baseline is 0 . ShellCheck is on the device ( apt install shellcheck ); on a laptop without it the script sends the files there.

The modal dimmer stops items, not pointer handlers: Qt Quick still hands a press to every handler under it after the dialog's button or field took it, and a page's DragHandler then takes the drag over past its threshold. Disabling the page while a dialog is up is no way out (a disabled ComboBox closes its own list at once). So the modal layers (dialogs, the MENU drawer, a drop-down's list) register in Session.overlays by identity (a repeated open cannot leave the page blocked), and every handler on a page or the header binds enabled: !Session.inputBlocked . tools/check-handlers.py ( static-analysis.sh handlers , also in all ) fails on a new one that does not.

What is left is known and accepted; anything not in this list is new and worth reading. Check Count Why it stays bugprone-implicit-widening-of-multiplication-result 12 soundfont record offsets ( index * Size ) and the track lanes: int-sized files and lists bugprone-signed-bitwise 11 MIDI status / channel and LED colour byte masks on int ; values are 0..255 bugprone-incorrect-roundings 3 int(x + 0.5) on frame counts, which are never negative bugprone-multi-level-implicit-pointer-conversion 2 jack_free(ports) and QMetaObject's void * arguments: the C APIs' own types bugprone-inc-dec-in-conditions 1 m_editGroup > 0 && --m_editGroup == 0 : the decrement is meant to be guarded readability-redundant-nested-if 1 LiveFx: the two conditions read as two decisions clang-analyzer-cplusplus.NewDeleteLeaks 1 false: the QFutureWatcher is parented to the machine and deleteLater() s itself clazy range-loop-detach 24 loops over temporaries ( toList() , split() ) on load paths; a member list looped often would be worth fixing (DrumKit::rows() was) clazy writing-to-temporary 2 QSettings(...).setValue() : the temporary's destructor writes it clazy connect-non-signal 2 clazy cannot follow a for over signal pointers (Studio); its own message calls it a clazy bug clazy qproperty-without-notify 1 HardwareEvent::accepted: a per-event object, never bound

main() writes the phases of a start to the journal ( src/startuptimer.h ): ravving: startup main 0 ms process up (after startx, X and the binary loading) ravving: startup application 18 ms QGuiApplication ravving: startup libzynthbox 649 ms libzynthbox's singletons and engines ravving: startup studio 2922 ms machines, effects, the session (Studio) ravving: startup qml 3681 ms Main.qml created ravving: startup first-frame … the first frame on screen ravving: startup wired … audio and MIDI connected tools/boot-timing.sh restart 5 # service restarts: CSV + medians, ms from the service starting tools/boot-timing.sh reboot 3 # reboots (ravving the default UI): also kernel boot → first frame tools/boot-timing.sh last # the last start, without restarting anything Compare medians, never single runs: the first frame moves by up to 3 s between runs because kwin starts beside ravving ( start.sh ) and the window is not shown before kwin manages it. The start depends on the page the session restores, since only the page on screen is built first: DRUMS is the heaviest (all three drum machines' step grids), BASS a typical one. Compare runs on the same restored page ( "page" in the session.json: 0 drums … 4 sampler), and before blaming a change for a slower start, compare against an old build (a git worktree , deployed) on the same day, project and page: the device's state moves the times too.

Restart sparingly. Every restart stops and starts the HiFiBerry's PCM, and after a few dozen in a session the Pi's RP1 audio DMA driver can oops (the device reboots itself). Prefer 3–5 runs per measurement, and take boot-timing.sh last after a start that happens anyway.

Deploy with checksums. rsync -a keeps the laptop's modification times, so a file edited before the device last built another tree arrives older than that build's objects and ninja skips it. tools/device.sh deploy syncs with rsync -rlp --checksum ; after switching trees by hand, find src qml -exec touch {} + on the device before building. What keeps the start short: 1. Only the page on screen is built before the first frame (Main.qml's PageLoader ): the other four pages and the mixer are built one per 40 ms tick once the first frame is up. main.cpp restores the page before loading the QML, so the first page built is the right one. 2. KnobBadge builds its drawing on first show ( shown , not visible ): most badges stay hidden. 3. The LV2 ports are cached on disk (JalvPlugin::readPorts, ~/.cache/ravving/lv2-ports.json ) instead of lv2info running for each plugin built at start. Each entry carries its bundle's and binary's modification times; an installed or upgraded plugin does not match and is asked again. Delete the file to force a full re-read. 4. Imported soundfonts cost next to nothing : only each font's preset list ("pdta") is read, found by walking the RIFF chunk headers ( SoundFontFile::presetData , which steps over an unpadded odd-sized chunk too). The journal says what it cost: ravving: kits N ms, imported soundfonts: F fonts, S sources, M ms (also after a USB import, refreshImported ); that line is the check after adding a font whose writer is new.

tools/qml-profile.sh NAME # ./NAME.qtd and ./NAME-summary.txt tools/qml-profile-summary.py NAME.qtd --type Creating --top 40 tools/qml-profile-summary.py NAME.qtd --from 2 --to 4 A systemd drop-in sets RAVVING_QML_DEBUG=10002,block : main.cpp opens the QML debug server and waits for qmlprofiler before loading any QML; the script attaches on the device, waits for startup wired , flushes the trace, then removes the drop-in and restarts ravving. The summary lists self time per event type, per file and per event: look at Creating first (how many of what were built) and the call counts (1436 calls of one component is the finding, not its 0.1 ms each). Never probe the debug port by connecting to it: the server takes the first connection as its client.

RAVVING_STYLE=Basic QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1 RAVVING_NO_ZYNTHBOX=1 \ RAVVING_DATA_DIR=$PWD/data RAVVING_PROJECT_DIR=/tmp/tour/project RAVVING_SCREENSHOT_DIR=/tmp/tour/shots \ build/ravving 2>&1 | grep -v -i jack It visits every page and a few dialogs, saves PNGs and quits (main.cpp). Start from an empty project folder each time (the tour turns knobs, and the session keeps them), build the reference from the previous commit the same way, and compare with compare -metric AE ref.png new.png null: (ImageMagick). QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING matters: without a terminal Qt logs to the journal and the run looks silent. The Zynthbox style is not on the laptop, hence RAVVING_STYLE=Basic .

tools/device.sh default ravving # or on the device: /usr/share/ravving/default-app.sh ravving tools/device.sh default status tools/device.sh default zynthbox # back to stock; add --purge to uninstall ravving too default-app.sh masks zynthbox-qml in root's user units (a --user disable cannot undo its global enable in /etc/systemd/user , and updates re-enable it globally; the mask wins over both) and enables ravving. Going back unmasks and starts zynthbox-qml, disables and resets ravving, and drops the development environment ( RAVVING_GDB , RAVVING_QML_DIR ).

h: 6. The Store AppImage: the release check
t: tools/appimage-test.sh builds the AppImage on the device, installs it the way the Store does and walks every choice of the setup page and ravving's ZYNTHBOX button by touch, with an assertion on the device's state after each step. Run it after a version bump or any change to setup/ , tools/default-app.sh , data/ravving.service or packaging/ . About eight minutes; results in analysis/appimage-test-<date>/ . Details in packaging.md .

h: 7. Soundfonts and engines: when one is added
t: sh tools/soundfont-check.sh (on the device, from the laptop) takes every soundfont data/kits.json names (the drum kits, the machines' default engines, every FluidSynth sound source) and checks each: the file exists, its zones can sound (a font whose instrument zones declare a velocity range of 0–0 is mute at any velocity: SynStrings, LaString, MelloString and Organ.sf3 on the image are such, and are left out), the preset the entry asks for (bank:program) exists in the font, and a chord rendered through fluidsynth offline on that preset (a kick, snare and hat for a kit, low notes for a bass, three seconds for pads that swell slowly) actually comes out. PASS / FAIL per font, exit status = failures. Run it after editing the sources in kits.json, after an image update (the fonts live in /zynthian/zynthian-data/soundfonts ), and before a release. Behind it, tools/soundfont.py (presets · ranges · render · categorise) looks inside one font and proposes kits.json entries for new ones ( categorise --json ), and tools/mididump.py shows what an engine's JACK MIDI port really carries, for a source that stays silent in ravving but sounds offline ( testing.md ). A new engine type (a SoundEngine subclass) gets the same treatment: its sources into kits.json, the check run, and a pw-top look at its nodes' rate and quantum against the graph's (48000 / 256 on the device).

ravving's music player needs pipewire-pulse (Qt's audio output on Linux is PulseAudio), so the unit wants it. Its stream runs at its own adapted quantum and leaves the graph at 256 / 48000; the graph's rate is pinned ( clock.allowed-rates = [ 48000 ] ), so a 44.1 kHz file cannot switch it. After a PipeWire update, check with pw-top -b -n 2 : idle, with an MP3 playing, and with the MP3 plus the transport, the driver must stay at 256 / 48000 with its xrun count unchanged.

h: 8. The audio graph: routing, clocks and xruns
t: When an engine, insert or route is added or changed, and in every phase pass: tools/device.sh graph all -s 60 # rates, idle-but-linked nodes, threads, xruns over 60 s, the links Expected on a Zynthbox: the driver is the sound card's playback node at 48000 / 256; every ravving-* audio node at 48000 with a period of 256 (jalv) or 512 (FluidSynth's stream, by design); no node with links that is not running; 0 xruns in 60 s, idle and with the reference project playing (run it twice, once with device.sh cuia SWITCH_PLAY_RELEASED first). Any steady xrun rate means a stall somewhere: the first thing to check is systemctl --user show-environment for RAVVING_GDB=1 (gdb costs 20–40 a minute), then graph-check.py threads for a render thread without realtime priority or one above PipeWire's data loops. What each column means, the tools behind it and the numbers PipeWire's data loops. What each column means and the tools behind it are in routing.md .

h: 9. What the rest costs the sound
t: The sound comes first on this device: a feature, a poll, a watcher or an animation may not cost the audio anything it can hear. ravving's audio threads run at realtime priority, so other work cannot preempt them directly; what it can do is load the CPUs and the memory bus they share, stall a cycle with a page fault on a realtime thread, or hold a lock the audio side needs. Measure it, before and after: tools/audio-impact.sh # 30 s idle, then 30 s with the transport playing tools/audio-impact.sh 20 idle # only the idle window (no keys pressed: safe while someone plays) tools/device.sh animations # what keeps the window drawing, item by item audio-impact.sh prints, per state: the frames per second the window put on screen ( Ravving.framesSwapped , counted on the render thread), CPU in % of one core for the render thread, the GUI thread, ravving's realtime threads (policy FIFO / RR: the JACK clients, SyncTimer, MidiRouter…) and the rest, the page faults the realtime threads took, and the graph's xruns over the window ( graph-check.py xruns , summed over the nodes: one graph-wide dropout counts once per node). playing presses PLAY and STOP: never run it while someone plays; idle only reads. What healthy looks like (a Pi 5, a full project): idle playing frames/s 0 16 (the 16ths' playhead and the 10 Hz meters) render / GUI thread 0 % / 3 % about 13 % / 10–15 % realtime threads about 14 % about 20 % RT page faults / 20 s 0–2 (PipeWire's own data loops) some in libzynthbox's SyncTimerThread, none in ravving's code xruns 0 0

An idle screen draws nothing. Before shipping UI work, tools/audio-impact.sh 20 idle must read 0 frames/s; if not, device.sh animations names the item. No Animator (Opacity/Scale/Rotation/XAnimator…) inside a Behavior : use NumberAnimation . No Behavior on something the transport changes at every step or every meter reading: those values change instantly. Anything fed by the audio side (positions, levels) is published at the rate the eye needs (15 Hz for a moving line, 10 Hz for meters), never per audio block. An infinite animation ( loops: Animation.Infinite ) runs only while its state lasts (a take waiting, a latched pad) and only while its item is shown. A grid, a play position or a progress reads the step playing only while visible : the hidden pages stay built in their StackLayout and must not follow the playhead. A poll that forks or blocks runs only while what it feeds is on screen, unless it watches for something that has to be noticed at once (a USB stick); measure it with this tool.

Views fed a plain list (a QVariantList from the backend, a JS array) rebuild every delegate whenever the list is set again; on the Pi a row with a Zynthbox Button costs ~1.4 ms to make (five SVG frames). The long or often-updated lists go through KeyedListModel (src/, tests in tests/: cmake -DRAVVING_TESTS=ON build && ctest --test-dir build ): a new list is applied as the fewest row changes, matched by a key; the longest also set reuseItems . Its roles only grow (a reset would rebuild everything), and a test keeps it so. Use KeyedListModel for any list that is long or updated often; small fixed lists (the banks, the kinds) stay plain. AFTER=script tools/qml-profile.sh profiles an interaction instead of a start.

Every phase of a feature ends with this pass, run with ravving under gdb on the device ( systemctl --user set-environment RAVVING_GDB=1 , then a restart: start.sh prints a backtrace to the journal on a crash) while the suites run, and gdb off again for the timing rows: Check How clang-tidy / clazy tools/static-analysis.sh : back to the accepted findings (§1) start-up (gdb off) tools/boot-timing.sh restart 3 : the medians against the last pass QML profile tools/qml-profile.sh NAME : what the phase adds to Creating screenshot tour §4: every shot, no QML errors feature suites (gdb on) the page's suite and any the change touches ( testing.md ) what it costs the sound tools/audio-impact.sh (§9) valgrind memcheck on the offscreen tour (laptop) with --leak-check=no ; read only the frames that name ravving (Qt's aeshash128 and forkfd reports are known false positives); it takes about 25 min
